@magpie-community/agent-aider.readme:
# @magpie-community/agent-aider

[Aider](https://aider.chat) as a magpie agent. magpie has no setup of its own
for Aider; with this plugin it is on magpie's Agents page like the agents
magpie ships with.

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-aider
```

Then pick one of magpie's models in Aider's row. magpie writes into
`~/.aider.conf.yml`:

```yaml
model: openai/deepseek/deepseek-flash   # magpie's model, through litellm's openai/ prefix
openai-api-base: http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1
openai-api-key: magpie-aider            # Aider's own key, so Usage names it
show-model-warnings: false
```

Your comments and other settings stay. Picking Aider's own model again, or
switching it off, puts every key back as it was. Restart Aider after a change:
it reads its settings when it starts.

How agent plugins work: [usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents).

@magpie-community/agent-bub.readme:
# @magpie-community/agent-bub

(中文说明在下面。)

[Bub](https://bub.build) as a magpie agent. magpie has no setup of its own for
Bub; with this plugin it is on magpie's Agents page like the agents magpie
ships with.

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-bub
```

Then pick one of magpie's models in Bub's row. magpie writes into
`~/.bub/config.yml`:

```yaml
model: magpie:deepseek/deepseek-flash   # magpie's model, through the provider below
providers:
  magpie:
    type: openai
    api_base: http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1
    api_key: magpie-bub                 # Bub's own key, so Usage names it
```

Your comments, `fallback_models` and your own providers stay. Picking one of
Bub's own models again, `magpie bub default`, or switching it off puts every
key back as it was (a file that had no `providers:` is left with
`providers: {}`, which Bub reads). Restart `bub gateway` and open `bub chat`
sessions after a change: Bub reads its settings when it starts.

## The Bub it needs

Bub 0.5.1 or later: from 0.5.1 Bub takes named providers under `providers:`
([bubbuild/bub#343](https://github.com/bubbuild/bub/pull/343)). 0.5.0 and
older don't. To update:

```sh
uv tool install --reinstall bub    # installed with pip: pip install -U bub
```

An older Bub fails every turn on a `magpie:` model, before any request
goes out: `'magpie' is not a supported provider`. If you see that, update Bub,
or pick one of Bub's own models in the row (or run `magpie bub default`) to put
the file back.

How agent plugins work: [usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents).

---

## 中文

[Bub](https://bub.build) 作为 magpie 的 Agent。magpie 没有内置 Bub 的接入；装上这个插件后，Bub 就和 magpie 自带的 Agent 一样出现在 Agent 页。

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-bub
```

然后在 Bub 那一行选一个 magpie 的模型。magpie 会改写 `~/.bub/config.yml`：

```yaml
model: magpie:deepseek/deepseek-flash   # magpie 的模型，经下面这个 provider 访问
providers:
  magpie:
    type: openai
    api_base: http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1
    api_key: magpie-bub                 # Bub 自己的 key，用量里能认出它
```

你的注释、`fallback_models` 和自己的 provider 都会保留。再选回 Bub 自己的模型、运行 `magpie bub default`，或者关掉开关，每个键都恢复原样（原来没有 `providers:` 的文件会留下 `providers: {}`，Bub 能正常读）。改完要重启 `bub gateway`，并重新打开 `bub chat` 会话：Bub 在启动时才读设置。

## 需要的 Bub 版本

需要 Bub 0.5.1 或更新版本：从 0.5.1 起，Bub 支持在 `providers:` 下写具名 provider
（[bubbuild/bub#343](https://github.com/bubbuild/bub/pull/343)）。0.5.0 及更早的版本没有。更新：

```sh
uv tool install --reinstall bub    # 用 pip 装的：pip install -U bub
```

更早的 Bub 遇到 `magpie:` 模型，每一轮都会在请求发出之前失败：
`'magpie' is not a supported provider`。看到这个报错，就更新 Bub；或者在这一行选回 Bub 自己的模型（或运行 `magpie bub default`），把文件恢复。

Agent 插件怎么工作：[usemagpie.ai/docs/zh/plugins#agents](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/zh/plugins#agents)。

@magpie-community/agent-cowork.readme:
# magpie-agent-cowork

把 **团结 Cowork**（Tuanjie Cowork，本地 agent 是 `codely.exe`）接成 magpie 的一个 agent：
在 magpie 里给 Cowork 选一个模型，Cowork 就用 magpie 网关上那个模型说话——用的是你已经在
magpie 里登进去的那些订阅的额度，Cowork 自己不用另登录。

```
magpie cowork workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash     # 换 Cowork 的聊天模型
magpie cowork                                    # 看它现在用哪个
magpie cowork default                            # 把 Cowork 交还给它自己原来的选择
```

装：

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-cowork
```

`seed.mjs` 需要 Node 18 以上（用了顶层 await 和全局 `fetch`），magpie 自己带的那套不影响它。
机器上没有 `node` 就用 Cowork 自带的那个——它不在 PATH 上，位置跟着安装目录变：

```sh
"<安装目录>\cli\bin\win32-x64\node.exe" seed.mjs
```

## 适用前提

这个包读的是 Windows 上 Cowork 桌面应用的存储布局，键名出自安装包 2026-10-14 那一版。成立的前提是三条：

- **Cowork 的主目录在默认位置 `~/.codely`。** 设置里的 Codely Home Location 能把它搬走，搬成功时 Cowork 把
  新位置写进系统环境变量 `CODELY_CLI_HOME`。`seed.mjs` 跟着这个变量走，但只认里面有 `ide-settings.json` 的
  目录——终端 `codely` 自己那份 `~/.codely-cli` 没有它，指过去就是把清单写进没人读的库。两个候选都不像
  Cowork 的家时它停住报错、不替你新建；硬指用 `--store <主目录>/settings.json`。**插件那一半没有这个余地**：
  `cowork.agent.js` 的 `config` 写死在 `~/.codely/ide-settings.json`，只跟着用户主目录，agent 契约也不允许
  一个插件写第二个文件。所以搬过主目录的机器上 `magpie cowork <模型>` 写的文件 Cowork 读不到、切换静默失效——
  这类机器用 `seed.mjs` 搬清单、在 Cowork 里点模型；要还能用命令行切，就把主目录搬回默认位置。
- **管的是桌面应用，不是终端里的 `codely`。** 后者用 `~/.codely-cli`，模型记在 `model-config.json`，文件和
  形状都和桌面应用不一样，本插件不动它。
- **Windows。** macOS、Linux 上这三份文件放在哪没有依据；其它版本的 Cowork 也没有依据说键名仍是
  `defaultChatModelTitle` / `customModels` / `customModelProviders`。

## 先跑一次 seed

Cowork 的模型清单在 `~/.codely/settings.json`，它当前用哪个模型记在 `~/.codely/ide-settings.json`
的 `defaultChatModelTitle`。这个值是清单里那条模型的**名字**（`displayName`），不是请求体里的 `model`
字符串——所以 `seed.mjs` 把它写进清单的每条模型都用模型 id 当名字，否则 `magpie cowork <模型>` 写进去
的字符串 Cowork 认不出来，会静默退回原来的模型。

改名只发生在**它记录的条目**上：某条是它写的、你后来在 Cowork 里换了名字，下次 seed 会把名字改回模型
id（不改的话 `magpie cowork <模型 id>` 选不中它）；如果这条正好是 Cowork 当前选中的，`defaultChatModelTitle`
在同一次运行里跟着改成新的名字，不留悬空选择，输出也会说明。记录里没有的条目——你自己加的、自己起名的，
包括你在 `magpie` 那家 provider 下自己加的——一个字都不改。`ide-settings.json` 读不出来时它整次停住
（退出码 2），不会把「读不到」当成「没选」再去改名或删条目。

插件本身只维护 `ide-settings.json` 这一个文件——magpie 的 agent 插件按契约只能碰一个配置文件，
而清单那个文件里是数组，magpie 的写入器碰到 `customModels: []` 会写成 `{"0": {…}}`，Cowork 读不了。
所以模型清单由包里的 `seed.mjs` 从 magpie 的 `/v1/models` 一次性搬过去。装完之后它在 magpie 的插件目录
`~/.config/magpie/plugins/node_modules/@magpie-community/agent-cowork/`（设了 `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` 的把
`~/.config` 换成它）：

```sh
cd ~/.config/magpie/plugins/node_modules/@magpie-community/agent-cowork
node seed.mjs            # 第一次写之前把原文件留成 settings.json.pre-magpie，只留这一次
node seed.mjs --check    # 只报漂移，不写；有漂移（含被扣下的条目）时退出码 1
node seed.mjs --prune    # 允许删掉记录里已不在 magpie 目录中的条目（见下）
node seed.mjs --remove   # 摘掉记录里属于本包的条目；那家 provider 只在没人用时才删
```

**跑之前先退出 Cowork。** `ide-settings.json` 有两个写者：magpie 切模型时写它，Cowork 自己在运行中也会
写回它。Cowork 开着的时候切模型，它下一次保存就可能
把刚写进去的名字盖回去。所以：退了 Cowork 再 seed，切完模型再启动；已经在开着的情况下切过，就
`cat` 一下确认那个名字还在。

**它只动自己写过的东西**：哪些条目是它写的记在同目录的 `settings.json.magpie-seeded`（一个 entry id
数组）。改名、删除与 `--remove` 要同时满足两条——那条在这份记录里，**且**它挂在包自己建的那家
`magpie` provider 下。你自己的 provider 就算地址也填的 magpie、就算被旧版记录误认领过，也不会被删、
也不会被改名；你手动加在 `magpie` 那家下面、名字自己起的条目同样不在记录里，`--prune` 和 `--remove`
都不碰。记录丢了但 `settings.json.pre-magpie` 还在（= 我们确实写过这个库）时，`seed.mjs` 会按形状
认领一次：只认挂在 `magpie` 下、名字正好等于模型 id、而且 magpie 现在仍提供的条目；`--remove` 在
记录缺失时不猜，会要求先跑一次 `seed.mjs` 把记录补回来。**卸掉插件不会自动跑 `--remove`**——magpie
没有这个钩子，卸完要自己跑一次，否则那家 provider 和它下面的 magpie 条目会留在 Cowork 里。

**这类模型不认模型 id**：某个模型在 Cowork 里的条目名字不是模型 id（通常是它只存在于你自己的 provider 下、
名字还是你起的）。`magpie cowork <模型 id>` 写进去的是 id，而 Cowork 按它显示的名字找条目，找不到就退回
原来的模型（不报错）。seed 会列出它们：能当参数的给出 `magpie cowork "<名字>"`；名字里带 `/`（会被
magpie 当成 `供应商/模型` 去校验）、以 `-` 开头（会被当成 flag）、或者正好叫 `default`（会把 agent
复位）的，则让你回 Cowork 里点。能传的名字直接用 Cowork 显示的名字切，例如
`magpie cowork "GLM-5.3-Flash · zcode"`——magpie 对不在目录里的写法是原样写入的；只有形如
`供应商/模型` 的写法会被当成目录引用去校验（供应商是 magpie 的 provider、模型又不在目录里就报错），
其余字符串照写。带 `/` 的名字就在 Cowork 里选，或者在 `magpie` 那家 provider 下加一条以模型 id
命名的条目。

**目录里没有的条目不删**：magpie 的目录会因为某个账号正在恢复、magpie 刚启动而临时变短，照着删就会
删掉你正在用的那条。所以记录里有、当前目录里没有的条目一律先留着，只报
`N recorded entries aren't in the catalog right now; pass --prune to drop them`；`--check` 仍把它算作
漂移（退出码 1）。要删请显式加 `--prune`；就算加了，`defaultChatModelTitle` 指的那一条也永远不删。
`--remove` 如果正好摘掉 Cowork 当前选中的模型，会明确说出来，你在 Cowork 里重选一个即可。

搬完之后，magpie 自己那批条目用 `magpie cowork <模型 id>` 就能直接切，不用回 Cowork 的模型列表里点；
你自己 provider 下的条目用它们显示的名字切（见上）。

**这一步得你手动跑，而且目录变了要再跑**：agent 插件按契约只能写 Cowork 的一个配置文件，模型清单在
另一个文件里、还是数组，插件搬不了。magpie 的目录本身会变，所以 `--check` 留了个能用退出码判断的
口子——目录新增、有被扣下的条目、provider 地址变了都算漂移，退 1；文件读不出来退 2 且不写。挂个
定时任务就行。**没搬进去的模型不会报错**：用 `magpie cowork <模型 id>` 切到它，title 写进去了，但
Cowork 找不到同名条目，会退回自己原来的模型。这是这条路线最难看的一点，目前只能靠「切之前先
`--check`」避开。

改动生效的时机：Cowork 启动时读这个文件，所以重启 Cowork 或新开一个会话才用新模型。

## 装完怎么确认

```sh
magpie ls          # 应当有一行 Tuanjie Cowork，右边是它当前的模型和配置路径
magpie cowork <某个模型>
cat ~/.codely/ide-settings.json     # defaultChatModelTitle 应当已经变成那个模型（搬过主目录的看那个目录）
```

然后在 Cowork 里发一句话，回话应当来自那个模型。若它回的是别的模型，说明那个名字在 Cowork 的清单里
没有对应条目——再跑一次 `node seed.mjs`。

图标取自 Cowork 安装包里的 `app/resource/dist/branding/logo_dark.png`，缩到 112px 后内联成 data URI
（和 `@magpie-community/agent-kimi-desktop` 一样的做法，好处是不依赖仓库先建好），同图另存一份 `icon.png` 随包发。

@magpie-community/agent-kimi-desktop.readme:
# Kimi desktop Work agent

Use the ordinary **Kimi desktop application's local Work agent** with a model selected in Magpie. This is not Kimi Code CLI, a Kimi subscription provider, or a way to spend Kimi Work subscription credits in other agents.

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-kimi-desktop
```

Open and sign in to Kimi desktop. On Magpie's Agents page select **Kimi**, pick a model, and connect. The adapter waits for the local Work runtime to be ready and idle, then applies the connection without restarting either application. Use Kimi's **Work** page. Chat and cloud Claw are outside its scope. The standard Kimi model menu continues to use the model selected in Magpie; this package does not modify Kimi's application resources or install a custom model-menu patch.

Disconnect Kimi in Magpie to restore its original model service address. Existing conversations, login credentials, unrelated settings, and native model entries are preserved.

## Library: instructions, MCP and skills

Version 0.1.1 registers ordinary **Kimi** as a target on all three Library pages. This is separate from **Kimi Code**. Existing assignments stay unchanged; select Kimi on the resources you want to share.

- Shared instructions are written by Magpie to `~/.config/magpie-kimi/AGENTS.md`. While connected, the adapter reads this file before each inference and inserts one separate system message, preserving Kimi's original prompts, tool calls and history. Changes also apply to existing Work conversations on their next request. Removing the assignment removes Magpie's managed block; other text in that file remains the user's own instructions. An unreadable/invalid file fails with `instructions_unavailable` rather than silently omitting active rules. These instructions do not apply when disconnected, to Chat, or to cloud Claw.
- MCP points through `~/.config/magpie-kimi/library-native/mcp.json` to ordinary Kimi's `daimon-share/daimon/runtime/kimi-code/home/mcp.json`. The format is Kimi's `mcpServers` object. Existing server entries are retained by Magpie's normal Library merge; new conversations load changed MCP settings. Existing conversations can use Kimi's own reconnect controls.
- Skills point through `~/.config/magpie-kimi/library-skills` to ordinary Kimi's `daimon-share/daimon/skills`. This exposes existing native skills as well as Library assignments. Bundled/user skills are not deleted or replaced by the adapter. Conflicts use Magpie's normal keep-own/use-library choice. Start a new Work conversation to load changed skills.

The two directory links are Windows junctions or macOS directory symlinks; no administrator authorization or app modification is needed. An existing different object at either link path is left intact and reports `library_path_conflict`. Resource files remain in Kimi when the model bridge disconnects. The adapter does not enable all resources or change another agent's assignments.

The Work provider carries an agent's messages unchanged; a provider is not a separate instruction target. Give shared instructions to the agent making the request. Using Kimi Work in Codex therefore uses Codex's instructions, while ordinary Kimi uses the Kimi assignment above.

## How it works

The import-free `kimi-desktop.agent.js` registers the agent using Magpie's agent interface. The Bun entry `index.mjs` is also necessary: Kimi's actual configuration belongs to its running local runtime, so changing a file alone does not reliably apply a model. It runs a loopback adapter and uses Kimi's authenticated local control API to reload the selected model.

Inference goes to Magpie using Magpie's agent credential. Kimi's web search/fetch tools continue through Kimi's original `agent-gw.kimi.com` service with Kimi's own credential. Kimi login credentials are never forwarded to Magpie or a third-party model provider. Requests to unknown paths and requests without Kimi authentication are rejected; no system proxy, certificate or firewall settings are changed.

Rate-limit and temporary-service responses retain the upstream status, body and `Retry-After` header, including both delay-seconds and HTTP-date values. Other upstream headers are not copied wholesale.

The adapter does not reload a busy Work runtime. If Kimi independently changes its service configuration while connected, adaptation pauses instead of repeatedly overwriting it; disconnect and reconnect in Magpie to retry.

## Local files and compatibility

- `~/.config/magpie-kimi/connection.json`: Magpie's selected model and connection.
- `~/.config/magpie-kimi/status.json`: fixed status categories, without credentials.
- `~/.config/magpie-kimi/adapter-state.json`: original service address and connection ownership; no Kimi login credentials.
- `~/.config/magpie-kimi/before-menu-models.json`: one snapshot of the original model list/current choice, removed after a clean disconnect. No full configuration or credential backup is written.
- Kimi configuration: `daimon/config.json` in Kimi's `daimon-share` folder: where `kimi-desktop/daimon-storage.json` points (`shareDir`; Kimi 3.2.21 on Windows writes it when installed on another drive, e.g. `D:\KimiData\daimon-share`, and on any system when its storage is moved), else `kimi-desktop/daimon-share`, under the platform's application-support directory (`%APPDATA%`, `~/Library/Application Support`, `~/.config`).

Verified with Windows 11, Kimi 3.2.17.10 and official Magpie 0.1.1275, including an actual Work request through Magpie. The [macOS record](COMPATIBILITY.md) verifies real control methods, connect/disconnect restoration and a real streamed bridge request on macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Kimi 3.2.17 build 3.2.17.4 and official Magpie 0.1.1276. That request was initiated by an HTTP test client; a macOS desktop UI-submitted Work turn remains unverified. The supported runtime has provider `daimon-kimi-code` with original service `https://agent-gw.kimi.com/coding/v1`; other layouts stop with `unsupported_kimi_config`.

The private control API is undocumented. Before connecting, the adapter probes `models.current`; a refused/missing method stops connection without changing the service address. A failed `conversations.setModel` rolls back that address. Failures of `conversations.getKimiModelList` or `conversations.updateKimiModelList` report `catalog_sync_failed` and preserve the existing catalog rather than inventing a different protocol. In that case the selected-model bridge may remain connected; disconnect it to return to Kimi's service. No vendor app files are patched, and no automatic upgrade to an unknown protocol is attempted.

No Kimi binaries, personal configuration, prompts, account identifiers or credentials are included. There are no runtime dependencies. Tests use isolated temporary directories and synthetic credentials.

```sh
bun test packages/kimi-desktop/kimi-desktop.test.mjs
```

The model catalog is fetched from Magpie's `/v1/models` with this agent's credential and registered User-Agent. Magpie owns its visibility, picked/hidden models, disables and ordering. The adapter never opens Magpie's `providers.json` or `settings.json`. It rechecks the gateway catalog before every inference; removed selections are refused even during a running turn, and an unavailable catalog returns a fixed error instead of falling back to an unrestricted list. This package includes no Electron injection hook or model-menu patch. The icon is Kimi's desktop application icon.

Thinking models with a complete, recognized effort list that omits `none` also declare `always_thinking` in both the runtime and menu model configurations. Kimi can then resolve an old Off selection using that model's thinking defaults. A list containing `none` remains switchable; missing or unrecognized effort metadata does not imply mandatory thinking. The adapter does not rewrite the inference request's thinking fields. See the [3.2.18 compatibility check](COMPATIBILITY.md#kimi-3218-isolated-compatibility-check).

The 3.2.18 check includes real model requests, four background-control turns, and three signed-in UI submissions in a separate official desktop profile. Both real models completed native read-tool loops, and the final UI turn recalled the earlier history without a tool call. The signed-in UI retained native model labels; this does not verify custom Magpie aliases in the online menu. The full record distinguishes these checks from the synthetic core tests.

## Shutdown and manual recovery

The shared plugin host owns process shutdown. This plugin installs no SIGTERM/SIGINT handler and never calls `process.exit`. On the host's normal exit event it synchronously restores the original address if the current address is still its own; restart Kimi to reload its runtime. An explicit disconnect while both apps are running additionally restores model selection/list through the control API.

Owner records are fully written to a temporary file and published with an exclusive hard link, so interruption during the write cannot publish an empty/partial `adapter-owner.json`. An existing live owner is left alone. A malformed legacy owner record reports `adapter_lock_invalid` in `status.json` and the plugin log; a file access/publication failure reports `adapter_lock_unavailable`. The plugin does not guess who owns a malformed record or automatically remove it. To recover from `adapter_lock_invalid`, close all Magpie instances first, remove only `~/.config/magpie-kimi/adapter-owner.json`, then reopen Magpie. Leave `connection.json`, the other state files and Kimi's credentials intact.

A forced kill, power loss or a broken private API can leave Kimi pointing at an inactive loopback bridge. To recover without starting Magpie:

1. Close Kimi normally. In `~/.config/magpie-kimi/connection.json`, set `enabled` to `false` so the adapter does not reconnect when Magpie next starts.
2. Open Kimi's `config.json` at the application-support path above. Only if `model.providers["daimon-kimi-code"].baseUrl` equals `bridgeURL` in `adapter-state.json`, change that one field to the same state's `originalBase` (normally `https://agent-gw.kimi.com/coding/v1`). Leave `credentials` and all unrelated fields untouched; do not replace the whole document from an old backup.
3. If `model.current` starts with `magpie-local-`, set it to `current` from `before-menu-models.json` if that alias still exists in `model.models`; otherwise choose an existing native `daimon-kimi-code` alias, such as `k3-agent` or `k2d8-preview`. Remove only `model.models` keys beginning with `magpie-local-` if present. Reopen Kimi; it refreshes its native model catalog.

Older experimental packages created full `backups/before-connect-*.json` copies, which can contain Kimi credentials. This package creates no such files and does not silently delete existing user backups. After recovery, users can remove those older copies locally. Do not upload them in an issue or PR.

manifest.name: @magpie-community/agent-opencodereview
manifest.description: Open Code Review (Alibaba's ocr CLI) as a magpie agent: pick one of magpie's models for ocr review / ocr scan on the Agents page

@magpie-community/agent-opencodereview.readme:
# @magpie-community/agent-opencodereview

[Open Code Review](https://github.com/alibaba/open-code-review) (`ocr`),
Alibaba's AI code review CLI, as a magpie agent. With this plugin it is on
magpie's Agents page like the agents magpie ships with: pick one of magpie's
models for it and `ocr review` / `ocr scan` run on that model.

This is an unofficial integration: Open Code Review is Alibaba's, and this
plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Alibaba. The icon is Open Code
Review's own logo, which magpie references by URL.

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-opencodereview
```

Then pick one of magpie's models in Open Code Review's row. magpie writes into
`~/.opencodereview/config.json`:

```json
{
  "model": "zai/glm-5.3",
  "provider": "magpie",
  "custom_providers": {
    "magpie": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3425",
      "protocol": "anthropic",
      "api_key": "magpie-…"
    }
  }
}
```

## What it owns

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `provider` | `magpie` |
| `model` | the magpie model picked |
| `custom_providers.magpie.url` | the gateway's base address, with no `/v1` |
| `custom_providers.magpie.protocol` | `anthropic` |
| `custom_providers.magpie.api_key` | the key magpie keeps for ocr |

`provider` and `model` are ocr's own selection; `protocol: "anthropic"` makes
ocr speak the Anthropic Messages API. The url has no `/v1` suffix because ocr
appends `/v1/messages` itself. These are the keys `ocr config set` writes for a
custom provider (`provider`, `custom_providers.<name>.url`, `.protocol`,
`.api_key`).

Everything else stays yours: other `custom_providers` entries, `providers`,
`llm`, `max_tokens`, `effort`, `language`, `mcp_servers`, `rule.json` and
sessions. magpie edits keys in place and stashes what it replaces.

A `custom_providers.magpie` you had before is replaced whole while connected —
the three fields above, and nothing else — and restored on disconnect. Its
values come back; its formatting and comments do not. Keep a manual service you
need beside magpie under another provider name.

The plugin gives ocr no Library instructions, MCP servers or skills: ocr keeps
its own `rule.json` and `mcp_servers`.

## Disconnecting

ocr reads the file on every run, so the next `ocr review` / `ocr scan` uses the
new model: no restart. Disconnecting — picking ocr's own model again or
switching it off — puts back the `provider`, `model` and
`custom_providers.magpie` values magpie replaced, and removes the keys it
added. A machine with no config file at all is left an empty
`custom_providers` object; ocr ignores it.

Disconnect before disabling or uninstalling the plugin: removing a plugin does
not run the agent's disconnect, and ocr would keep pointing at a gateway that
is no longer configured for it. If that happens, set `provider` back to the
provider you used before, or remove `provider` and `custom_providers.magpie`
by hand.

## Other ways ocr finds an endpoint

ocr resolves its endpoint from the config file first, then `OCR_LLM_URL`,
`OCR_LLM_TOKEN` and `OCR_LLM_MODEL`, then `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`,
`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, then shell rc files. A complete
config file wins, so the saved `magpie` provider takes precedence over those
variables (checked with ocr v1.13.2). `ocr llm test` sends a test conversation
to the configured model and is the quickest way to verify the setup.

## Configuration path

ocr keeps its config at `~/.opencodereview/config.json`, its home taken from
the OS. It has no flag or environment variable that moves it (v1.13.2), so a
different `HOME` (or `USERPROFILE` on Windows) is the only way it moves; the
descriptor uses the same `~` magpie expands.

## Requirements and verified versions

magpie installed and signed in; `ocr` installed with
`npm install -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review`.

Tried on macOS 26.6.2 arm64 with magpie 0.1.1326 and ocr 1.13.2, including
`ocr llm test`'s tool round trip and disconnect restoring a pre-existing
config. The descriptor has no platform-specific code; the same path and keys
apply on macOS, Linux and Windows, though only macOS was tried.

## Development

```sh
bun test packages/opencodereview
magpie plugin add ./packages/opencodereview   # try it on your own magpie
```

The module is one file with no imports, run by magpie's engine. The
repository's `scripts/check.mjs` skips agent packages; this package's test
checks the descriptor and what `connect` returns.

How agent plugins work: [usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents).

manifest.name: @magpie-community/agent-pig
manifest.description: PiG as a connect-only Magpie agent: inject endpoints and model catalog without changing startup settings

@magpie-community/agent-pig.readme:
# agent-pig

`@magpie-community/agent-pig` adds [PiG (Pi in Go)](https://github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG) to Magpie as a **connect-only agent**. It supplies Magpie's endpoint and model catalog in `~/.pig/agent/models.json`. You choose the model in PiG. The plugin never writes `settings.json`.

The Agents row identifies PiG with the project's pixel-pig icon from its official site. The image is not bundled: Magpie references it by URL and keeps its own cache. This is an unofficial integration; PiG is a project by Michael Kinsy and is not affiliated with, or endorsing, Magpie.

## Installation

With a Magpie release that supports connect-only Agent plugins:

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-pig
```

1. Open Magpie's Agents page and turn on **PiG**. Its row is a provider switch, with no model picker. CLI equivalent: `magpie pig provider magpie`.
2. Start PiG, run `/model`, and select a model under the **Magpie** provider. Reopen `/model` after Magpie's catalog changes; restart PiG if your installed version does not reload it there.
3. Before disconnecting, choose a model from another provider in PiG. Turn off **PiG** in Magpie, or run `magpie pig default`.

Saving a startup default is a separate PiG action: use PiG's own model picker to save it. The plugin does not set or restore defaults, thinking preferences, or scoped models. An existing `enabledModels` scope can restrict selection; change that scope yourself in PiG if necessary. Disconnecting cannot repair a saved default or resumed session that still names a Magpie model.

Disconnect the PiG agent before disabling or uninstalling the plugin; do not rely on removing a plugin to run the agent's disconnect flow.

## What it owns

Magpie manages **one complete object**, `providers.magpie`, inside `models.json`:

| Field inside the managed object | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | `Magpie` |
| `baseUrl` | The gateway's supplied `/v1` address |
| `apiKey` | The key supplied by Magpie for PiG; normally `magpie-pig` on loopback |
| `api` | `openai-completions` |
| `models` | The catalog Magpie exposes to PiG |

Magpie stashes the previous object and restores it on **agent disconnect**. If no `magpie` provider existed, the entire provider is removed. An empty top-level `providers` map or file can remain, but a provider object with no settings of its own must not.

Other provider IDs, unrelated top-level keys, and document comments outside the managed object stay in place, including changes made while connected. A pre-existing provider with the same `magpie` ID is temporarily replaced and restored semantically on disconnect; its internal formatting/comments are not a byte-for-byte backup. While connected the entire `magpie` object, including personal overrides there, is managed and refreshed by Magpie. Keep concurrently used manual services under a different provider ID.

The plugin does not change `auth.json` or PiG's credential precedence. A stored credential for the reserved `magpie` ID can take precedence over the injected key; use a distinct ID for an independently configured manual service.

The plugin preserves catalog IDs (including slashes), names, image input capability, positive context/output limits, and supported Pi thinking levels. A known output limit is capped at the known context window, matching Magpie's Pi adapter. Unknown limits are omitted so PiG applies its own defaults. The public Agent hook does not provide a model's native protocol, prices, or a separate reasoning flag: all models use Magpie's documented Chat Completions endpoint, and reasoning is advertised when `efforts` is nonempty. Magpie handles upstream protocol translation. This is not the full native-protocol behavior of Magpie's built-in Pi adapter.

It reads no credentials, installs no PiG extension, runs no daemon, and provides no Library integration. Requests use Magpie's supplied key, so usage can be attributed to `pig` without claiming Pi's User-Agent.

## Configuration paths

The shipped descriptor targets **the default PiG directory only**, `~/.pig/agent`. It does not automatically follow `PIG_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, `PIG_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, or `PIG_USE_PI_DIRS=1`. The current public Agent contract offers one static config path (with `~`/`$VAR` expansion), not a conditional directory resolver. Do not turn this descriptor on when PiG uses a different directory.

For a custom directory, make a local copy of `pig.agent.js`, change `agent.config` and `agent.dir` to the actual selected PiG paths, and install that file with `magpie plugin add /absolute/path/to/custom-pig.agent.js`. Install only one descriptor with id `pig`. Do not change PiG's directory layout for this plugin. In Pi sharing mode, editing a shared `models.json` also affects Pi; that is an explicit custom setup, not the default plugin behavior.

## Platform support

The same `pig.agent.js` was tested on native Linux and Windows with Magpie 0.1.1294 and PiG 0.5.1+1.3.0.1402973a using an external real-binary harness (not shipped in this package): 8 end-to-end tests and 3 lifecycle tests per platform. They cover fresh connect/disconnect/reconnect with a real PiG parse afterwards, a pre-existing manually configured API-key service used before, during and after injection, and restoration of a prior same-name provider. On Windows the default path resolves to `%USERPROFILE%\.pig\agent\models.json`, including when the test workspace and home paths contain spaces.

Magpie owns native home expansion, path separators, command detection, file edits and restoration. The plugin has no platform branches or platform-specific dependencies. macOS and WSL have not been tested on real machines.

## Development

The runtime module is a single file, without imports, runtime dependencies or install hooks. `package.json` declares `magpie.agent` and no `main`, following the [community Agent convention](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins#agents) and [public contract](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents).

From `packages/pig` in a checkout of the community plugins repository, run the included unit tests with Bun:

```sh
bun test pig.test.mjs
```

The repository's `scripts/check.mjs` skips Agent packages; `pig.test.mjs` checks this plugin's descriptor and `connect()` output. The published npm package excludes tests and research artifacts.

## 中文

这是仅注入模型目录的 PiG 适配插件。通过 `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-pig` 安装后，在 Magpie 的 Agent 页打开 **PiG**，再到 PiG 中运行 `/model` 选择 Magpie 模型。

插件只通过 Magpie 托管 `~/.pig/agent/models.json` 中完整的 `providers.magpie` 对象，不修改 `settings.json` 或 `auth.json`，也不替用户设置启动默认模型、思考等级或模型范围。断开时，原先有同名 provider 就恢复原对象，原先没有就移除整个 provider，避免空 provider 导致 PiG 解析失败。

其他 provider 和顶层设置不在托管范围内。若原先就手动配置了名为 `magpie` 的 provider，它在接入期间会被替换，断开后恢复；接入期间对该区块的手写改动会被同步覆盖。需要同时使用的手动服务应使用其他 provider ID。插件不会修改既有凭证优先级。

默认仅支持 `~/.pig/agent`。使用环境变量改过目录或开启 Pi 共享目录的用户，需要先明确实际路径，再安装改过路径的本地描述文件。不要直接启用默认描述文件。

断开前在 PiG 中换回其他 provider 的模型；先断开 PiG，再禁用或卸载插件。PiG 自行保存的默认模型和会话引用不由本插件恢复。

## License

MIT.

manifest.name: @magpie-community/gateway-aelios
manifest.description: Aelios long-term memory for every agent behind magpie: recall before each turn, optional recording after it

@magpie-community/gateway-aelios.readme:
# Aelios plugin for Magpie

[Aelios](https://github.com/wusaki0723/Aelios) is a layered long-term memory
you deploy yourself on Cloudflare: it recalls what fits each turn, keeps what
was said, and tidies it overnight. This plugin brings it to **every agent
behind Magpie**: before each turn, the memory Aelios recalls for it is added
after the user's message; after the reply, and only if you turn `record` on,
the turn is handed to Aelios to remember. Your agents keep whatever models and
subscriptions they use in Magpie; nothing has to point at an Aelios gateway.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent as Any agent
    participant Magpie
    participant Plugin as Aelios hook
    participant Aelios as Your Aelios Worker
    participant Model
    Agent->>Magpie: Request
    Magpie->>Plugin: onRequest
    alt the user said something
        Plugin->>Aelios: POST /v1/hook/recall (slimmed request)
        Aelios-->>Plugin: memory patch
        Plugin-->>Magpie: patch added after the last user message
    else a tool step or helper request
        Plugin-->>Magpie: request unchanged
    end
    Magpie->>Model: One inference request
    Model-->>Agent: Live reply through Magpie
    Magpie--)Plugin: onResponse (completed reply)
    opt record is on
        Plugin--)Aelios: POST /v1/hook/record (slimmed request + reply)
    end
```

The package declares `magpie.hooks: "./aelios.hooks.mjs"`, Magpie's
asynchronous Bun hook entry. It is not gateway middleware and has no OpenCode
provider. It needs **Magpie 0.1.1273 or newer** and Bun; from **Magpie
0.1.2210** the key Magpie writes into your own agents on this computer
(`magpie-key`) counts as yours too.

## Before you start

1. **Deploy Aelios yourself.** Follow the
   [Aelios README](https://github.com/wusaki0723/Aelios#readme). The plugin
   needs an Aelios that has the hook endpoints, `POST /v1/hook/recall` and
   `POST /v1/hook/record`, including the recall endpoint's explicit `record`
   permission added in [commit a57269c](https://github.com/sakisakisa-design/Aelios/commit/a57269c)
   ([Aelios PR #102](https://github.com/wusaki0723/Aelios/pull/102)).
   Deploy that commit or a later version containing it; omitting `record`
   saves no user message or remember-now memory. An older Aelios without these endpoints
   answers 404; the plugin then leaves requests alone and shows *unavailable*.
2. **Add your agents' model names to the assistant's main models** in Aelios
   `/admin` (or use `*`). The plugin checks the authorized main-model list
   locally; unmatched requests are not sent and show *unbound*. To keep GPT
   and Claude in separate spaces, set each assistant's
   main models separately in `/admin`.

## Install and configure

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/gateway-aelios
```

Then open **Plugins › Aelios** in Magpie. On first use, enter the server URL
and API key and click **Connect and test**. The plugin saves through Magpie,
confirms the saved settings, then opens its local service page with automatic
testing enabled. If saving cannot be confirmed, your edits stay in the form
and the page does not navigate.

Once configured, the page shows the saved URL, a **Change connection** control,
and the recall/record switches (*Recall memory* on, *Record conversations* off
by default). Configured settings do not mean the connection has been verified.
**View matching list / retest** opens the local service page, which tests the
saved connection and shows the server-authorized assistants and their main
model matching rules through read-only `GET /v1/hook/identities`. This list needs
an Aelios version containing that endpoint. If the list is unavailable (including
on older Workers), hooks pause without sending conversations and show *unavailable*. The service
page has a button back to settings. Testing
sends empty messages; it creates no dialogue and records nothing.

**Assistant assignment** defaults to **Automatic**. The plugin uses Aelios's
authorized matching list to select the first assistant whose main-model pattern
matches locally. Unmatched turns are not sent. If the list is unavailable,
recall and recording pause with status *unavailable*. Existing `identity` or
`routes` are shown as **Custom** and retain their routing priority. The collapsed **Advanced
settings** section contains the default/fallback identity, ordered identity
routes, agent filter, API key environment variable and remote-request switch.
You can continue editing those settings there; ordinary saves preserve them.
No hand-written JSON is needed.

The same options can still be set from the command line:

```sh
magpie plugin options aelios '{"serverUrl":"https://<your-aelios>.workers.dev","gatewayTimeoutMs":5000}'
```

Give it your Aelios API key in Magpie's environment as `AELIOS_API_KEY`, or as
`apiKey` in the options. The key is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` to
your `serverUrl` only, never through a redirect.

Set `gatewayTimeoutMs` as above: without it Magpie gives a hook 1 second, and
the plugin then gives Aelios a little under that. The page fills in 5000 when
the setting is absent.

To use a separate assistant space (recommended while you try it out), create
one in Aelios `/admin` and set `"identity": "<its slug>"`.

## Route models to separate identities

Create `gpt-husband` and `claude-husband` identities in Aelios `/admin`, then
configure the plugin:

```json
{
  "serverUrl": "https://<your-aelios>.workers.dev",
  "gatewayTimeoutMs": 5000,
  "record": true,
  "routes": [
    { "models": ["gpt-*"], "identity": "gpt-husband" },
    { "models": ["claude-*"], "identity": "claude-husband" }
  ]
}
```

Routes are checked in order; **the first match wins**, ahead of the top-level
`identity`. Model patterns match the whole name, case insensitively, with `*`
matching any characters. Both the full Magpie model name and the suffix after
its last `/` are tried, so `openai/gpt-5` matches `gpt-*`. Other punctuation
is literal. The request body's model is used if Magpie provides no model.

A route can also select exact Magpie agent ids:
`{"agents":["codex"],"models":["gpt-*"],"identity":"gpt-husband"}`.
When both selectors are present, **both must match**. Agent ids are case
sensitive; `*` has no special meaning in an agent id. The top-level `agents`
option still limits which requests the plugin handles.

With nonempty `routes`, an unmatched request uses only an explicitly configured
top-level `identity`. Without that fallback, both recall and recording are
skipped, preventing accidental use of the server's default identity. Omit
`routes` or use `[]`: the top-level `identity` is used when set; otherwise the
plugin selects the first authorized assistant whose main models match locally.
Unmatched requests are not sent. Custom identities and route targets must also
be authorized and match the request model in the server's main-model list.

**Separate identities need separate Aelios memory namespaces.** Give these
identities different `namespace` values and avoid shared `readNamespaces` if
they must not recall each other's memories. Routing chooses an identity; it
does not create identities or isolate spaces that Aelios is configured to
share. Each identity's Aelios `models` whitelist must also allow its actual
model names (or `*`), including provider-prefixed names when sent; the plugin's
route patterns do not configure that server whitelist.

Routing also applies to tool continuations and `recall: false`. The original
identity, model, agent, session and slimmed request are saved before recall,
so recording uses the same exchange metadata even if the response context or
route options change. Recording still requires the current `record` permission
and the current origin and top-level agent restrictions. Recall backoff is
separate for each resolved identity.

## What is sent

Recall sends a **slimmed copy** of the request: roles and message text, tool
names, and the session id. Historical tool calls keep only their type and
name; their arguments and input are never sent. It does **not** send system
prompts or instructions, what tools returned (tool results are sent empty),
images, files or audio (replaced by `[image]`, `[file]`, `[audio]`), or thinking.
Only turns where the user said something are recalled; tool steps are not
sent for recall.

**`record` is off by default.** Recall sends `record: false`, so Aelios
searches existing memories without saving the user's words or creating new
memories. This requires an Aelios hook endpoint that honors the `record`
permission; upgrade older hook endpoints before using the plugin.
If you want Aelios to remember your conversations, turn it on:

```sh
magpie plugin options aelios '{"serverUrl":"https://<your-aelios>.workers.dev","gatewayTimeoutMs":5000,"record":true}'
```

With `record` on, after each reply the slimmed request and a **slimmed reply**
are sent to Aelios: what you said, what the assistant said, the arguments of
its tool calls, and the completion status. Thinking/redacted-thinking blocks,
Responses reasoning items and summaries, Chat reasoning fields, signatures,
encrypted content and other provider metadata are omitted before the secret
check and before export. Tool results are not sent. For coding agents
(Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, …) Aelios replaces code blocks with `[code]`.
If the current user text looks like it contains a credential (an API key, a
token, a private key, `password=`…), the entire turn skips both recall and
recording, even with `record: false`, so read-only recall cannot upload it.
Historical text that matches the same check is replaced with the fixed marker
`[credential omitted]` in the slimmed copy, preserving the message structure.
A later ordinary user turn can recall and record normally; a credential in
history does not disable memory for the rest of the conversation. The original
request sent to the model is untouched by this sanitization. A credential in
the completed reply's retained text or tool arguments still skips recording.
The reply delivered to the client remains unchanged. Each
record is sent once and never retried.

## Things to know

- **Don't double up.** If an agent already uses an Aelios gateway as its
  upstream, it gets memory there; exclude it here with `agents` or every turn
  is recorded twice.
- **Tools.** The plugin adds no tools. For `recall` / `remember` tools, add
  Aelios's `/mcp` endpoint in Magpie's **Library › MCP**.
- **Who it serves.** By default only direct requests on this computer
  (`local`) and Magpie's own key for your agents (`magpie-key`) are handled.
  Other gateway keys (possibly a friend's), remote requests and requests of
  unknown origin are left alone unless you set `allowRemote`.
- **Fails open.** If Aelios is slow, down, refuses the key or is too old, the
  request goes to the model as it came. After a timeout, connection failure,
  5xx, 404 or 401, recall pauses for `recallBackoffMs` before trying again. A
  client that cancels does not count.
- Gemini requests are not supported yet and pass through untouched, as do
  Responses requests that continue server-side state
  (`previous_response_id`, `conversation`).

## Options

| Option | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `serverUrl` | none | Your Aelios Worker. Without it nothing is sent. HTTPS only (plain HTTP allowed for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`); no user, password, query or fragment in the URL. |
| `apiKey` | none | Aelios API key. Without it, the variable named by `apiKeyEnv` is used. Without either, nothing is sent. |
| `apiKeyEnv` | `AELIOS_API_KEY` | Environment variable that holds the key. |
| `identity` | none | Aelios assistant space slug; fallback for unmatched routes. Without routes and when empty, the plugin selects the first authorized assistant whose main models match locally; unmatched requests are not sent. Custom identities must also be authorized and match the model. |
| `routes` | none | Up to 64 identity routes in priority order. Each needs a valid ASCII identity slug (max 64 characters; Aelios reserved slugs excluded) and nonempty `models` and/or `agents` arrays. Model patterns are nonblank strings up to 200 characters; agents are nonblank exact ids. Nonempty routes without a match or explicit `identity` skip recall and recording. |
| `agents` | all | Only these Magpie agent ids, e.g. `["claude","claude-desktop"]`. Empty means all. Other ids include `qwen` and `kimi`; legacy `claude-code` remains supported as an exact id. |
| `recall` | `true` | Recall before each turn. |
| `record` | `false` | Record each turn after the reply. |
| `allowRemote` | `false` | Also handle other gateway keys, remote and unknown origins (recall and record). |
| `gatewayTimeoutMs` | Magpie's 1000 | How long Magpie waits for the hook, 100–10000 ms. Set it to about 5000. |
| `requestTimeoutMs` | `4000` | Deadline of one recall request to Aelios, 50–9000 ms, kept just under `gatewayTimeoutMs`. Records have their own 10 s. |
| `recallBackoffMs` | `30000` | After a failure, how long recall is paused (0 turns the pause off). |
| `port` | `3481` | Loopback port of the settings page's connection test. Change it only if that port is taken. |

Invalid options make the hook stand aside (*invalid*); the key never appears
in a report or error.

## Status codes

Magpie's Plugins page shows one code per request, never any content:
`ready` (memory added, with its size), `empty` (nothing relevant),
`unbound` (not a main model, or the key has no such assistant),
`unauthorized` (Aelios refused the key, or there is none), `unavailable`
(timeout, 5xx, missing hook endpoints or authorized matching list, or paused after a failure),
`invalid` (bad options or an answer the plugin can't read) and `skipped`
(origin or agent not handled, a tool step, Gemini, server-side Responses
state).

## Development

```sh
bun test ./*.test.mjs      # Aelios faked with fetch; no network, no key
```

The settings page is `page/settings.html` with `page/settings.js`, `page/form.js`,
`page/style.css` and `page/i18n.js`; the connection test is `service.mjs` and
`probe.mjs`. `page.test.mjs` drives the browser script in a small `node:vm`
harness, so the form's validation, the option merge and the save/test paths are
covered without a browser. Magpie frames a page with `allow-scripts` but not
`allow-forms`, so saving is a button click and never a form submit.

@magpie-community/gateway-nowledge-mem.readme:
# Nowledge Mem plugin for Magpie

[Nowledge Mem](https://mem.nowledge.co) is a local-first memory layer for
people and AI tools. Magpie is the gateway in front of every harness, so this
plugin puts Mem *in the gateway*: every request Magpie routes gets the Memory
that fits it, and completed conversations can flow back into Mem. No harness
needs its own Nowledge Mem plugin, skill or MCP configuration for that.

Agent-callable Memory tools are a separate surface and stay where Magpie
already provides them: the plugin installs Mem's own MCP server and a short
skill into Magpie's [Library](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mcp-hub), given to no
agent; choose the agents there. This keeps one tool surface, Mem's own.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Harness as Any harness
    participant Magpie
    participant Plugin as Nowledge Mem hook
    participant Mem as Nowledge Mem
    participant Model
    Harness->>Magpie: Request
    Magpie->>Plugin: onRequest with host-derived origin and agent
    opt Recall origin allowed
        Plugin->>Mem: POST /memories/search (latest user turn)
        Plugin->>Mem: GET /context/bundle (first turn of a session)
        alt bundle is empty, missing or failing
            Plugin->>Mem: GET /agent/working-memory
        end
        Mem-->>Plugin: Memory and session context
        Plugin-->>Magpie: Context-enriched request
    end
    Magpie->>Model: One inference request
    Model-->>Harness: Live response through Magpie
    Magpie--)Plugin: Completed response notification
    opt Capture enabled and origin allowed
        Plugin-)Mem: POST /threads/import (completed conversation)
        Mem->>Mem: Background distillation into Memory
    end
```

Requires **Magpie 0.1.1273 or newer** and Bun. From **Magpie 0.1.2210** the
sharing key Magpie writes into your own agents on this computer arrives as
`magpie-key`, and recall and saving include it automatically. On an older
Magpie every harness key is `gateway-key`, which is not included: upgrade
Magpie for keyed harnesses, or only unkeyed local requests get Mem. The package declares
`magpie.hooks: "./nowledge-mem.hooks.mjs"`, Magpie's asynchronous Bun hook
entry; it is not gateway middleware and has no OpenCode provider. Use **Magpie
0.1.1531 or newer** for options saved from the plugin page to reach the hook on
the next request; earlier hook-capable versions need a restart after saving.

## Connecting

Mem runs on this machine at `http://127.0.0.1:14242` by default; an Access
Anywhere, Nowledge Cloud or self-hosted endpoint works the same way over HTTPS.
Configure it in the plugin page, or with the CLI:

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/gateway-nowledge-mem
magpie plugin options @magpie-community/gateway-nowledge-mem '{"serverUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:14242"}'
```

The hook reads its endpoint and key from the option first, then from the
environment Magpie starts with, as Mem's own clients do:

| Option | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `serverUrl` | `NMEM_API_URL` | Mem base URL; the local default when neither is set |
| `apiKey` | `NMEM_API_KEY` | Sent as `Authorization: Bearer …`; no key for an unauthenticated local Mem |

A key saved in the page is kept in Magpie's local plugin configuration, not the
system keychain, and takes precedence over the environment. Enter it directly;
the form also accepts an existing `Bearer …` value. The page's **Configure
connection** form also sets the Space, Agent and the recall, Context Bundle,
capture switches; Magpie's plugin **Options** editor remains available for
advanced settings. Saving conversations remains a separate opt-in.

`serverUrl` must be HTTPS, or HTTP only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and
`[::1]`. Credentials, a query or a fragment in the URL are refused. Set
`allowInsecureHttp` only for a trusted LAN server.

## One gateway, several harnesses

Magpie knows which agent sent a request. Unless `hostAgentId` is set, the hook
uses `magpie:<agent>` as the host identity and sends it with the Context Bundle
request. Mem derives an AI identity per harness from it, so a Claude Code
session, a Codex session and a chat UI behind the same Magpie keep distinct
provenance without sharing one anonymous identity. The same value and the raw
agent name are recorded on imported Threads.

Each harness also gets its own recall cache: the same prompt from two harnesses
does not reuse the other's block. An explicit `hostAgentId` overrides the
derived value for all of them.

## Options

- `serverUrl`: Mem base URL. If unset, `NMEM_API_URL`, then
  `http://127.0.0.1:14242`.
- `apiKey`: Bearer API key. If unset, the variable named in `apiKeyEnv`.
- `apiKeyEnv`: environment fallback name, default `NMEM_API_KEY`; only an `NMEM_*` name is accepted. The environment key goes to the endpoint the hook resolves: page `serverUrl` first, then `NMEM_API_URL`. Keep the two paired; a page URL with an unrelated `NMEM_*` key sends that key there.
- `spaceId`: Mem Space for recall, context and imports. Empty means the default
  Space.
- `agentId`: optional portable Mem agent profile. It selects a profile for the
  Context Bundle and is recorded on imported Threads; it is not authentication.
- `hostAgentId`: optional fixed host identity. Empty derives
  `magpie:<agent>`, or `magpie` when Magpie reports no agent.
- `recall`: default **true**. Whether a turn gets Mem context. Recall only
  happens when a Mem endpoint is reachable; failures leave the request as it
  came.
- `contextBundle`: default **true**. On a session's first turn, ask Mem for its
  Context Bundle (owner profile, rules and Working Memory) and add its rendered
  markdown. When the bundle is empty, missing or failing, the hook falls back
  to today's Working Memory. A bundle outage never disables Memory recall.
- `maxMemories`: how many search hits to consider, default 5, range 1–20.
- `maxBytes`: recall budget for the block's content, default 6000, range
  512–32768. On the first turn the session context takes up to 45% of it, and
  the rest stays available for Memory.
- `requestTimeoutMs`: deadline for each search, bundle or Working Memory
  request, default 900, range 50–5000. It fits inside Magpie's default 1000 ms
  hook deadline. The host's hook deadline can end it
  earlier. Thread imports keep a separate ten-second deadline because a
  completed reply's notification is not bound to the live request.
- `gatewayTimeoutMs` (Magpie's own option, not this package's): the whole hook
  chain's deadline, default 1000 ms, range 100–10000. A local Mem fits the
  default; over the network, set it to 5000–10000 so the first turn's Context
  Bundle and search can finish.
- `recallBackoffMs`: after a connection failure, timeout or unavailable
  response, skip Mem for this endpoint/credential/Space for this long, default
  30000, range 100–300000. A failing optional bundle backs off only itself; the
  Working Memory fallback keeps being tried. Client cancellation does not
  trigger backoff.
- `capture`: default **false**. Import completed conversations as Mem Threads.
  Set `"capture": true` explicitly to opt in.
- `captureTools`: default **true**. Include client tool results as `tool`
  messages. Turn it off to import only what the user and the assistant wrote.
- `allowInsecureHttp`: default **false**. Permits plain HTTP to a server that
  is not a loopback address. Prefer HTTPS.
- `port`: the loopback port of the page's connection test, default 3479. Change
  it only when another program holds that port; the page reads the same value.

## What recall adds

The latest user turn (Magpie's `ctx.query`, not client environment notices,
bounded to 2000 characters) is sent to `POST /memories/search`. On a session's
first turn the Context Bundle comes with it, or Working Memory when the bundle
is unavailable. The answer is wrapped in a `<nowledge-mem-reference>` block and
appended to that turn:

```
## Context bundle
<Mem's rendered Context Bundle>

## Recalled memories
### <title>
<Memory text>
nowledgemem://memory/<id> · relevance 0.94
```

When the bundle falls back, the heading is `## Working Memory` instead. Each
Memory keeps its title and up to 1000 characters of text, and the whole section
stays within `maxBytes`.

The block says the text is untrusted historical evidence, not instructions.
Recalled text cannot close the block it is in. A turn keeps the block it was
given for the rest of the conversation, so the request prefix stays stable for
the provider's prompt cache; a tool loop or a retry reuses it without asking
Mem again. A turn that already carries this plugin's block, or Mem context
injected by another connector (such as the DeepSeek Harness bundle), is left
alone rather than given a second copy.

Nothing recalled means the request is returned unchanged. Timeouts, an
unreachable server, an unknown Space and an unauthorized key all keep inference
available; the Plugins page shows a fixed outcome code and byte count, never
recalled text or a token.

## What capture imports

With capture on, a completed reply is turned into the conversation the client
sent plus the assistant's reply, and imported with `POST /threads/import`:

- `thread_id`: `magpie-<session>-<digest>`, or a digest of the opening turn for
  a client with no session. It stays the same across turns, so Mem appends
  missing messages instead of creating a Thread per turn.
- `title`: the first line of the message Magpie read as the user's query.
  A Thread keeps the title it opened with, so a client's environment notice
  before the real prompt does not become it.
- `source`: `magpie`; `tool_version`: `magpie-nowledge-mem/<version>`.
- `metadata`: `source_app`, protocol, the harness (`agent`), the host identity,
  an optional agent id, and SHA-256 digests of the session and working
  directory — not their raw values.

Messages are text only. Assistant tool-call steps with no text are not
messages; client tool results are included while `captureTools` is on. The
recalled `<nowledge-mem-reference>` blocks are stripped before import, so
Memory is never learned as a new conversation. A conversation with a
credential-like assignment, URL password, bearer token or common key format in
its text or tool arguments is not captured at all — a best-effort safeguard,
not a guarantee. Each Thread import is one bounded request; conversations over
512 KiB are skipped, and an identical replay of the last successful import is
not sent twice. A failed import fails open and is not retried blindly.

`capture` is the only switch that exports conversation content. Recall works
without it.

## Tools: Mem's own MCP server

The package adds no Library entry, no Magpie tool hook, no skill and no
system-prompt edit. To give agents Mem's tools, add Mem's official MCP server
once in Library › MCP, with `<serverUrl>/mcp` (or `NMEM_API_URL` when Server
URL is empty) and the connection's key. With the
[MCP hub](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mcp-hub) on, each agent still gets a single
`magpie` entry, and the tools are Mem's own, not a second surface.

The page shows the effective Server URL in its summary; it does not add the
Library entry itself. If you want a custom system prompt for Memory, Magpie's
[system-prompt](../system-prompt) middleware does that on its own.

## Validation

```sh
bun test packages/nowledge-mem                  # offline tests
NMEM_E2E=1 bun test packages/nowledge-mem       # also the live checks, when .env is set
bun packages/nowledge-mem/e2e.run.mjs           # the live checks alone
```

The hook tests fake Mem with `fetch`: no server, no sign-in and no network. The
end-to-end checks talk to a real Mem and are skipped unless `NMEM_E2E=1`; they
read the repository's `.env` (the file wins over an ambient `NMEM_API_URL` or
`NMEM_API_KEY`):

```sh
set -a; . ./.env; set +a
bun packages/nowledge-mem/e2e.run.mjs
```

The checks create a few Memories and Threads per run and delete them afterwards.
They verify that `.env` reaches Mem, that recall returns a seeded Memory and
cites its id, that the Context Bundle arrives on a session's first turn, that
capture creates one Thread and appends only the new messages idempotently, that
the Thread records the harness and host identity, and that a wrong key and an
unknown Space report fixed codes. `e2e.test.mjs` runs them in a process of its
own: the offline tests replace `globalThis.fetch` to keep Cursor's token local
(`packages/cursor/nonet.mjs`), and a live check must not share that process.

## Page

The page uses only Magpie's released `magpie.options` and theme bridge. It
declares no reads and saving stores configuration without probing the
connection or writing Memory. It shows the Server, API key, Space, Agent, the
recall, Context Bundle and capture switches. Its **What is sent** section says
the scope: direct local requests and `magpie-key` from this computer; other
gateway keys and remote requests are never included. It follows Magpie's language (English, Simplified and
Traditional Chinese, Japanese, German) and theme, and preserves options it does
not show.

**Test connection** is a real check, not a saved flag. Magpie's page sandbox
has `connect-src 'none'`, so the page cannot call Mem itself; the package's
small host part serves a loopback page on `127.0.0.1:<port>` and the frame
navigates to it. The **Test connection** button tests the saved options, so
save changes first. The language travels in the test URL's query; the test
page asks for a click, then the service reads the saved plugin options itself
and makes one public health request and one authenticated Working Memory
request. No URL, key, Space or return address travels through the page. It
writes nothing and shows reachability, the key and the Space with a fixed code
and milliseconds. **Back to settings** uses the frame's history to return to
the plugin page; the test saves nothing and changes no form values.

The helper binds `127.0.0.1`, answers only when `Host` is `127.0.0.1:<port>` or
`localhost:<port>`, and needs the page's per-process token. Its JSON endpoint
accepts `Origin: null` from the sandboxed page and nothing else, and returns no
`access-control-allow-origin: *`; `POST` and the page's `fetch` are therefore
closed to other sites. The test page takes no return address; its Back button
only walks the frame's history. Because the `Host` must be loopback, the test
works in the desktop app, not through a remote `magpie web` proxy.

The test needs the plugin host, which the gateway hook already starts; a
page-only install of an older Magpie version shows the test page failing to
connect rather than a wrong result.

@magpie-community/gateway-powercontext.readme:
# PowerContext gateway plugin

Recall sends the latest user turn to the PowerContext Server configured explicitly
in plugin Options, even when capture is off, and adds returned Memory/Profile
context to the model request. Optional capture exports full user and assistant
turns, including client tool calls and results, to that same Server. Capture is
off by default. No configured URL means no service requests. Recall and capture
allow only host-classified local requests by default; other callers require
separate `recallRemote` and `captureRemote` opt-ins.

Requires **Magpie 0.1.1273 or newer** and Bun. The package declares
`magpie.hooks: "./powercontext.hooks.mjs"`, the released asynchronous Bun hook
entry. `magpie.gateway` is a synchronous middleware alias and must not be used
for this plugin. See the [host contract](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1273/docs/subsystems/gateway-request-hooks.md).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Magpie
    participant Plugin as PowerContext hook
    participant PC as Standalone PowerContext
    participant Model
    Client->>Magpie: Request
    Magpie->>Plugin: onRequest with host-derived origin
    opt Server configured and recall origin allowed
        Plugin->>PC: Resolve Scope, latest user turn, latest Handoff
        PC-->>Plugin: Untrusted reference text
        Plugin-->>Magpie: Context-enriched request
    end
    Magpie->>Model: One inference request
    Model-->>Client: Live response through Magpie
    Magpie--)Plugin: Completed response notification
    opt Server configured, capture enabled and origin allowed
        Plugin--)PC: Complete conversation Source
        PC->>PC: Background Memory extraction
    end
    Note over PC: Future sessions can recall generated Memory
```

## Installation and connection

Deploy PowerContext independently using the
[official quickstart](https://powercontext.oceanbase.io/en/docs/get-started/quickstart/).
This plugin does not install Python, download executables, start services, or
manage their lifecycle. Configure Generation, Embedding and the Memory schedule
in the Server when automatic extraction and semantic search are needed.
Gateway clients need no separate PowerContext MCP or skill.

Install with Magpie 0.1.1273 or newer:

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/gateway-powercontext
magpie plugin options @magpie-community/gateway-powercontext '{"serverUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:8000"}'
```

Alternatively, find **PowerContext** in Magpie's Plugins discovery tab.
Use **Magpie 0.1.1531 or newer** for configuration saved from the plugin page
to take effect on the next request. Earlier hook-capable versions require
restarting Magpie after saving page options.

In the plugin page's Connection settings, enter the existing Server address,
optional Scope ID and service key. Leave Scope ID empty to use the session/workspace
binding or the Server's default Scope. Enter the token directly; the form adds `Bearer`
automatically and also accepts an existing `Bearer <token>` value. Leave it empty
when the Server does not require authentication. The key is stored in Magpie's
local plugin configuration, not the system keychain. Do not put credentials in
the URL. The page also configures optional conversation capture. The
native plugin Options editor remains available for advanced settings.

Existing `authorizationEnv` configurations remain supported: when no direct
`authorization` value is saved, the hook reads `Bearer <server token>` from
the named variable in Magpie's startup environment. Clearing the form's key
removes the direct value and restores this fallback.

Installing the plugin does not deploy its external service.

## Behavior and options

- `serverUrl`: standalone Server base URL, **no default**. Set it explicitly
  in Options; without it,
  neither recall nor capture sends anything.
- `authorization`: authorization header, such as `Bearer <server token>`.
  The connection form sets this from the service key and takes precedence over
  the environment variable.
- `authorizationEnv`: optional fallback variable (default `POWERCONTEXT_AUTHORIZATION`).
- `scopeId`: explicit Scope. If absent, resolve an existing Magpie session or
  workspace binding. A missing binding fails open; the plugin does not create
  scopes or grant a model permission to change them.
- `recallRemote`: default **false**. Recall and sticky context replay allow only
  host-classified `local` requests. Remote, named/shared Gateway Key and missing
  or unknown origins make no service requests by default. Enable this option
  only if these callers may send their prompts to the configured Server and
  receive its Scope's Memory/Profile. It does not enable capture. Recall caches
  are isolated by origin and protocol, including when remote recall is allowed.
- `maxBytes`: recall budget, default 8000 bytes.
- `gatewayTimeoutMs`: Magpie's bounded async hook deadline, default 5000 ms.
- `requestTimeoutMs`: deadline for each Scope, context and Handoff request,
  including response body reads; default 1000 ms, range 50–5000 ms. The host's
  cancellation/deadline can end it earlier. A recall normally resolves Scope
  first, then prepares context and a first-turn Handoff in parallel, so its
  service wait can span two such deadlines, bounded by the host deadline.
- `recallBackoffMs`: after a service connection failure, timeout or unavailable
  response, skip service lookup and cache replay for this Server/credential/Scope
  configuration; default 30000 ms, range 100–300000 ms. The next request after
  that interval can try again; continued failure starts another interval.
  Client cancellation does not trigger backoff. A missing/pending Handoff
  (404/503) is normal and does not trigger backoff. Source writes retain their
  separate ten-second deadline and are not retried.
  An optional Handoff connection failure or timeout backs off only Handoff
  lookup for that service/credential/resolved Scope, so healthy Memory recall
  continues. It never disables context preparation or sticky context replay.
- `capture`: enable completed-conversation capture, default **false**. Recall
  works independently. Set `"capture": true` explicitly in Options to opt in.
- `captureRemote`: default **false**. With capture enabled, only host-classified
  `local` requests are captured. Remote, named/shared Gateway Key (even on
  loopback), and missing/unknown origins are skipped. Set `"captureRemote": true`
  only if you intend to capture these other callers too and have their consent.
  This option alone does not enable capture or recall. With capture explicitly
  enabled, it may send Scope-resolution requests and conversation Sources even
  when remote recall is disabled. Forwarded/proxied requests are
  nonlocal even when Magpie trusts the proxy for authentication.
- `idleCaptureMs`: default ten minutes; range 1000–86400000 ms. A later user
  turn confirming a retained answer can trigger capture earlier.
- `allowInsecureHttp`: explicit opt-in for non-loopback HTTP; prefer HTTPS.

`POWERCONTEXT_SERVER_URL` and `POWERCONTEXT_SCOPE_ID` are not read; stale
settings from another integration cannot enable this plugin or override its
Scope. The authorization environment variable remains supported for credentials.
Scope resolution sends the session ID as a binding key and a SHA-256 digest of
the normalized workspace path. Source metadata uses SHA-256 digests for both
session ID and workspace path; it does not contain their raw values. Conversation
content is otherwise complete and can itself contain paths or identifiers.

Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages and Gemini requests retain their
protocol. Context is escaped and enclosed as untrusted reference text in the
latest user message, preserving prior context blocks for prompt caching. Latest
committed Handoff hints accompany recall when available. Credentials are not
included in model input. Sticky recall has an 8 MiB encoded-byte budget for
all conversations combined, in addition to 256 conversations and 128 turns per
conversation. It counts full escaped reference blocks, Scope IDs and turn keys;
oldest-used whole conversations are evicted first. Evicted turns can be recalled
again, so prompt-prefix retention is best-effort under memory pressure. This is
a cache payload limit, not a bound on the Bun process's total heap.
Timeout, invalid context, unauthorized access and a service outage keep
inference available. With capture off, tool-only continuations and turns that
already contain a reference block do not perform a Scope lookup.

Before staging or saving conversation history, the plugin checks message text
and tool arguments/results for credential-like assignments, JSON fields,
prefixed environment variables (including `PGPASSWORD` and `MYSQL_PWD`) and
common token formats, including URLs with `user:password@` credentials, Stripe
secret/restricted live keys (`sk_live_…`, `rk_live_…`) and Google API keys
(`AIza` followed by 35 key characters). A match skips the whole capture, rather
than redacting parts. This is a best-effort safeguard,
not a guarantee that arbitrary secrets can be identified; capture remains an
explicit opt-in for content permitted on the configured Server. Arbitrary prose
secrets and CLI password flags are not exhaustively detected.

Capture stores the complete conversation available to the request: user and
assistant messages, plus client-owned tool calls and results when supplied by
the client. **Files read by the Agent and command output returned by its tools
are included in those tool results and can be exported to the configured
Server.** Enable capture only for conversations whose content may be stored
there. It excludes injected reference blocks and private authorization.
Responses `previous_response_id` history is recovered only for capture when
observed by this host; missing history does not modify model input or pretend to
be a complete transcript. Failed, truncated and incomplete replies are skipped.

The gateway completion notification and plugin's idle capture timer are
best-effort. Process shutdown can lose pending capture; this is not durable or
exactly-once delivery. Source identifiers/digests provide stable content
identity, but do not establish an exactly-once guarantee. Each Source fragment
is attempted once. An uncertain or failed write is not automatically retried;
remaining fragments stop after a failure, and delivery may be lost or partial.

PowerContext's configured background inference turns Sources into Memory. It
needs its own generation model and credentials; the plugin does not reuse the
client's model authorization. Configure generation through the independent
Server's documented setup.

## Memory tools

This plugin neither declares nor executes memory tools. If an Agent needs
explicit search or remember tools, configure PowerContext's existing MCP server
through the client's Library MCP integration. The client owns tool execution and
subsequent model calls. Automatic recall/capture requires no MCP or skill.

## Validation

Run `bun test packages/powercontext` from the repository root. Tests use fake
HTTP responses and do not install or start PowerContext. Independent real-service
acceptance is maintained outside this repository, with results posted in the PR.
The supported host entry is the released `magpie.hooks` contract in Magpie
0.1.1273 and newer; the package is not a synchronous gateway middleware.

## Configuration page

The PowerContext page uses only the released `magpie.options.get/set` and theme
bridge. Choose **Configure connection** on this page to open a themed configuration
dialog. Magpie's plugin-list **Options** action remains the host's JSON editor;
the released API does not let a plugin replace that action. The dialog stays
inside the plugin page's sandbox. It preserves advanced options when saving changes. Capture is off by
default and requires explicit consent; remote recall and capture remain separate
opt-ins. The form stores configuration, not a verified connection status.

The page and dialogs inherit Magpie's light, dark and system theme through the
official bridge, including surface, text, border and button colors. The official
reverse PowerContext logo is used in dark mode. No separate theme setting or
system preference listener is added by the plugin.

The page follows Magpie's language through its official theme bridge: English,
Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese and German. Language changes
also update dialogs, validation and status messages without discarding unsaved
form edits. Unsupported languages fall back to English. Brand names, identifiers
and the official documentation URL stay unchanged.

The page contains the connection summary and form, the capture switch, an
explanation of what recall and capture send to the configured service, and the
official deployment guide. Scope ID is optional, matching the hook's service-side
binding/default resolution. Use the independently deployed PowerContext dashboard
for service records and Memory provenance, and Magpie's native plugin diagnostics
for hook outcomes. Saving options does not probe the Server or write Memory.

The package has no installer, CLI executable, background supervisor or standalone
management server. Tests in this repository cover the hook contract; external
service acceptance is run separately in the author's local environment.
