@magpie-community/hooks-mail-watch.readme:
# @magpie-community/hooks-mail-watch

Email alerts from [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai)'s gateway: a provider error the user should know about, a subscription quota close to or past its line — sent as plain mail through your own SMTP account, with your own words in it.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/hooks-mail-watch`. It has no page and no tab; it watches from beside the gateway.

## What it watches

Two signals, both from files magpie already keeps, read after an exchange finishes:

- **Provider errors** — a model call that ended in a 4xx/5xx (`usage.jsonl`'s own row for the call: status, the vendor's error type and words, provider, model, agent). A try the gateway handed on to another provider is skipped: the request was answered on a later try, so it was no failure of the request.
- **Quota windows** — a subscription account's allowance windows (`quotas.json`), each one a percentage used: exhausted at 100%, or over the low line you set.

## Options

Set them in magpie's plugin options for this package. All of it is yours: the mailbox, the words, and what to watch.

```jsonc
{
  "smtp": {
    "preset": "gmail",             // or host/port/secure by hand; a preset fills all three
    "host": "smtp.example.com",   // a hand-set host wins over the preset
    "port": 465,                  // default: 465 with TLS, 587 without
    "secure": true,               // default true: TLS from the first byte; false = plain relay
    "user": "me@example.com",     // omit on a plain relay that wants no sign-in
    "pass": "the app password",
    "from": "magpie@example.com"  // default: user
  },
  "to": ["me@example.com"],       // recipients; a comma string works too
  "watch": {
    "errors": true,               // provider call failures
    "quotaExhausted": true,       // a window at 100%
    "quotaLow": false,            // a window over quotaLowPct (but under 100)
    "quotaLowPct": 90,
    "providers": []               // empty: every provider; else only these
  },
  "cooldownMinutes": { "error": 10, "quota": 240 },  // one mail per key per window
  "maxMailsPerHour": 20,          // the whole hour's budget, on top of the per-key cooldowns
  "report": { "hours": 6 },       // opt-in only: a periodic usage digest; unset means none
  "template": {
    "subject": "[magpie] {{kind}} · {{provider}}{{window}}",
    "body": "What: {{kind}}\nProvider: {{provider}}{{account}}\n{{modelLine}}{{windowLine}}When: {{time}}\n\n{{detail}}"
  }
}
```

A note on `secure`: it defaults to `true` — TLS from the first byte, the usual submission port (465), which every major mailhost offers. A plain relay must say so explicitly (`"secure": false`): a localhost or LAN mailhost that wants no sign-in. A user/password on a plain wire is refused, because AUTH PLAIN is the password in base64 and a plaintext port would broadcast it. STARTTLS (an upgrade offered on a plain port, port 587's habit) is not supported: the runtime's TLS upgrade dies mid-session on some platforms, so rather than a send that breaks at random, use your mailhost's 465 port instead. TLS is verified against your system's certificate store; `smtp.insecure: true` turns that off for a mailhost with a self-signed certificate you know.

Presets name the mailhosts people actually forward mail through, so the options can just name one and add an address plus an app password: `qq` (smtp.qq.com), `163` (smtp.163.com), `126` (smtp.126.com), `gmail` (smtp.gmail.com), `zoho` (smtp.zoho.com), `yahoo` (smtp.mail.yahoo.com) — all TLS on 465. QQ/163/126 call the password an 授权码， Gmail an app password. A hand-set host or port wins over the preset; an unknown preset is ignored.

The cooldown keys are `provider` + error type (or status), and `provider` + account + window: one mail per key per window of minutes, so a vendor's bad hour is one mail, not four hundred. The cooldown marks the send before it is attempted — a broken SMTP server collects no backlog; the next matching event tries again after the window. On top of that, `maxMailsPerHour` (default 20) caps the whole hour: a bad hour across many keys still stops at N mails. Sent-marks older than the longest cooldown in force are pruned, so the state file doesn't grow without bound.

## Usage digest (opt-in)

Set `report.hours` and the plugin mails a periodic summary of the window since the last digest: calls (ok/failed), credits, tokens in/out, sessions (first 8 characters of the id), agents, providers, models — the shape of your own usage, in English by default (`template.reportSubject` / `template.reportBody` / `template.reportHtml` override the words). It is off unless you set it: filling in SMTP alone never starts a digest. An empty window sends nothing. The digest honours the same `watch.providers` list as the alerts — allow-listed providers only, not the whole gateway — and its timer is armed once per window, so it fires on schedule even while exchanges keep coming (the schedule only moves when you change the hours, or turn the report off).

Quota windows are read as magpie wrote them: the key is `provider/account` (the account lowercased), and a window whose reset time already passed is a stale last reading, not a window still full, so it is skipped rather than re-alerted every cooldown.

## Template variables

| Variable | Fills with |
| --- | --- |
| `{{kind}}` | `error`, `quota exhausted`, `quota low` |
| `{{provider}}`, `{{account}}` | where the call went / whose subscription |
| `{{model}}`, `{{agent}}` | the model asked, the agent that asked |
| `{{status}}`, `{{errType}}`, `{{endpoint}}` | HTTP status, the vendor's error type, the path called |
| `{{window}}`, `{{used}}`, `{{resetsAt}}` | the quota window's name, % used, when it resets |
| `{{time}}` | ISO time the alert was made |
| `{{modelLine}}`, `{{windowLine}}` | ready-made lines, empty when they'd say nothing |
| `{{detail}}` | the whole story: status + error, or window + % + reset |

A `{{name}}` the event doesn't carry becomes empty; braces that aren't a variable (`{{not a var}}`) are left alone. The subject is UTF-8 encoded for the header (RFC 2047), so any language works.

## How it runs

The package is one of magpie's asynchronous gateway hooks (`magpie.hooks`): magpie's Bun host calls `onResponse` once an exchange with a model is over — successfully or not. The hook waits a moment (1.5 s, so a burst of parallel calls is one scan), reads magpie's own log and quota files, and mails what is new through a queue that sends one mail at a time. It never awaits any of this — the bounded hook returns at once, and a broken send must not touch the request or magpie's log. Nothing is imported from npm; the SMTP client is hand-rolled over Bun's own socket API (implicit TLS or a plain relay, full reply-code validation).

State (how far the log was read, what was sent when) sits in `mail-watch-state.json` beside magpie's own config files, written atomically — one file shared with the digest's cursor, so neither walker disturbs the other's place. Its first run starts from the log as it is — a fresh install does not replay every past failure.

Where the files are is decided in one place: a plugin installed from the registry lives under magpie's config dir, so the plugin walks up from its own folder to the folder holding magpie's files — which also finds a portable install's data folder — and otherwise reads `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/magpie`, else `~/.config/magpie`, the same rule magpie itself follows.

## Privacy

What a call's error said stays between you and your own mailbox: the mail carries the provider, model, agent, status and the vendor's own error words, cut to 400 characters, and nothing else — no conversation content, no prompt text. The hook reads only magpie's own files and your SMTP server; it sends to no third party. The digest, when you turn it on, carries only counts — sessions as id prefixes, agents, providers, models, tokens and credits — and only for the providers on your list, if you set one.

## Test

```sh
bun test packages/mail-watch
```

@magpie-community/middleware-antigravity.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-antigravity-cloak

Claude Code and Claude Desktop on an Antigravity account, as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware.

Antigravity answers a request whose system prompt reads as Claude Code's or the Claude Agent SDK's (which Claude Desktop's chats use) with `429 Resource has been exhausted`, however much quota is left. magpie shows it as a 400 that says so. Tried with a real account, Antigravity matches these pieces of the prompt:

- Claude Code's billing line, `x-anthropic-billing-header: …`;
- `You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK`;
- Codex's own prompt for its GPT-5 models, `You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-5` or `You are Codex, a coding agent based on GPT-5`. A Codex chat begun on a GPT model keeps it after `/model` or a fork onto an Antigravity model, so that chat 429s while a new one works;
- Hermes Agent's earlier default persona, `Hermes Agent, an intelligent AI assistant created by Nous Research`, which a SOUL.md the user edited keeps (Hermes' current default goes through). Breaking it after `You` doesn't help; it is broken after the `H`.

The same prompt goes through when each has a zero-width space (U+200B) inside it. This middleware puts one after the first letter of `x-anthropic-billing-header`, `Claude Agent SDK`, those two Codex lines and Hermes' line, in the system prompt only, and only in what an Antigravity account is sent. Every other provider, a Claude subscription above all, gets the prompt as the agent wrote it, even in a routing group that tries Antigravity first. The model reads the words as before.

It needs a magpie with the `onProvider` hook (v0.1.1283 or later): an older magpie loads it and never calls it, so requests go as they came.

magpie v0.1.1641 and later break these same lines on an Antigravity account by themselves (`magpie provider set antigravity prompt=as-written` turns that off), so there this middleware adds only `extraWords`.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-antigravity-cloak`.

## Before you turn it on

- This changes what Google is sent so that a request it means to refuse isn't refused. It may be against Antigravity's terms, and Google can ban the account for it. Use it on an account you can afford to lose.
- Google can change what it matches at any time. Then the refusal comes back, and magpie may no longer recognise it as this refusal: it can read as a real quota running out and rest the account. If that happens, add the new words to `extraWords`, or turn the plugin off.

## Options

```json
{ "extraWords": [], "accounts": ["antigravity"], "off": false }
```

- `extraWords`: more words to break the same way, matched whatever their case.
- `accounts`: the subscriptions it acts on, by kind. `antigravity` is the default.
- `off`: leave every request as it came.

中文：Antigravity 看到 Claude Code / Claude Agent SDK / Codex GPT-5 / Hermes Agent 旧版默认人设的系统提示词会回一个假的 429。这个中间件只在发给 Antigravity 账号的请求里，往 `x-anthropic-billing-header`、`Claude Agent SDK` 和 Codex 给 GPT-5 模型的身份行（在 GPT 模型上开始、再切到 Antigravity 模型的 Codex 对话会带着它），以及 Hermes Agent 旧版默认人设（SOUL.md）那句里插一个零宽空格，其他供应商（尤其是 Claude 订阅）收到的提示词不变。这样做可能违反 Antigravity 的条款，账号有被封的风险，请只用在可以承受损失的账号上。需要 magpie v0.1.1283 或更新版本。

After [hexiaolv/magpie-antigravity-cloak](https://github.com/hexiaolv/magpie-antigravity-cloak) (MIT), which breaks a longer list of words in every request, whatever provider it goes to.

@magpie-community/middleware-block-patte.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-block-patterns

Rejects requests that contain text you list, as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. A request with one of your words or patterns in it is turned away with a 400 before it reaches a model; everything else is sent on untouched.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-block-patterns`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options block-patterns '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "words": ["project-codename"],
  "patterns": ["\\b\\d{3}-\\d{4}\\b"],
  "system": true,
  "message": "" }
```

- **`words`.** Plain substrings, matched anywhere in the text, ignoring case.
- **`patterns`.** Regular expressions, also matched ignoring case.
- **`system`.** `true` (the default) reads the system prompt as well as the user's turns, so a word in either turns the request away. `false` leaves every system prompt out and reads the user's turns alone. Where each API keeps its system prompt is listed under "What it reads".
- **`message`.** The error text to use in place of the default one.

## What it reads

Every content shape an agent sends, in all four APIs magpie serves: plain string content, `text` and `input_text` blocks, Responses `input` items, and Gemini `parts`. Anthropic, Chat Completions, Responses and Gemini are all covered.

Every user turn is read, not only the last one, so a word earlier in the conversation is caught. System prompts are read too, unless you set `system` to `false`. Each API keeps its system prompt in its own place, and all of them are read:

| API | Read when `system` is true |
|---|---|
| Anthropic | the top-level `system` field, as a string or as text blocks, and any `system` / `developer` message |
| Chat Completions | any `system` / `developer` message |
| Responses | `instructions`, and any `system` / `developer` input item |
| Gemini | `systemInstruction` and `system_instruction`, as a string or as a `{ parts }` object |

Tool calls, tool arguments, tool results and Gemini thought parts are never read, so a file an agent reads that contains a word doesn't stop it, and a word the model said back doesn't either.

## If a pattern does not compile

A `patterns` entry that is not a valid regular expression is ignored, and the rest of your options still work. Nothing is thrown: a typo in one entry cannot turn away every request the gateway sees. Fix the pattern in **Plugins › Installed › Options** — the entries that failed are not reported, so check the spelling if a word you listed seems to be passing through.

## What it is not

This is literal matching, not a safety classifier. It does not understand what a request means, and it does not judge whether anything is harmful. A synonym, a paraphrase, a misspelling or a word split by formatting passes it. Don't rely on it as a real guardrail against a determined prompt: use it to keep listed text — an internal codename, a customer's name, an unreleased feature — out of what your gateway sends.

## Word Guard vs this

Both match a list of words and regular expressions, and both can turn a request away, so it is worth saying which to install.

- **Word Guard** can mask a match and send the request on, and can mask matches in the replies as well. It reads only the last user message by default, and never reads a system prompt.
- **This one** only turns requests away — there is no mask and it never reads replies. In exchange it reads every user turn and every system prompt, wherever the API keeps it.

Install this one when you want a listed word to be an error rather than something silently rewritten, and when a system prompt is part of what you want to keep off the wire. Install Word Guard when you would rather the request go through with the word blanked out. They can be installed together.

magpie already redacts secrets (API keys and tokens) before a request leaves your computer, and puts them back in the reply. Neither package is needed for that.

中文：按你列出的词与正则拒绝请求（纯字面匹配，不是安全分类器），可选择是否读取 system 提示词。

# @magpie-community/middleware-codex-history

**Magpie 原生历史过滤插件 / Native history compatibility middleware**

缓解 Codex 切换供应商、账号或上游资源后，旧会话出现密文验证失败、部分历史 item ID 不属于当前资源的问题。只处理发出的 Responses 请求，不修改原会话文件或 Codex `base_url`。

**插件只提供历史过滤，不包含 ModelTrace、降智检测或模型保护。** 无独立后台服务、管理端口、运行时依赖或额外模型请求。规则默认全部关闭，在 Magpie 自带的插件 Options 中按供应商设置。

## 安装

在 Magpie 的 **Plugins → Discover → Gateway middleware** 中安装 **Codex History Filter**，或使用命令行：

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-codex-history
```

社区版本只发布历史过滤中间件；模型工作台单独本地维护，不包含在本包中。无需启动 Codex Filter Manager，不要同时启用两份过滤插件。需要支持 gateway middleware 及 `onProvider` 钩子的 Magpie；v0.1.2 已在 0.1.2131 的隔离实例中验证，其他版本需核对插件加载状态。

## 设置

打开 **Plugins → Installed → 本插件 → Options**，保存以下示例，替换 `demo` 和 `backup` 为你实际使用的 Magpie 供应商 ID：

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "magpie:demo": {
      "historyFilter": true,
      "preserveEncryptedInclude": true
    },
    "magpie:backup": {
      "historyFilter": false,
      "preserveEncryptedInclude": true
    }
  },
  "aliases": {}
}
```

- 请求模型为 `demo/gpt-6-astra` 时，使用 `magpie:demo` 的规则；ID 是模型前缀，不是供应商显示名称。
- 通过 Magpie 路由组或 fallback 发出的请求（模型名是分组），在每次实际尝试某个供应商时，按该供应商 ID 的规则过滤。不需要、也不应该为路由组单独建规则。
- `historyFilter: true` 开启过滤；`false`、删除该规则或空配置均为直通。不同会话按各自请求独立处理，可同时过滤多个供应商。
- `preserveEncryptedInclude: true` 保留客户端对**新响应**中 `reasoning.encrypted_content` 的请求，推荐开启。它不会保留**旧历史**中的密文。省略或设置为 `false` 会移除这一 include 值，不影响其他 include 项。
- 供应商改名后，旧会话可能仍发送旧前缀；可设置 `"aliases": {"old-demo": "demo"}`。别名同样作用于路由组中实际尝试的供应商 ID，只用于选择过滤规则，不改写请求模型，也不替代 Magpie 自己的路由别名。
- 无 `供应商/模型` 前缀或非 Responses 协议的请求保持原样。未配置的供应商不会被自动过滤。

保存 Options 后，Magpie 在后续请求加载规则。无需另开网页或重启 Codex；是否成功加载以 Magpie 插件页的错误统计为准。插件页的调用次数统计每次钩子调用：每个 Responses 请求经过 `onRequest`，每次供应商尝试经过 `onProvider`，没有命中规则、原样放行的请求也会计入，它不表示过滤次数。

## 原理与边界

开启后，插件移除旧 reasoning 条目、明确标记的加密内容，以及可独立携带内容的消息和工具条目中的可选服务器 ID；设置 `store: false`。保留正文、工具参数、结果、`call_id` 配对、文件引用及普通业务 ID，不改变请求模型或推理强度。

**v0.1.1：历史搜索兼容修复。** 原生 `web_search_call` 可能依赖已删除的 reasoning，导致上游提示 `was provided without its required reasoning item`。开启过滤后，历史搜索条目转为带标记的助手文字，保留已记录的动作、查询、状态和来源数据，去除服务器条目 ID 与内部回合元数据；后续结论、引用及普通工具调用配对保持原样。不重新搜索、不补造未记录的结果。该处理适用于携带明文历史的普通对话和文字总结，不解密压缩历史。

**v0.1.2：路由组与 fallback 兼容修复。** 经 Magpie 路由组或 fallback 发出的请求，模型名是分组而不是供应商，路由前的前缀匹配找不到规则，旧密文和条目 ID 会原样发给已开启过滤的成员，上游返回 `created under a different Azure OpenAI resource` 等错误。现在 `onProvider` 在每次供应商尝试时按该供应商规则过滤；直接选择供应商的请求仍在 `onRequest` 过滤，并通过 `ctx.state` 标记，不会重复处理。

`previous_response_id`、`conversation`、`item_reference`、加密压缩历史和 `/responses/compact` 无法安全跨资源迁移时，会明确拒绝，提示整理文字摘要后新建会话，不会静默丢弃这些上下文。

- 不能解密旧密文、迁移所有服务器资源引用，或保证消除全部 Azure 历史错误。移除内部推理状态也可能影响长任务连续性。
- Magpie 请求钩子限时 250 毫秒；加载失败、异常或超时可能按 Magpie 的机制放行原请求。插件不是强制安全边界。
- 只覆盖进入 Magpie agent middleware 的 Responses 请求；Magpie 自身的标题、分类器等内部请求不经过此钩子。WebSocket、Chat Completions、Lite HTTP 标头修改不在本插件范围内。
- 直接选择供应商时按模型前缀选择规则；路由组和 fallback 按每次实际尝试的供应商选择。`onProvider` 不能拒绝请求，所以上述无法迁移的内容经路由组发出时只能原样发送，由上游报错；直接选择供应商时仍会被明确拒绝。其他插件若在本插件之后再改写请求，结果不受本插件控制。
- 不采集或保存凭据、请求正文，不执行检测、重试或模型调用。上游正常请求仍按上游规则计费。

## 停用、升级与旧版迁移

在 Magpie 插件页关闭本插件即可停止全部过滤；删除某条供应商规则只停用该供应商。卸载也在 Magpie 中完成，不需要恢复 `base_url`。通过本地路径安装时，移动或删除目录前先卸载旧插件。

若此前使用 Codex Filter Manager v1.0.5 自动安装的本地 `magpie-plugin`，先在旧管理页关闭该供应商的自动保护（若有旧设置），停止旧管理服务，再在 Magpie 中停用或卸载旧的本地历史插件，最后安装本插件并复制所需历史规则。原有规则的 `stripResponsesLiteHeader` 会被忽略，可删除。不要同时启用两份历史过滤插件。

社区版本合并并完成 dist 发布后，可在 Magpie 插件页更新；现有 Options 无需改写，更新前可自行备份。不要上传 Magpie 的 `plugins.json`，它可能包含其他插件的私有设置。本插件不直接读写该文件，规则由宿主通过 Options 传入。

## English

Opt-in Magpie gateway middleware for Codex Responses history after switching providers or accounts. It strips old reasoning/encrypted items and optional server IDs from portable history, preserving readable content and tool-call pairing. **History filtering only: no model detector, guard, background server, credentials or extra upstream calls.**

Install from **Plugins → Discover → Gateway middleware**, or run `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-codex-history`. In the plugin's **Options**, configure `providers["magpie:<provider-id>"]` as shown above. Every provider defaults to passthrough. A request to `provider/model` uses that prefix's rule. A request through a Magpie group or fallback is filtered on each provider try with the tried provider's rule, so a group needs no rule of its own. Requests from different sessions remain independent. `aliases` maps an old prefix or provider ID to a rule ID only. `preserveEncryptedInclude: true` keeps requests for new encrypted response content while still removing historical ciphertext.

Unsafe server-only references and encrypted compaction are rejected explicitly when a provider is chosen directly. A provider try can't be refused, so through a group they are sent as they were. Magpie may fail open on plugin errors/timeouts. The Plugins page counts every hook call, passed-through requests included, not filtered requests. Disable or remove it in Magpie; it never edits Codex configuration.

Version 0.1.1 converts historical native `web_search_call` items to labeled assistant text after removing old reasoning. Recorded actions, queries, status and sources remain available; native item IDs and internal turn metadata are removed. Subsequent answers and ordinary tool-call pairs remain intact. No searches are rerun, absent results are not reconstructed, and encrypted compaction is not decrypted. The community package contains only the middleware; the optional model workbench is maintained separately for local use.

Version 0.1.2 filters group and fallback requests on each provider try (`onProvider`). Before it, a request named after a group matched no rule, so old ciphertext and item IDs reached providers whose filter was on. A direct request filtered by `onRequest` is marked in `ctx.state` and isn't filtered again.

## 开发与来源

```sh
bun test packages/codex-history
```

测试只使用本地虚构数据，不调用模型。核心代码来自 [Codex Filter Manager](https://github.com/unisong/codex-filter-manager)（MIT），本包的镜像源码在 [magpie-codex-history-filter](https://github.com/unisong/magpie-codex-history-filter)，来源提交和 SHA-256 记录于 [PROVENANCE.json](PROVENANCE.json)。为匹配社区 middleware 包格式，将共用算法与请求钩子合并为单个无 import 文件。

接口参考：[Magpie middleware 文档](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#middleware)。

MIT，保留原项目贡献者署名，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

manifest.name: @magpie-community/middleware-history-trim
manifest.description: Send a request's history smaller: blank-line runs folded, a system prompt written twice and a message repeated right after itself dropped, a past tool result longer than maxToolLength cut, as magpie gateway middleware

@magpie-community/middleware-history-tri.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-history-trim

A request's history, sent smaller, as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. It folds a run of blank lines, drops a system prompt written twice and a message repeated right after itself, and cuts a past tool result longer than `maxToolLength` at a word boundary.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-history-trim`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options history-trim '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "maxToolLength": 2000 }
```

**`maxToolLength`** (the default, 2000). A tool result from an earlier turn longer than this many characters is cut to it, at the nearest word boundary within 80 characters, and ends with `\n...[truncated]`. A cut never splits an emoji or another surrogate pair in half.

- The turn being sent now is never cut, and never rewritten by any of the four steps. A message at or after the last assistant message is the history the model has not read yet, so it goes out whole — a patch line, a Markdown hard line break or a trailing tab in it survives; a history with no assistant message in it is left whole too.
- Both shapes are cut: a Chat `role: "tool"` message whose content is a string, and an Anthropic `tool_result` block inside a content array, whether its content is a string or an array of text parts.
- A number below 256 or above 1000000 is not a length anyone means, and falls back to the default.

**`compressToolResults: false`**. Leaves every tool result whole. The other three steps still run.

**`preserveSystemPrompt: true`**. Keeps system messages out of all four steps: not folded, not deduplicated, not dropped as a repeat.

Nothing sent once is dropped. Apart from the tool-result cut, every step removes only what is there twice: a second system message with the same text, and a message equal to the one before it in every field — role, content, `tool_calls`, `name` — neither of them a tool result.

**Prompt cache.** Dropping a message or folding whitespace changes the prefix of the request, and a provider caches on that prefix: the request after each change, and every turn of a conversation whose history keeps changing, is billed as uncached input. On a long history read back many times that is a fraction of what the steps save; on a short history that would have been a cache hit every turn it can cost more than it saves.

Only `body.messages` is read, so it acts on a Chat or an Anthropic request. A Responses or a Gemini request carries its history elsewhere and goes on unchanged; so does a request whose body it cannot read, because an exception here would take the request down with it.

Ported from OmniRoute's lite engine (`open-sse/services/compression/lite.ts`, MIT); what was left out, and the four places this one deliberately differs, are listed in `PROVENANCE.json`.

中文：把请求的历史发得更小——连续空行折叠成一行空行、逐字重复的 system 提示与紧挨着重复的消息去掉、历史中超过 `maxToolLength` 的工具结果在词边界处截断并标上 `[truncated]`。正在发送的这一轮（最后一条 assistant 之后的消息）四步都不碰：补丁行、Markdown 硬换行、行尾空白原样发出；整段没有 assistant 的首轮请求同样原样发出。判"重复"比的是整条消息不是内容——system 要整段文本相同，其它消息要每个字段（`tool_calls`、`name` 都算）都相同。只读 `body.messages`，Chat 与 Anthropic 请求生效；`compressToolResults: false` 不截断工具结果，`preserveSystemPrompt: true` 让 system 消息不被任何一步改动。prompt cache 的账：删一条消息或折叠空白都会改掉请求前缀，提供方按前缀缓存，改动后的那次请求、以及历史一直在变的后续轮次，输入按未缓存价计费——历史长且反复回读时这笔开销只占省下的一小部分，历史短且本来每轮都命中缓存时可能得不偿失。

manifest.name: @magpie-community/middleware-model-map
manifest.description: New API's model_mapping (模型重定向) as magpie gateway middleware: send the model an agent asks for as another, and keep the asked name in replies

@magpie-community/middleware-model-map.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-model-map

New API's **模型重定向** (a channel's `model_mapping`) as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. The model an agent asks for is sent upstream as another model. Replies then name the model the agent asked for, so an agent that reads its model's name back (Claude Code does, to size its context window) sees the name it asked for.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-model-map`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options model-map '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "mapping": {
    "fast": "deepseek-chat",
    "/^claude-(.*)$/": "glm-$1"
} }
```

- **Mapping.** A name maps to its target. Names chain (`a → b → c`) until there is nothing more to map, and a cycle stops before it repeats.
- **Patterns.** A key written `/like this/` is a regular expression, and its target can use `$1` for the first group.
- **Flat form.** New API's flat form, `{"fast": "deepseek-chat"}`, works as well.
- **`keep_upstream_name`.** Set it to `true` to leave the upstream model's name in replies.

The target has to be a model magpie can route: a model of one of your providers, or one of magpie's own ids (`deepseek/deepseek-chat`, for example).

**Gemini.** A Gemini request names its model in the URL; magpie moves it into the body before the middleware runs, so it is mapped like any other API, and the reply's `modelVersion` names the model asked for again.

中文：New API 的「模型重定向」，作为 magpie 网关中间件。回复里的模型名会还原成 agent 请求时用的名字。

manifest.name: @magpie-community/middleware-param-override
manifest.description: New API's param_override (参数覆盖) as magpie gateway middleware: set, delete, move and rewrite any field of what agents send, with conditions

@magpie-community/middleware-param-overr.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-param-override

New API's **参数覆盖** (a channel's `param_override`) as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. It sets, deletes, moves and rewrites any field of the requests agents send through magpie, whichever provider serves them. The options are New API's JSON as it is, so you can paste a `param_override` from New API unchanged.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-param-override`. Then set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options param-override '<json>'`.

## Options

There are two forms, as in New API:

```json
{ "temperature": 0.2, "max_tokens": 8000 }
```

Each key is set on the body as it is.

```json
{ "operations": [
  { "path": "max_tokens", "mode": "set", "value": 32000,
    "conditions": [{ "path": "max_tokens", "mode": "gt", "value": 32000 }] },
  { "path": "temperature", "mode": "delete",
    "conditions": [{ "path": "model", "mode": "contains", "value": "reasoner" }] },
  { "mode": "return_error", "value": { "message": "opus is not allowed here", "status_code": 403 },
    "conditions": [{ "path": "model", "mode": "contains", "value": "opus" }] }
] }
```

The operations run in order. Keys set beside `operations` are applied first.

| Field | |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | A gjson path: `a.b.0`. `messages.-1` counts from the end, `tools.*.name` matches every item, and `\.` is a dot inside a key. |
| `mode` | `set` (`keep_origin`: only when missing), `delete`, `move` / `copy` (`from`, `to`), `prepend` / `append` (arrays joined, strings joined, objects merged; `keep_origin` keeps keys already there), `trim_prefix`, `trim_suffix`, `ensure_prefix`, `ensure_suffix`, `trim_space`, `to_lower`, `to_upper`, `replace` / `regex_replace` (`from`, `to`; Go's `${1}` works), `return_error`, `prune_objects` |
| `value` | What to set, join or trim. For `return_error`, a message or `{message, status_code}`; the agent gets the error in its own API's shape. For `prune_objects`, a `type` or `{type, where, conditions, logic, recursive}`. |
| `conditions` | `[{path, mode, value, invert, pass_missing_key}]`, where `mode` is `full`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `contains`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt` or `lte`. A path is looked up in the body first, then in the request: `model`, `request_path`, `protocol` (`anthropic`, `chat`, `responses`, `gemini`), `agent`, `stream`. |
| `logic` | `OR` (New API's default) or `AND`. |

Some of New API's modes have nothing to act on here and are left out: the header modes (`set_header`, `pass_headers`…), `sync_fields`, and conditions on retries, users and groups. The middleware sees only the body.

Unlike New API, an operation that can't apply is skipped (a `move` from a missing path, `trim_prefix` on a number) and the request goes on. If the middleware itself fails, magpie sends the request as it came.

## Recipes

- Cap `max_tokens` for a provider with a lower limit: the first example above.
- Drop a parameter a provider refuses: `{"path": "tools.*.input_examples", "mode": "delete"}`.
- Strip a vendor prefix from model names: `{"path": "model", "mode": "trim_prefix", "value": "openai/"}`.
- Keep an agent off a model: `return_error` with a `model` condition.
- Remove old thinking blocks: `{"path": "messages", "mode": "prune_objects", "value": "thinking"}`.

中文：New API 的「参数覆盖」，作为 magpie 网关中间件。配置是 New API 的同一份 JSON，可以原样粘贴过来。

manifest.name: @magpie-community/middleware-reserve
manifest.description: Routings for magpie's gateway that keep something in reserve: fill accounts in order up to a ceiling, or spend subscriptions before pay-per-token keys

@magpie-community/middleware-reserve.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-reserve

Two routings for [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) that keep something in reserve. Pick one for a provider's accounts or keys, or for a routing group's members, and magpie's gateway tries them in the order it gives.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-reserve`. While it is on, every routing picker offers `reserve/ceiling` and `reserve/accounts-first`. From the command line, a group takes one with:

```sh
magpie group set <id> routing=reserve/ceiling
```

## Routings

**`reserve/ceiling`** fills the accounts in the order listed, but keeps the last share of each one's allowance.

- The first account takes requests until it has used `ceiling` percent of its allowance, then the next one takes over.
- Once every account is past the ceiling, the least used goes first.
- A seat whose allowance isn't known (an API key, or an account not read yet) counts as below the ceiling.
- A seat resting after a failure goes last.

Use it to keep, say, a fifth of your main account's week for when you're at its own app, while the gateway uses the rest.

**`reserve/accounts-first`** puts subscriptions before API keys, so what you have paid for already goes first. A key that bills by the token is used only when no account can take the request.

- Accounts go least used first.
- Keys go by their weight, highest first, then by what they were sent lately.
- Seats resting after a failure go last.

## Options

```json
{ "ceiling": 80 }
```

`ceiling` is the percent of an account's allowance past which `reserve/ceiling` moves on, from 1 to 100. It is 80 when none is set. Set it under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options reserve '{"ceiling": 70}'`.

## Test

`strategies.json` holds the cases: seats in, the order wanted out. `reserve.test.mjs` runs them with `checkStrategies()` from `scripts/middleware.mjs`, and checks that each answer is a permutation of the seats.

```sh
bun test packages/reserve
```

中文：两种为账号留余量的路由。`reserve/ceiling` 按列出的顺序使用账号，每个账号用到额度的 `ceiling`%（默认 80）就换下一个，全部超过后用得最少的优先；`reserve/accounts-first` 订阅账号优先于按量计费的 API key，key 按权重排序。休息中的总是排最后。

manifest.name: @magpie-community/middleware-system-prompt
manifest.description: New API's system_prompt (系统提示词) as magpie gateway middleware: give agents' requests a system prompt of yours, in each API's own place for it

options.system_prompt: Reply in the language the user writes in.

@magpie-community/middleware-system-prom.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-system-prompt

New API's **系统提示词** (a channel's `system_prompt` and its override switch) as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. It gives the requests agents send a system prompt of yours, in each API's own place for one:

| API | Where the prompt goes |
| --- | --- |
| Anthropic | `system` |
| Chat | the first `system` or `developer` message |
| Responses | `instructions` |
| Gemini | `systemInstruction` |

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-system-prompt`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options system-prompt '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "system_prompt": "Reply in the language the user writes in.",
  "override": true, "position": "append",
  "agents": ["claude"], "models": ["deepseek"] }
```

- **No system prompt yet.** A request without one gets yours.
- **`override`.** A request that has its own prompt keeps it unchanged, unless `override` is `true`. Then yours goes in as well, placed by `position`:
  - `"append"` (the default) puts yours after it. Agents cache their own prompt, so adding after it keeps that cache.
  - `"prepend"` puts yours before it, as New API does. This makes the provider read the whole prompt again on every turn.
- **`agents`.** When given, the prompt applies only to these agents, by magpie's agent ids: `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, and so on.
- **`models`.** When given, the prompt applies only to models whose names begin with one of these prefixes.

Codex sends its own model instructions, and changing them can change how its models behave. Use `agents` to leave Codex out if you don't want that.

中文：New API 的「系统提示词」，作为 magpie 网关中间件。默认把你的提示词加在 agent 自己的提示词之后，这样不会破坏提示缓存。

manifest.name: @magpie-community/middleware-think-tags
manifest.description: Take a model's <think>…</think> out of its reply's text, or put a Chat reply's reasoning_content into it (New API's thinking_to_content), as magpie gateway middleware

manifest.name: @magpie-community/middleware-think-tags
manifest.description: Take a model's <think>…</think> out of its reply's text, or put a Chat reply's reasoning_content into it (New API's thinking_to_content), as magpie gateway middleware

@magpie-community/middleware-think-tags.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-think-tags

A model's thinking, where its reply's text is, as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. It either takes thinking out of the text, or puts it in (New API's `thinking_to_content`).

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-think-tags`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options think-tags '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "mode": "strip" }
```

**`strip`** (the default). Some models (open reasoning models served by vLLM, Ollama and many relays) write their thinking into the reply as `<think>…</think>`. This mode takes that block out, so an agent doesn't keep it in its history and send it back every turn.

- Only a block at the start of the text is taken out. A `<think>` the model writes later, in code for example, stays.
- A `</think>` inside the block in Markdown code (`` `</think>` ``, or a fenced block) is part of the thinking, an example written out, not its end.
- A tag split across streamed chunks is still found.
- It works on Anthropic, Chat and Responses replies, streamed or whole.

**`to_content`**. A Chat reply's `reasoning_content` (or `reasoning`) is put into its text as `<think>…</think>`, for a client that shows only the text.

- This mode works on Chat replies only. An Anthropic thinking block carries a signature, and turned into text it would fail the next turn.
- It changes what the agent keeps and sends back, so it suits a chat client better than a coding agent.

中文：`strip` 去掉回复开头模型写出的 `<think>…</think>`；`to_content` 把 Chat 回复的 reasoning_content 放进正文（New API 的 thinking_to_content）。

manifest.name: @magpie-community/middleware-word-guard
manifest.description: New API's sensitive-word filter (敏感词过滤) as magpie gateway middleware: turn away or mask words and patterns in what agents send, and in replies

@magpie-community/middleware-word-guard.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-word-guard

New API's **敏感词过滤** as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. It keeps the words and patterns you list out of what agents send: a request with one is turned away, or has the word masked. It can mask them in replies too.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-word-guard`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options word-guard '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "words": ["project-codename"],
  "patterns": ["\\b\\d{3}-\\d{4}\\b"],
  "action": "reject",
  "check": "last" }
```

- **`words`.** Words matched anywhere in the text, ignoring case.
- **`patterns`.** Regular expressions, also matched ignoring case.
- **`action`.** `reject` (the default) turns the request away with a 400 that names the word, in the agent's API's error shape. `mask` replaces each match with `mask` (default `***`) and sends the request on.
- **`check`.** `last` (the default) reads only the last user message that has text, which is the turn being sent. That is what New API reads. `all` reads every user message, so a word earlier in the conversation keeps turning requests away.
- **`replies`.** Set it to `true` to mask matches in the text that comes back as well, in every API magpie serves — Anthropic, Chat, Responses and Gemini, streamed or whole. A word split across two streamed events isn't caught.
- **`message`.** The error text to use in place of the default one.

The middleware reads only the user's own text. It doesn't read tool results, tool calls or the system prompt, so a file an agent reads that contains the word doesn't stop it.

If you want a listed word to be a 400 rather than something masked, and you also want every earlier user turn and the system prompt read, that is [block-patterns](../block-patterns). It never masks and never reads replies, so the two can be installed together.

magpie already redacts secrets (API keys and tokens) before a request leaves your computer, and puts them back in the reply. You don't need this middleware for secrets.

中文：New API 的「敏感词过滤」，作为 magpie 网关中间件。只检查用户自己写的文字，可拒绝请求或替换成 `***`，也可以替换回复里的词。

@magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth

[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) / [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) provider 插件：**AutoClaw（智谱澳龙 / OpenClaw 云端账号体系）**。

一个包注册两个供应商，按账号所在地分开登录、分开记额度：

| 供应商 id | 登录方式 | 上游 host | 模型引用 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `autoclaw` | Google / z.ai 网页 OAuth | `autoglm-api.autoglm.ai` | `autoclaw/zai_auto` 等 |
| `autoclaw-cn` | 手机验证码（+86） | `autoglm-api.zhipuai.cn` | `autoclaw-cn/zai_auto` 等 |

两个供应商都支持 magpie 的多账号、故障切换、token 自动轮换与积分余额显示。实测可用的 4 个在线模型为带前缀的 routeModelId（`zai_` 智谱 / `zaicoding_` coding plan）：

- `zai_auto` / `zai_auto-fast`（自动路由，支持 reasoning variants：low / high / max）
- `zai_glm-5.3-flash`（极速推理，支持 reasoning variants）
- `zaicoding_glm-5.3`（GLM-5.3 编程专项，支持 reasoning variants）

> 注：旧版中的 `zai_glm-5-turbo` 以及豆包 DeepSeek 映射 `tdpsk_deepseek-v4-flash-202605`、`tdpsk_deepseek-v4-pro-202606` 已被上游下线（调用均返回 `400 非法模型`），本版本已从模型列表中移除。

## 安装

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth
magpie plugin login autoclaw                   # Google / z.ai 网页登录
magpie plugin login autoclaw-cn                # 手机验证码
magpie provider test autoclaw zai_auto
magpie quota                                   # 积分余额
```

OpenCode 同样可加载（`opencode auth login`）。登录信息保存在 magpie 的 `plugin-auth.json`（600 权限）/ OpenCode 的 `auth.json`。

## 直连说明（不经本地网关）

插件**直连上游云 API**，登录/对话/刷新/积分全部自行完成：

- 对话走 `POST {host}/autoclaw-proxy/proxy/autoclaw/v1/chat/completions`（`X-Authorization` 鉴权）；
- token 过期前自动轮换（refresh token 一次一换，`auth.refresh` 钩子交给 magpie 串行化，不会双花）；
- 积分余额通过 `auth.usage` 的 `balance` 显示（纯积分制，无总量上限，细分钱包写在括号里），
  同时作为预付钱包窗口 `{ name: "积分余额", balance, unit: "积分" }` 上报（magpie ≥ v0.1.1790，
  #3950）：路由按真实余额认识和排位账号，不发明百分比，余额 0 算用完；更早的 magpie
  不认识 `balance`，账号维持原状。
  上游没有积分流水/用量接口（wallets.v2 只有余额），「本轮消耗」窗口**由本地余额差值算**：
  每次 `usage()` 记下本轮峰值，`峰值 − 当前 = 本轮已消耗`，**任何上涨**（相对上次
  观察到的余额，含从 0 回升——每日签到、礼包、兑换）都开新一轮，不等涨过旧峰值（签到常在花费
  之后到）。因为每天签到都会开新一轮，「本轮」≈「自今天签到以来」。这个窗口带
  `aside: true`，只展示、不参与路由：它的百分比是「自上次上涨以来花掉的比例」，不是池子剩余。
  `total_balance` 为 null/空串/非数时按未知处理（「积分响应异常」），不记账。
  状态按账号（键复用 `signinAccountKey`，#254：uid，没 uid 按 refresh token 哈希）存在
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/magpie/autoclaw-usage.json`（或 `~/.config/magpie/`，`AUTOCLAW_USAGE_STATE_FILE`
  可改址），临时文件 + rename 写入，30 天没动的条目清走；插件更新不会丢。
  测试可用 `_internal.setUsageStatePath` 把状态文件指到临时目录。
- **国际版登录是完整本地实现**：插件在 127.0.0.1 上取官方 TokenServer 端口池中的一个端口
  （18432/19654/19723/53699，OAuth client 回调白名单；被占自动顺延）起临时服务器，内嵌引导页完成
  阿里滑块验证（`AliyunCaptcha` SDK，`ali_captcha_verify_param` 回执）→ 获取授权页 →
  自动跳转 Google/z.ai → 回调自动捕获 code，全程浏览器完成、无需粘贴；登录结束服务器即关
  （未完成时 10 分钟后自动关闭释放端口）。回调 code 必须匹配授权页下发的 `state`，其余一律拒收
  （防伪造回调劫持登录）；本地服务器的写接口仅接受 127.0.0.1/localhost 来源。

## 每日签到

两种方式，推荐用**原生签到**：

**① magpie 原生签到（magpie ≥ v0.1.1083，推荐）**：插件实现 `auth.checkin` 钩子，走 magpie 统一调度——Settings → Usage → Plugins 里每个供应商有 **Daily check-in** 开关（默认关），打开后每天每账号自动签一次（北京时间；启动 2 分钟后首查、每 30 分钟轮询，失败 30 分钟后重试），账户 Usage 卡片显示签到结果，也可 **Check in now** 手动签。

**② 旧链路自动补签（默认关）**：查额度（`magpie quota`、GUI 刷新）与 token 刷新时发现未签就补签（服务端幂等，本地按天去重、失败按小时重试）。旧版 magpie / OpenCode 宿主或偏好该行为的用户开启 `signinOnUsage`。

`magpie quota` 的额度窗口里始终显示**每日签到**状态行（今日已签 ✓ / 今日未签 +N）。

旧链路的开关有**两个通道**（插件 options 优先，配置文件兜底；原生签到开关只在 GUI 的 Settings 里）：

```sh
# 通道 1：插件 options（magpie CLI）
magpie plugin options @magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth '{"signin": false}'        # 关闭自动补签总开关
magpie plugin options @magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth '{"signinHour": 8}'        # 只在 8:00–8:59 补签
magpie plugin options @magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth '{"signinOnUsage": true}'  # 开启查额度/刷新自动补签

# 通道 2：配置文件 ~/.config/magpie/autoclaw.json（保存即生效，热读取）
cat > ~/.config/magpie/autoclaw.json <<'EOF'
{ "signin": true, "signinHour": null, "signinOnUsage": true }
EOF
```

| 选项 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `signin` | `true` | 旧链路自动补签总开关（不影响原生 checkin） |
| `signinOnUsage` | `false` | 查额度/刷新时自动补签（默认关，交给原生开关） |
| `signinHour` | `null` | 限定补签小时：`8` = 仅当本地时间处于 8:00–8:59 时补签；`null` 不限 |

## 对话网关与请求整形

AutoClaw 对话网关对请求形状有硬性要求，缺任一条都回 `406 Not Acceptable` 且 body 为空：
- **官方 system 前缀**：必须以 `You are AutoClaw. Answer the user directly and concisely.` 开头（插件会自动合并进 caller 已有的 system 消息，无 system 时补一条最小 system）
- **删除 max_tokens**：网关拒收 `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens`，插件会在发送前自动剔除
- **不发送 X-Harness-Type**：上游收到 `X-Harness-Type` 即报 406，已删除该残留请求头
- **改写外部 Harness 身份声明**：上游拦截 system 中包含的外部 agent 身份句（如 `You are Codex`、`You are Claude Code` 等），插件的 `unflag` 会自动将其替换为兼容措辞，避免 406 拦截

- **官方客户端指纹（国际版对话）**：国际版对话请求带官方 AutoClaw 2.0.3 桌面端（`official` 渠道）的整套请求头，取自其 AppImage 的 `dist/main.cjs`：`X-Channel: official`、`X-Version: 2.0.3`、`X-Lang: en`、`X-Client-Type: pc`、`X-Product: autoclaw`、`x_trace_id: autoclaw-desktop`、`X-Auth-Appid/X-Auth-TimeStamp/X-Auth-Sign`（`md5("100003&<秒级时间戳>&<appKey>")`，与登录/积分接口同一签名）、`X-Request-Id` = `X-Trace-Id`（每次请求一个 UUID）、`X-Session-Id`（同一对话不变的 UUID，插件由对话首条消息导出）、OpenAI SDK 6.26.0 的 `User-Agent` 与 `X-Stainless-*`。`X-Tm` 与官方 `managedPlatform()` 一致：macOS `mac`、Windows `win`、Linux `linux`（x64/arm64 相同）。网关只在**非官方指纹**旁拒收 `X-Tm: linux`（403 `forbidden`，#367）；0.2.7–0.2.11 发的 `linux-x64` 只是绕过，不是官方值。

国内版 `autoclaw-cn` 走 AutoClaw 2.1.0 managed gateway（`autoglm-acceleration-api.zhipuai.cn`）；国际版 `autoclaw` 走海外直连网关（`autoglm-api.autoglm.ai`）。两者均已通过真实调用与推理验证。

## 已知行为

- 手机号账号只认国内 host（走 managed gateway，401/403 标记登录失效）；z.ai/Google 账号只认国际 host（401/403 自动换侧重试，均拒绝时标记失效）。
- 额度用完不算登录失效：上游以 `403` + `{"code":810000,"message":"GLM-5.3 免费额度已用完,…"}` 回答时（或 403 正文说额度/余额已用完），插件转成 `429`，原样带上游文案，登录保留（`X-Magpie-Sign-In: kept`），国际版也不再换 host 重试（plugins#274）。
- 账号被封不算登录失效：上游以 `403` + `{"code":410004,"message":"The account has been banned"}` 回答时（或 code/message 字段说 banned / 封禁 / 账号异常 / 账号被冻结等），对话、刷新、积分与签到都原样带上游文案，对话转成 `403 permission_error`，登录保留（`X-Magpie-Sign-In: kept`），不再换 host 重试。其他 401/403 仍按登录失效处理。
- 上游模型白名单随版本变化，模型下线时上游返回 `400 非法模型`（原样透传错误消息）。
- refresh token 与 AutoClaw 桌面端**共用会互踢**（双方都轮换），插件账号请勿同时在桌面端登录。
- 上游偶发改协议时，`CLIENT_VERSION` / 端点路径可能需要随官方客户端更新。

## 免责声明

本包为**非官方**社区插件，与智谱 AI / OpenClaw / AutoClaw 无任何关联。实现基于对官方客户端行为的逆向分析与实测，仅供个人学习研究；使用产生的账号风险由使用者自行承担。上游协议变更可能导致插件随时失效。

### Local sign-in page ownership

The plugin waits for the loopback listener before returning its guide URL. Magpie/OpenCode opens that URL; the callback does not launch a second browser through a shell. Cancelled or expired sessions release their port; begin a new sign-in rather than reusing the old URL.

The guide distinguishes an intentional authorization redirect from the user closing the page. The redirect must keep the loopback callback alive; closing a guide before authorization still cancels it. The guide reports a disconnected or expired session explicitly.

@magpie-community/opencode-catpaw-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-catpaw-auth

[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) / [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) provider 插件：**妙手（CatPaw，美团 `ai.catpaw.meituan.com`）**——登录、模型清单、聊天转发、余额查询。

请求形态按妙手桌面客户端 2026-10-09 的真实抓包移植（`round → event(running) → turn(SSE)` 简化链路，无跨请求会话复用）：请求头、`permissionMode` 均为客户端原样取值，脱敏抓包存于 `testdata/captured-*.json`，测试逐键比对。

## 安装

```
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-catpaw-auth
magpie plugin login catpaw     # 选「网页登录」/「妙手桌面端登录态」/「手动粘贴 token」
```

## 能力

- **登录**：
  - `网页登录`：插件问 `login-config` 取官方登录页，浏览器完成登录后，插件按官方客户端同款 **poll-token 通道**每秒轮询 `?sid` 直接拿 token——服务端对服务端，无监听端口、不受浏览器私有网络检查（PNA）影响；再问一次 `current-user` 补 uid/昵称（失败不影响登录）。
  - `妙手桌面端登录态`：每次请求前实时读 `~/.meituan-catpaw/auth.json`（mtime 缓存 5 分钟内；重开妙手即自动刷新）。
  - `手动粘贴 token`。
- **无续期接口**：token 过期后 401，网页登录重新发起一次即可；桌面端登录态则在妙手里重新登录（下一请求自动读新 token）。
- **聊天**：`round → event → turn` 三步会话机；上游 SSE 帧为累积式，插件做差分转 OpenAI delta（`content` + `reasoning_content`），流式与非流式都支持。
- **模型**：妙手桌面端的 9 个模型（longcat-2.0 / glm-5.3 系列 / deepseek-v4 系列 / minimax-m3 / kimi-k3 / auto），静态表（无远程目录接口）。不声明各模型的上下文/输出窗口（客户端未公布，不编造数字），也不声明图片输入（见下）。
- **工具与图片**：会话协议只收一段扁平文本 prompt，工具定义、工具结果与图片都无法送达——带这些的请求以 **400 明确拒绝**（而不是悄悄丢掉后答错）。
- **余额（usage）**：`GET https://catx.nocode.cn/api/gateway/credit/balance`，鉴权头是 **`X-Auth-Token: <accessToken>`**。
  - ⚠️ 这个接口与聊天网关**不是同一个鉴权头**：它只认 `X-Auth-Token`，把聊天用的 `Cookie: X-Passport-Token` 发到这里会稳定 401（body `code 4010`）。magpie 把 usage 的 401 当作「登录态失效」，所以鉴权头必须分开核对。
  - 读成功后**不带 `signIn` 字段**：magpie 以此把「已退出登录」的标记撤掉。
- **无签到**：CatPaw 没有每日签到活动。

## 协议细节

- 请求头（客户端抓包原样）：`m-appkey: com.sankuai.mcopilot.cli`、`m-debug: true`、`User-Agent: axios/1.19.0`、`m-traceid`/`x-request-id`/`x-trace-id` 每请求随机、`x-agent-version: 1.2.0-beta.6`、`Cookie: X-Passport-Token=...`（聊天网关 `ai.catpaw.meituan.com`）；抓包里的 `m-host` 是客户端本机局域网 IP，插件不发这个头。
- 请求体（客户端抓包原样）：`source: CatX`、`mode: CATX_APP`、`permissionMode: "unsafeBypassPermissions"`、`toolVersion: 2.0.2`。
- **注意**：上表是**聊天网关**的头；**余额接口**（`catx.nocode.cn`）改用 `X-Auth-Token`（见上）。
- turn SSE 总超时：15 分钟（带工具循环的长回答全程在推流，更短会把长回答掐断）。

## 环境变量（测试 / 镜像用）

| 变量 | 默认 |
|---|---|
| `CATPAW_AUTH_PATH` | `~/.meituan-catpaw/auth.json`（妙手桌面端登录态） |
| `CATPAW_BALANCE_URL` | `https://catx.nocode.cn/api/gateway/credit/balance`（余额接口，测试用） |
| `CATPAW_PASSPORT_BASE` | `https://catx.nocode.cn`（网页登录的 passport 域，测试用） |

## 测试

```
bun test packages/catpaw
```

测试打到本地假上游（`fake.mjs`），不触网、不使用真实 token。

## 许可

MIT。

# @magpie-community/opencode-cline-auth

Cline (cline.bot) on your own Cline account: the models Cline's gateway
serves — usage-billed models, ClinePass's and Cline's free models alike.
Provider id: `cline`.

## Signing in

- **Cline device sign-in** — the flow Cline's own client runs: the plugin asks
  WorkOS for a device code and opens the approval page, polls until you
  approve, then trades the WorkOS tokens at Cline's `/api/v1/auth/register`
  for the account's own token pair.
- **Cline API key** — create one at [app.cline.bot → Settings → API Keys](https://app.cline.bot/dashboard/account)
  and paste it. Sent as a plain Bearer key.

The sign-in is kept where OpenCode keeps auth (`auth.json` under the data
directory); magpie keeps plugin sign-ins in its own store
(`~/.config/magpie/plugin-auth.json`).

Refreshing:
- Access tokens are renewed through `/api/v1/auth/refresh`. Cline rotates
  the refresh token and refuses one already spent, so the rotated pair is
  kept in memory beside the store the moment it arrives: a save that fails
  can't leave the next request spending the token that was already spent.
- magpie renews the token ten minutes before it ends, through the plugin's
  `auth.refresh`, once for the account and before its requests, models and
  usage need it; magpie saves the new pair. OpenCode doesn't call that hook:
  there the token is refreshed five minutes before it ends, before a
  request, and the new pair is saved.
- Refreshes are serialized, magpie's renewal included, so two at once can't
  spend one token and lose the other; one that finds the token already
  renewed uses that pair.
- A refresh that fails for a while keeps the token that is still good, as
  Cline's own client does (magpie tries its renewal again shortly); only a
  refresh Cline refuses, or a token that has actually expired, is treated as
  the sign-in gone.

## Requests

Chat completions go to `https://api.cline.bot/api/v1/chat/completions` in
OpenAI's format (streaming included), with `Authorization: Bearer
workos:<access token>` for a signed-in account or the raw API key, and the
full client-identity header set Cline's own clients send (`HTTP-Referer`,
`X-Title`, `User-Agent: Cline/<version>`, `X-CLIENT-TYPE: cline-cli`,
`X-CLIENT-VERSION`, `X-PLATFORM`, `X-PLATFORM-VERSION`, `X-CORE-VERSION`,
`X-IS-MULTIROOT`) — pinned to Cline's current CLI release, which is also
what the free models' gate reads; when Cline ships a new release, move the
pinned numbers in `index.mjs` along. All models use one `X-Task-ID` per
named chat session, derived as a UUID from the session. With no named session
(including magpie's synthetic id from the first user message), no task id
is sent. The session crosses the plugin's hooks in a private header that is
removed before the request goes to Cline. Auth and account requests carry
the same identity. A finished non-streaming answer rides in a
`{"data": …}` envelope the official clients take apart; the plugin takes it
apart too. The model list is read from
`/api/v1/ai/cline/recommended-models` and `/api/v1/ai/cline/models` (neither
needs a sign-in); usage reads `/api/v1/users/me` and the account's `/balance`
(its balance is counted in millionths of a dollar), and ClinePass's 5-hour,
weekly and monthly limits from `/api/v1/users/me/plan/usage-limits`
(`{limits: [{type, percentUsed, resetsAt}]}`, what app.cline.bot's
subscription page shows). An account without ClinePass (a 404 there) has
none; limits that fail to read for any other reason say so on the card beside
the balance, and limits read are kept when the balance can't be.

### DeepSeek models only through DeepSeek's own API

Cline's gateway picks among the providers that serve a model. On ClinePass
its own routing for a model wins over `only` alone, so since 0.1.11 a request
for a ClinePass DeepSeek model (`cline-pass/deepseek-…`) carries, by default:

```json
"providerOptions": {"gateway": {"only": ["deepseek"], "has": ["vision", "implicit-caching"]}}
```

`has` is the gateway's capability filter: the upstream must cache a repeated
prefix by itself, and take images — `vision` is asked only of a model Cline's
catalog says takes images (or a request carrying one), never of the text-only
`deepseek-v4-pro`. With it the request is answered by DeepSeek's own API
(hy125245 on X: `finalProvider` `deepseek`, and a fake upstream in `only`
refused with "no matching upstream"). A pinned request that fails with no
upstream matching it, or with a 5xx, goes once more as sent, so the pin
never fails a request that would have worked; a refusal of the account (401,
402, 403, 429) is answered as it is. A request with `provider` or
`providerOptions` of its own — magpie's extra body, say — goes as sent. Set
`pinUpstream` to `false` to send ClinePass's DeepSeek models unpinned.

With the `pinUpstream` option on, a request for any DeepSeek model (not the
`cline-free/` ones) is pinned too, the ClinePass ones as above without the
way back, the others with `"providerOptions": {"gateway": {"only":
["deepseek"]}}`, so it is answered by DeepSeek's own API only, and one for a
GLM model (`cline-pass/glm-…`) carries `["zai"]`, so it is answered by Z.ai's
own API only — the same as magpie's built-in ClinePass tick. Cline sends
`glm-5.3-flash` through OpenRouter rather than Vercel's gateway, and OpenRouter
ignores `providerOptions`, so that model's request carries OpenRouter's own
`"provider": {"only": ["z-ai"]}` instead (since 0.1.10). Other models, and a
request with `provider` or `providerOptions` of its own, go as sent. It is off
by default. Turn it on:

- in magpie: the provider's editor › Upstream › tick "DeepSeek and GLM
  models only from their makers' own APIs";
- in OpenCode: `"provider": {"cline": {"options": {"pinUpstream": true}}}` in
  `opencode.json`, or the plugin's own options:
  `"plugin": [["@magpie-community/opencode-cline-auth", {"pinUpstream": true}]]`.

## Models

The list is Cline's own, merged from the two feeds its clients read: the
recommended-models feed (its recommended picks, its free models and
ClinePass's) and the whole cloud catalog (`/ai/cline/models`, where the
usage-billed models the recommended feed doesn't name live). Refreshed from
the live feeds whenever they answer; until then a bundled snapshot of the
recommended list, Cline's own default (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`) among it.
Cline's `clineCloud` group is left out, as Cline's own clients leave it out
unless they opt in.

Each model's context window is the cloud catalog's (`context_length`). Its
reply limit is left unsaid: the catalog's `max_completion_tokens` can be most
of the window, and an agent keeps that much free for the reply. The `cline-free/…`
and `cline-pass/…` models aren't in that catalog, so they say none, and magpie
takes the window models.dev gives the model after the prefix
(`cline-free/mimo-v2.6-flash` is `mimo-v2.6-flash`).

- The **free** group (`cline-free/…`, `stealth/…`) costs nothing — the names
  say "(free)". They are gated on the client surface a request claims; the
  plugin claims what it is, and the gate takes it. If Cline ever narrows that
  gate to its own apps, those models go away.
- The **ClinePass** group (`cline-pass/…`) needs a ClinePass subscription —
  the names say so, and asking without one answers 403.
- The rest are usage-billed against the account's Credits balance.

## Not included

- Cline's MCP and web-search endpoints — a chat provider only.
- Team/organization account switching.

# @magpie-community/opencode-cloudflare-workers-ai-auth

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md)

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm%20version-0.0.4-EA4335.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@magpie-community/opencode-cloudflare-workers-ai-auth)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-FBBC05.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

A provider plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) 1.x and
[magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) that signs in to **Cloudflare Workers AI** with your
API token and serves it as a provider every agent can use: 28+ models discovered
live from [models.dev](https://models.dev), paid-only models flagged,
and a daily Neurons allowance row in `magpie quota`.

> Not affiliated with or endorsed by Cloudflare.

## What you need

| Item | Where to find it |
|---|---|
| Cloudflare Account ID | 32 hex characters, on the dashboard's **Account home** → right sidebar |
| Cloudflare API token | Dashboard → avatar → **My Profile** → API Tokens → create a **Custom Token** with `Account → Workers AI → Edit` (add `Account Settings → Read` for the plan name and `Account Analytics → Read` for today's actually-used Neurons in `magpie quota`) |
| magpie | 0.1.1110 or later, or OpenCode 1.x |

No zones need to be selected on the token. Free and Paid plans both get
**10,000 Neurons/day** free; eight frontier models need Workers Paid or prepaid
AI Gateway credits (flagged below).

The quota card shows the daily free allowance as a count and a Used / Left
percentage, resetting at 00:00 UTC. Paid or unconfirmed plans keep this window
informational; only a confirmed Free plan stops routing when it is spent.

## Install in magpie

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-cloudflare-workers-ai-auth   # from npm
magpie plugin add /path/to/folder                                        # local copy
```

Then sign in:

```sh
magpie plugin login cloudflare-workers-ai
```

| Prompt | What to enter |
|---|---|
| API Token | the Workers AI:Edit token from the table above |
| Account ID (optional) | 32 hex characters; leave empty to use the plugin's `accountId` option |

- Each sign-in is one account. Sign in again to add another one (e.g. a Free
  account and a Paid account) — magpie fails over between them automatically;
  `magpie quota` shows each account's row separately.
- Sign in again with the same Account ID to replace that account, e.g. to rotate
  the token. Sign-ins are kept in magpie's account storage; nothing is written
  outside magpie's config.
- If Cloudflare refuses the token, magpie marks the account and asks you to sign
  in again.

## Commands you'll actually use

```sh
magpie providers                                                     # is the provider signed in?
magpie provider test cloudflare-workers-ai                           # one small request (~300 ms in our sandbox)
magpie provider test cloudflare-workers-ai @cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast
magpie quota                                                         # plan + Neurons/day window
magpie claude cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast   # run Claude Code on it
magpie codex cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b                     # or Codex, same idea
magpie plugin logout cloudflare-workers-ai                           # remove the sign-in
```

Models are named `cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/<org>/<model>` — the same IDs
[models.dev](https://models.dev) lists for the provider, refreshed hourly.

### In OpenCode 1.x

`opencode.json`:

```json
{ "plugin": ["@magpie-community/opencode-cloudflare-workers-ai-auth"] }
```

then `opencode auth login` → Cloudflare Workers AI (same two fields).

## Paid-only models

Eight models are gated by Cloudflare behind Workers Paid or prepaid AI Gateway
credits and are flagged **(Paid)** in the name — that is exactly how the
model picker renders it:

`@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6`,
`@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code`, `@cf/zai-org/glm-5.2`, `@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3`,
`@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash`, `@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731`,
`@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`,
`@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro-0813`

Everything else counts only against the shared 10,000 Neurons/day allowance
(billed on a Paid account past it), so no model carries a free badge by design.

## Options

```sh
magpie plugin options opencode-cloudflare-workers-ai-auth '{"accountId": "…", "discoveryTTLMs": 1800000}'
```

| Option | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `accountId` | — | default Account ID used when a sign-in leaves it empty |
| `apiKey` | — | default token (the sign-in's key wins) |
| `baseTemplate` | see below | template target that the Account ID is interpolated into |
| `discoveryTTLMs` | `3600000` | catalog refresh interval |

**`baseTemplate` default** (insertion target, Account ID interpolated per account):

```
https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}/ai/v1
```

## Troubleshooting

| You see | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Model list empty, provider missing | `magpie plugin add .` again, then `magpie plugin --json`: the `error` field says why (catalog fetch failed, or the token was refused) |
| `magpie: the sign-in failed: 需要 API Token` | the token prompt was left empty — re-run `magpie plugin login cloudflare-workers-ai` |
| 401 `Authentication error` from `provider test` | the token was refused: check scope (`Workers AI:Edit`) or sign in again |
| 403 from `provider test`  | token and Account ID don't match |
| 400 `No route for that URI` | if this survives a re-`plugin add`, it's a stale plugin version — the current proxy normalizes template URLs; file an issue |
| `Model … absent from the current catalog` | the model id isn't in models.dev's cloudflare-workers-ai section; pick a listed model |
| 400 on a (Paid) model | your plan is Free and the model needs Workers Paid or AI Gateway credits |
| Quota row shows the fallback plan text | the token lacks `Account Settings → Read`; the escalation is purely cosmetic — the Neurons window is still shown |
| Quota row shows 10,000 / 10,000 remaining but requests fail with `used up your daily free allocation` | the token lacks `Account Analytics → Read`, so the used amount is unknown and magpie renders the allowance as untouched — grant that scope and refresh |

## Development

```sh
node --check src/index.mjs       # parse guard (the upstream bug that started this fork)
node --test                     # 23 tests, no network needed
sh scripts/sandbox.sh login      # magpie 0.1.1326 in a throwaway HOME
sh scripts/sandbox.sh test       # provider test inside that sandbox
sh scripts/sandbox.sh json       # plugin --json inside that sandbox
```

`scripts/sandbox.sh` keeps its HOME in `.sandbox/` (git-ignored), so your real
magpie, agents and sign-ins are never touched.

## Plugin contract notes

- Single async plugin function; `config`, `auth.methods` (one `api` method with
  `password` prompts), `auth.loader`, `auth.usage` and `provider.models` hooks
- `loader(getAuth, provider)` reads the contract account shape (`auth.key`,
  `auth.metadata.accountId`); the legacy OpenCode multi-method shape works too
- `authorize` returns `{ type: "success", key, metadata }` / `{ type: "failed", error }`
- On catalog failure at load, `config()` degrades to an empty model list instead
  of throwing; the per-account `provider.models` serves the cached catalog after
- One file, zero runtime dependencies, ESM, `node >= 20`

## Version / license

| | |
|---|---|
| **Version** | 0.0.4 |
| **License** | [MIT](LICENSE) — Copyright (c) 2026 Guislabert |
| **Runtime** | Node.js >= 20, ESM only |
| **Author** | [@Guislabert](https://github.com/Guislabert) |
| **中文** | [README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md) |

MIT © [Guislabert](https://github.com/Guislabert)

@magpie-community/opencode-codearts-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-codearts-auth

Signs in to **Huawei Cloud** and serves two providers in OpenCode and magpie:

- **CodeArts** (华为云码道, the CodeArts Agent coding plans: Trial, personal and enterprise
  credit plans) — provider id `codearts`: GLM, DeepSeek, openPangu and more.
- **OfficeAce** (华为云 AgentArts / MaaS) — provider id `officeace`: GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi
  and 盘古 models, its credit buckets and its daily check-in.

Each card signs in on its own: the two providers hold separate records with separate Huawei Cloud
refresh tokens, because an STS refresh token is spent once — two records sharing one would sign
each other out. The same Huawei Cloud IAM account works for both, and a credential issued for one
endpoint also signs the other vendor's API (measured, see below), so signing in twice costs two
clicks and nothing else. OfficeAce was its own package (`officeace-auth`) until 0.3.0; accounts
signed in there are read from where magpie already keeps them and keep working — no second
sign-in for those.

> **Unofficial.** This package is not affiliated with, authorized or endorsed by Huawei,
> Huawei Cloud or CodeArts; their names and marks belong to their owners. It talks to the
> non-public APIs the CodeArts client uses and identifies itself the way that client does
> (including claiming the daily free benefit and check-in), which may not be allowed by Huawei
> Cloud's terms of service, and those APIs may change at any time. Use it at your own risk,
> including the risk of restrictions on your account.

## Install

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-codearts-auth
magpie plugin login codearts      # CodeArts; the OfficeAce card signs in separately
```

or install it from magpie's Plugins tab and sign in there. **Coming from `officeace-auth`?**
Nothing to do: the account is stored under the same provider id (`officeace`) and in the same
credential shape, so it is read as it is. Remove the old package first (both cannot serve one
provider id: magpie asks which one if they are both installed).

## Sign-in

**Sign in with Huawei Cloud** opens Huawei Cloud's consent page. The plugin listens on a
loopback port (`127.0.0.1`, ≥ 10000) for the redirect and exchanges the code at Huawei Cloud
STS — a PKCE flow whose token requests carry an ES256 DPoP proof, as the CodeArts client does.
STS answers with temporary AK/SK/security-token credentials and a refresh token. The callback
server takes one GET to `/oauth/callback`, exactly; one that comes back without a code (the
portal's error) fails the sign-in at once.

**Where it is kept:** the whole credential (AK/SK/security token, expiry, refresh token, the
PKCE verifier and the DPoP private key) is a JSON string in the account's `access` field, in
magpie's (or OpenCode's) own account store. `auth.refresh` renews it 30 minutes before it
expires, reusing the same verifier and DPoP key; a stale credential met on a request
(`401`, `APIG.0602`) is renewed once and the request sent again. A refresh token is spent once
per account, however many loaders ask; a renewal that only fails for now (STS unreachable)
answers `503` and keeps the sign-in, and only one STS turns away for good marks it.

**The card's name:** the account is shown by its **phone number** (`138****8000`, masked the way
the other magpie cards mask theirs), read once after signing in from Huawei Cloud IAM —
`GET https://iam.cn-north-4.myhuaweicloud.com/v3.0/OS-USER/users/{principal_id}`, signed with
the same temporary credentials — and kept on the credential as `user_phone`. The refresh token
names the signer only by IAM's own ids (`hw12323`, and the URN
`iam::<domain>:user:<name>`), which read as an ID nobody can tell apart from another account's;
the account name is the fallback when the phone can't be read, and the URN never is.

`accountId` is the account's identity — the URN, as before — and it never changes: magpie
keys the user's own name for the account, its proxy, model picks and a gateway key's list by
it, so a re-sign-in and a renewal give the same value back. The card's name is usage's `user`,
which shows `user_phone` once a sign-in or renewal has read it. IAM is *not* one of the hosts the plugin signs forwarded requests for
(`SIGNED_HOSTS`): the one phone read is made by the plugin itself, for that one URL.

## Models

The account's live list: CodeArts' builtin models, plus the free models of its daily benefit
once today's benefit has been claimed (`POST /api/v1/benefit/claim`, once a Beijing day, as the
client does; a `benefit not found` on a day not yet claimed claims it too). Each model's credit
rate (the client's 「消耗系数」) is reported as magpie's `rate`,
with its reasoning flag and limits, from the account's main agent (`build`) model list. Before
signing in, a short built-in catalog stands in.

## Requests

- Every request is signed with Huawei's SDK-HMAC-SHA256 using the temporary credentials, and
  only for CodeArts' own two hosts, `snap-access.cn-north-4.myhuaweicloud.com` and
  `opengw.developer.huaweicloud.com`: a request anywhere else (an overridden `api`) is refused
  before the credentials leave, and no signed or token request follows a redirect.
- The gateway allows 3 concurrent sessions per account and tells them apart by
  `x-ot-session-id`; the plugin sends one stable session id per account (and a fresh trace per
  request) like the client, keeps at most 3 chats in flight per account, retries
  `TM.00001041` with backoff, and waits in the gateway's own queue (`429` +
  `queue-status: queued`) the way the client does. Only then does magpie get a `429`. Since
  0.2.3, when magpie has another candidate after this request (`x-magpie-fallback: 1`), a queued
  request leaves the queue at once and answers `503` with the queue's `Retry-After`
  ("CodeArts queued the request; try again in 20s"), and magpie asks the next.
- Chats always go upstream as streams — CodeArts meters only streamed answers — and are folded
  back into one `chat.completion` when the caller asked for JSON.
- `thinking: { type: "enabled" }` is sent unless the caller set it, so the reasoning lands in
  `reasoning_content` and `content` is only the reply.
- Errors the gateway puts inside a `200` stream (spent quota, unknown model) come back as
  `429` / `400` / `502` with the vendor's words. The `codearts/` prefix is stripped and output
  budgets are clamped to 65536.
- CodeArts takes tool names of up to 64 characters. A longer one (an MCP tool such as
  `mcp__plugin_android-emulator_android-emulator__android_discover_project`) goes as its first
  55 characters, `_` and 8 hex of its SHA-256, and the tool calls in the answer, streamed or
  not, carry the agent's own name again.
- Every model is listed as text only (`modalities.input: ["text"]`, `image: false`): CodeArts
  answers an image with `InferHub.001001020.406` "The request model is not multimodal". Since
  0.2.4 magpie is told so, and describes an image for the model or leaves it out. That refusal,
  inside a `200` or with any status, comes back as a `400`, not a `502` an agent would ask again.

## Usage and check-in

- Usage: the credit buckets of `snap-manager/v1/statistics/plugin` (only the package total
  pauses the account; the basic / on-demand / bonus buckets are shown aside) and the free daily
  token pool.
- When each credit batch expires is read from the CodeArts console's own calls
  (`snap-manager/v1/package/credit/page`, `v1/ops/credit/*`); when those can't be read, the
  plugin falls back to a small ledger of the check-ins it claimed,
  `~/.config/magpie/codearts-checkins.json` (or `MAGPIE_CODEARTS_LEDGER`). This part is still
  being checked against more accounts — trust the CodeArts console where they differ.
- `auth.checkin`: the client's 「限时福利 → 每日领取」 — `GET /v1/ops/delivery?channel=IDE`,
  `POST /v1/ops/claim`, then `POST /v1/ops/confirm` when the claim answers an id. A claim whose
  confirm failed is kept in that ledger for the day and confirmed at the next check-in; one the
  client leaves unconfirmed (`id: null`) never is. Turn on
  *Auto check-in* for CodeArts under **Settings → Usage → Plugins**.

## OfficeAce (the second provider)

**Signing in.** The officeace card offers the same 「Sign in with Huawei Cloud」 as the CodeArts
card, and it is the same account system: a CodeArts STS triple signs OfficeAce's subscription API
(V11-HMAC) and passes its CLAW permission check, and an OfficeAce triple signs CodeArts'
`snap-access` calls. But the two cards keep **separate records with separate refresh tokens** —
a sign-in writes only the card it was made on. A Huawei Cloud refresh token is spent once, so two
records holding one token would each sign the other out at its next renewal; one record per
sign-in is what keeps a CodeArts-only user from being asked to sign in again because of the
OfficeAce card. Sign in on the OfficeAce card to get an OfficeAce account.
A sign-in is the only thing that creates an OfficeAce account: a listing never adopts one from
another provider's record, so an account the user signed out of cannot come back by itself.

**From `officeace-auth`.** That package's records are read unchanged: the account is under the
same provider id and its `access` field holds the same JSON (`modelAppKey`, `securityToken`,
`dpopPrivateJwk`, `refreshToken` …). Its refresh token is still spent at the OAuth client it was
issued to (`pdp5_for_agentarts`), so those accounts keep renewing too.

**What a record is named, and what a renewal may touch.** `accountId` is the vendor's own stable
id — the IAM domain id, as the record `officeace-auth` wrote carried — and never the masked
phone: magpie hangs a user's own name for the account, its proxy and a gateway key off
`accountId`, so the phone belongs only in `usage().user` (#483, magpie#4416). A renewal never
renames an account: the stored `accountId` and `uid` stand exactly as written — the domain id, or
the phone `officeace-auth` 0.1.14 and later stored — and a value computed from the credential is
only filled in when the record has none. A new sign-in names its account by the domain id.

**A record is renewed only with its own refresh token.** The unit of coordination is the refresh
chain: the OAuth client a token was issued to plus the token's lineage (a rotation keeps its
parent's, so a record still holding the spent token is known to be on the same chain). Each card's
record holds its own refresh token, from its own sign-in, so it is a chain of its own and spends
its own token however many hooks ask.
An `officeace-auth` record beside a CodeArts record holds a token from another issuer
(`pdp5_for_agentarts` against `codearts-agent`), so it is another chain: it spends its own token,
keeps its own MaaS pair, and a renewal that fails fails — it is never handed another record's
credential. No record's renewal writes another one: a renewal writes only the record it was asked
to renew. That is deliberate — writing the new credential into the other record is exactly what
used to bring a removed account back.

**Models.** OfficeAce's catalog (`GET {maas}/v2/models`) is a registry, not a promise: 26 entries,
most of which answer `404 ModelArts.81009 Invalid model` at chat. The plugin cuts it down to the
billable list (`GET {subscription}/v1/model-token-rates`, 9 entries) and never lists three ids
measured to always 404. A rates read that fails keeps the last good table — an empty one would
put the un-callable ids back in front of the user. Before a sign-in a built-in table of 10 stands
in. Names carry the account's multiplier (`GLM-5.3 · x0.18`), and the vendor's trailing newline in
`model_name` is trimmed.

**Requests.** MaaS wants `Authorization: Basic base64(appKey:appSecret)`; the plugin rewrites the
SDK's Bearer header, strips the `officeace/` model prefix, and sends the request to the MaaS base
the account's own credential names (official direct when it names none). A `401` (or a `4xx`
naming the Basic pair) renews the credential once and sends it again — but only when the renewal
changed the pair; the same pair would get the same refusal. An account that signed in without
opening MaaS gets a `400` saying so, not an empty Basic header sent upstream.

**Usage and check-in.** `GET {subscription}/v1/subscription`: plan buckets (`skus[].quotas`) and
activity bonuses (`bonus_skus`) become magpie windows; a `.trial` bucket carries no expiry and
gets none invented; an expired bucket is folded away (`aside`) and takes no part in routing. The
check-in is `POST {subscription}/v1/subscription/bonus/claim` once a Beijing day: a 2xx with no
`bonus_skus` is 「今日已无新增可领」 (`done`), not a failure. Turn on *Auto check-in* for OfficeAce
under **Settings → Usage → Plugins**.

**Known limits.**

- STS spends a refresh token once. Each card of this package signs in on its own and holds its own
  record and its own refresh token, so the two cards never affect each other. **A renewal writes
  only the record being renewed**, which is also why a record the user removed can never come
  back: no other record is written, whether it was listed, used, or not seen at all, and across a
  restart too. An old `officeace-auth` record likewise renews only along its own chain. Two
  separate magpie processes renewing the same account at the same moment still race; the loser
  asks again and is signed out only if the token stays spent.
- `officeace-auth` and this package cannot both serve the `officeace` provider id. Magpie asks
  which plugin serves it; remove the old one.

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `maxInflight` | `3` | chats in flight per account; it can only lower the vendor's cap of 3 sessions |
| `retryBudgetMs` | `150000` | how long to retry `TM.00001041` before answering `429` |
| `retryDelays` | `[2000,4000,6000,8000,10000]` | retry waits in ms (the last repeats) |
| `queueBudgetMs` | `300000` | how long to wait in the gateway's queue |
| `thinking` | `true` | `false` stops adding `thinking: { type: "enabled" }` |
