@magpie-community/opencode-joycode-auth.readme:
# JoyCode

把京东云 **JoyCode**（JoyCoder IDE 自带的模型额度）作为一个多协议供应商接进 [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai)。装好后，所有 agent（Claude Code、Codex 等）都能通过 magpie 用 `joycode/<model>` 访问 JoyCode 的模型，并享受 magpie 的多账号号池、故障切换和用量统计。

逆向了 JoyCode IDE 的「彩网关」协议（`https://api-ai.jd.com/api`，HMAC-SHA256 签名 query + `ptKey` 账号票据头）。请求与 IDE 本身走同一账号、同一额度。

## 安装

```bash
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-joycode-auth
```

```bash
magpie plugin login joycode
```

两种登录方式（任选）：

1. **浏览器登录（京东账号）**（推荐）— magpie 打开 JoyCode 官方登录页，用京东账号/扫码登录，完成后自动拿到凭证。和 JoyCode IDE 自己的登录走的是同一套流程。
2. **手动粘贴 ptKey** — 从已登录的 JoyCode IDE 登录态里提取（`%APPDATA%\JoyCode\User\globalStorage\state.vscdb` 的 `JoyCoder.IDE` → `joyCoderUser.ptKey`）。这是**账号票据**，等同密码，勿外传。这种方式还会追问可选的 tenant（企业租户名，个人账号留空）。

凭证由 magpie 存在自己的 `plugin-auth.json`（权限 600），本插件目录里不落任何凭证。

多账号 = 多次登录：`magpie plugin login joycode` 再跑一遍（或在应用里再点一次），每个账号是一个号池座位，magpie 会自动轮换。

## 模型

模型由登录账号的 `joycode_modelList` 动态同步，不需要在插件里逐个维护。插件读取每个模型的 `extJson.adapterType`，为它选择对应的协议、AI SDK 和 JoyCode 网关：

| `extJson.adapterType` | 上游协议 | AI SDK | JoyCode `functionId` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 缺失 / 其他 | OpenAI Chat Completions | `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` | `chat_completions` |
| `openai-response` | OpenAI Responses | `@ai-sdk/openai` | `responses_completions` |
| `anthropic` | Anthropic Messages | `@ai-sdk/anthropic` | `anthropic_completions` |

因此 GPT 模型会走 Responses，Claude 模型会走 Anthropic Messages，GLM、Kimi、DeepSeek、MiniMax、Doubao 等继续走 Chat Completions。2026-10-28 使用真实账号核对时，`joycode_modelList` 返回 15 个模型：10 个 chat、4 个 `openai-response`、1 个 `anthropic`，三类均已覆盖。

同时通过 `plugin_config` 的 `billingRate` 场景同步积分消耗倍率。点击「重新获取模型」可更新模型和倍率；按 `chatApiModel` 匹配，不会把仅出现在计费表中的模型加入列表。模型自身的倍率优先；公共倍率配置遵守 `excludeTenants`，无租户或被排除的租户不套用公共倍率。明确的 0× 会标记免费；查不到的倍率不当作 0×，也不虚构优惠前倍率。

当前实测：JoyAI-Code-1.6 0×、GLM-5.3 0.6×、Kimi-K2.6 0.5×、MiniMax-M3 0.4×、Doubao-Seed-2.0-pro 0.4×。这些是查询结果，代码没有写死价格。它们是积分倍率，不是美元/token 价格。

**视觉（image_url）为实验性**：按接口 `features` 声明能力，实际图片请求尚未验收。

## 消息转发策略

根据 2026-10-30 的 JoyCode 实测，仅对 Responses 协议做以下兼容：GPT-6 Astra、GPT-6.1 Sol 的显式 `none` / `minimal` 转为 `low`；GPT-6 Sol、GPT-5.6 Sol 仅将 `minimal` 转为 `low`，保留上游接受的 `none`。其他 reasoning 参数、有效或未指定的强度、未知模型和其他协议均不变。启用低档推理可能增加用量。此表基于当前账号目录，不自动覆盖未来新增模型。

默认保留完整多轮对话、工具调用和模型原生请求格式。插件从当前账号的 `joycode_userInfo` 获取真实 `userId`、`tenant`、`orgFullName`，按 JoyCode 请求格式补入正文；三种协议统一设置 `language: UNKNOWN`。身份信息按账号 loader 隔离缓存，不接受客户端指定的用户身份。缺少这些元数据时，已观察到网关返回 `AI_GRAY_ACCESS_DENIED`。

网关可能以 HTTP 200 和 SSE 响应头返回裸 JSON 错误；插件会把这种错误转换为明确的失败响应，避免客户端一直等待。普通 403 权限错误不会再被误标为登录失效。

JoyCode 的 Anthropic 与 Responses 网关还会给 SSE 多加一层 framing（Anthropic 为 `data: event: …` 和 `data: data: …`，Responses 为 `data: data: …`）。插件在流式转发时增量还原标准 SSE，不缓存完整回复；否则官方 Anthropic/OpenAI SDK 会分别表现为空流和 `malformed server-sent event JSON`。标准 SSE 会按原字节透传，跨上游 chunk 的边界也有回归测试。

Codex 在 `store: false` 下仍可能重放带 `rs_…` id 的 reasoning item。JoyCode 的 Responses 后端会把这些 id 当成已持久化条目查找，找不到便以 `Item with id 'rs_…' not found` 拒绝整个请求，压缩尤其容易触发。插件在转发前移除这类 reasoning item 的 `id`，保留其 `summary` 和 `encrypted_content`；`store: true` 时保留 id，其他 item 的 id 也不改。

0.1.1 已实测 JoyAI-Code-1.6 完整流式文字回复、工具调用及工具结果往返，并通过 magpie `provider test`。0.2.0 于 2026-10-28 通过真实账号验证：`provider test` 的 `GPT-6 Astra` Responses 请求返回 200（3.0 秒），`Claude-Opus-5-hq` Anthropic Messages 请求返回 200（7.3 秒）；再经 magpie 网关用官方 OpenAI SDK 的 Responses 流和官方 Anthropic SDK 的 Messages 流各发一条短请求，均正确收到文本 `OK` 和完整事件序列（2.9 秒、7.6 秒）。更早的 Claude 冷启动曾出现 34.7 秒，分段计时显示时间耗在上游响应头而不是插件缓冲。Anthropic 的 `/v1/messages/count_tokens` 在插件本地返回 404，不访问 JoyCode，避免把 token 计数误发成一次付费生成。

如果实测 JoyCode 后端拒绝多轮/工具调用格式的消息，可以开启回退模式：

```bash
magpie plugin options joycode '{"flatten": true}'
```

flatten 模式会把 Chat Completions 消息压平成 `system + 单条 user prompt`（工具调用和工具结果会被丢弃），Responses 和 Anthropic Messages 不受影响。**开了 flatten 就别用 chat 模型跑需要工具的 agent 会话**，只适合纯对话。默认关闭。

## 已知限制

- **额度展示**：通过 IDE 同款 `get_newpoint_ide` 接口读取套餐、已用/总积分、剩余积分和有效期文字，可在账号及用量页面刷新。有效期文字不等同于额度重置时间，因此不推算重置倒计时。多个积分池分别显示，不相加；额度窗口仅作展示，由上游判定具体模型能否继续使用。
- **ptKey 失效**：表现为账号被标记「需要重新登录」，重新 `magpie plugin login joycode` 即可。
- **签名 key 轮换**：签名 key 是内嵌在每份 JoyCode IDE 里的公开协议常量，不是密钥。若 JoyCode 轮换它，从新版 `extension.js` 重新提取后，可通过环境变量 `JOYCODE_SIGN_KEY` 覆盖，无需改代码。
- 登录方式默认 `loginType: PIN_JD_CLOUD`；如果你的账号是京东云企业域登录且请求被拒，改 `index.mjs` 顶部的 `LOGIN_TYPE` 常量。

## 开发

```bash
bun test                # 浏览器登录、额度映射、模型倍率回归测试
```

相关文档：[magpie 插件开发](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/zh/plugins)。版本变更见 [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)。

这是非官方适配插件，与京东或 magpie 官方无隶属关系。JoyCode 图标及商标归其权利人所有；代码的 MIT 许可不授予这些品牌资产的权利。

@magpie-community/opencode-kimi-work-aut.readme:
# Kimi Work

Use the ordinary **Kimi desktop Work subscription** as a provider in Magpie or OpenCode. This is separate from Kimi Code's subscription/API and from the Kimi agent package, which sends Kimi's inference in the opposite direction to Magpie.

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-kimi-work-auth
magpie plugin login kimi-work
```

Open Kimi desktop and sign in to Work on the same computer first. Choose **使用本机 Kimi Work 登录** in the provider's sign-in menu. If the desktop provides a membership access/refresh pair, explicit sign-in imports it into the host's auth store and Magpie renews it directly with Kimi near expiry, including while the browser and desktop app are closed. Older desktops without a refresh token still sign in as reference-only accounts and read membership access from the desktop file. This package does not capture browser cookies or offer an API-key fallback.

Version **0.1.15** adds membership renewal and a single shared monthly meter to upstream 0.1.14. It retains the storage-pointer and sign-in diagnostics fixes (#425/#444), distinct account IDs and per-user Work keys (#440), and spent-quota 403→429 handling (#465), alongside the earlier menu/header fixes. **Existing reference-only accounts through 0.1.14 continue to read quota without reconnecting.** They do not silently migrate or spend the desktop refresh token. Explicitly reconnect only to opt into host-managed renewal when a desktop refresh token is available. Accounts already saved with a pair keep their format.

Request-body buffering for schema conversion also follows the caller's abort signal: cancelling while a stream is still being read cancels that read and returns the original cancellation reason before any upstream request is sent.

## Models and requests

The account's models and reasoning options come from the two lists Kimi's desktop reads: Work's model menu, `kimi.gateway.config.v1.ConfigService/DescribeKimiWorkConfig` on `www.kimi.com` (asked with the desktop's web sign-in), and `https://agent-gw.kimi.com/coding/v1/models`. The menu lists the models a membership tier adds (K3.1 Pro on the 99 plan) that `/models` leaves out; since 0.1.7 both are listed, the menu's names first, and either one failing leaves the other. Since 0.1.9 the menu is asked with the headers the desktop sends it (`x-msh-platform` `mac` or `windows`, `x-msh-version`, `R-Timezone`): asked without them, Kimi answers with the web menu, which has no K3.1 Pro (`k3d1-agent`). Since 0.1.10, when the menu can't be had with the web sign-in (Kimi's file holds a web sign-in www.kimi.com no longer takes, answered 401, or another failure or an empty reply), it is asked again without one, as the desktop asks it before signing in, which gives the same desktop menu; each failure is written to Magpie's log, without the token. Chat completions, streaming, tool calls and cancellation use the same Work gateway, with the headers Kimi's own Work client sends it (0.1.8). It never uses `api.kimi.com` or a Kimi Code API key.

Version 0.1.4 preserves the calling agent's shared instructions, prompts, history and tools unchanged. Since 0.1.5 one exception: tool schemas Kimi's "moonshot flavored json schema" check refuses are rewritten to an equivalent it takes (#287). A `$ref` beside a `type`, as zod writes a schema derived from a reused one, gets its target written in; a `type` beside an `anyOf` is left out; an untyped `enum`, `const` or `$ref` target gets the type its values or keywords say. A request with none of these goes byte for byte. Instructions, MCP and skills are assigned to that agent in Magpie's Library; the provider does not create a second target or enable resources on its own. The ordinary Kimi agent's Library support starts at `@magpie-community/agent-kimi-desktop` 0.1.1.

An inference HTTP 401 marks the provider sign-in as expired (`kimi_work_login_expired`). Sign in to desktop Work if needed, then **reconnect Kimi Work in Magpie** (or run `magpie plugin login kimi-work`); signing in to the desktop alone does not reconnect the provider. A 403 whose body says the allowance is spent (Kimi's "You've reached your usage limit for this billing cycle", `resource_exhausted` "insufficient balance") goes to Magpie as a 429 with Kimi's body and headers, so Magpie rests that account until its allowance is back and asks another one (#465); any other 403 passes through as a 403. Other HTTP errors, including 429 and 5xx, pass through unchanged with Kimi's status, headers, body and Retry-After. This preserves the distinction between concurrency limits and exhausted allowance, including any upstream reset details. Network failures use `kimi_work_connection_failed` and retain the underlying cause code or fetch error message for diagnosis. Rate limits and service failures do not invalidate the desktop sign-in. Cancellation stays cancellation. No automatic retry sends a conversation twice or falls back to Code.

Models use standard context, capped at 262,144 tokens, rather than silently enabling the higher-priced XL context. The reply limit is the menu's `maxTokens` (32,768 for every model it lists today). Until the signed-in account's live catalog is read, and when it can't be, the models offered are `kimi-work/k3-agent` and `kimi-work/k2d8-preview`, the two ids Work's `/models` has listed; the live catalog replaces them, so a model Kimi adds to the account (such as K3.1 Pro) shows under the id the menu gives it. Since 0.1.6 a model whose reasoning levels come in a shape not seen before keeps the levels that can be read, rather than the whole catalog failing over to the fallback.

Usage comes from Kimi's membership `GetSubscriptionStats` endpoint. The card's **月度共享额度** heading and single **本月** meter report `subscriptionBalance.amountUsedRatio`, the fraction used of the shared monthly membership pool. If returned, `subscriptionBalance.kimiCodeUsedRatio` appears only as **Code 已用 …%（占总额）** in the meter's text and tooltip: Code's share of the entire monthly pool, not another allowance or the fraction of the used portion. It is never another window/ring, because Magpie renders even informational `aside` windows as separate remaining allowances. Code's share does not constrain Work routing. Missing monthly data stays unknown; Code's five-hour/weekly limits are never substituted. No reset time is reported: `subscriptionBalance.expireTime` and `upcomingExpiration.timestamp` are expiration fields, and have not been verified to describe allowance resets. Magpie's compact card currently labels a window with no reset time as "Not used yet" even when usage is nonzero; that host wording does not mean the monthly pool is unused. An observed Windows request was classified by Kimi as `FEATURE_WORK` while the Code five-hour and weekly ratios stayed unchanged. Kimi controls billing, shared allowances, access and rate limits.

Every reasoning-effort value returned by `/models` is retained, including `STANDARD` if listed. The checked Windows catalog in `tests/fixtures/work-models.redacted.json` lists `LOW` (displayed by Kimi as **Standard**), `HIGH` and `MAX`; the plugin sends the advertised effort value instead of guessing from the display label.

## Sign-in and local files

The plugin reads Kimi's `daimon/config.json`, `daimon/kimi-code-key.json` and optional `daimon/runtime/kimi-code/home/device_id` in its `daimon-share` folder. That folder is where Kimi's own `daimon-storage.json` points (`shareDir`), or, without a valid pointer, `daimon-share` inside Kimi's data folder:

- Windows: `%APPDATA%/kimi-desktop/`
- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/kimi-desktop/`
- Linux: `~/.config/kimi-desktop/`

Kimi 3.2.21 on Windows, installed on another drive than `%APPDATA%`'s, keeps it there (`D:\KimiData\daimon-share` for an install on D:), and Kimi writes the same pointer on any system when its storage is moved. When the sign-in can't be found, the error names the file it looked for. Since 0.1.13, when the `daimon-share` folder itself is gone (moved, deleted, or on a drive that isn't mounted), the error names that folder instead (`kimi_work_share_missing`) and does not mark the account signed out: the sign-in in it isn't known to have lapsed. Putting the folder back makes the account work again at once, with no new sign-in. Kimi makes the folder again only when it starts, so signing in again in a running Kimi doesn't bring it back; quit and reopen Kimi, then sign in to Work.

The internal Work credential is named `credentials.kimiCode`, but its origin must be exactly `https://agent-gw.kimi.com/coding/v1`. Work credentials stay in Kimi's files and are reread for inference/model discovery. `credentials.kimiWeb.accessToken`, optional `refreshToken` and `userId` supply membership access. Only explicit sign-in can copy a complete membership pair to the host. The plugin never writes Kimi's configuration or creates a separate credential file.

Reference-only accounts continue to read the desktop webToken on each quota request, after checking the saved account reference. They never consume a desktop refresh token or write auth state. A legacy membership 401 tells the user to open Kimi desktop to refresh membership access and keeps the Work sign-in. Paired accounts use their own saved access without reading desktop membership state; a membership 401 shows a reconnect hint while leaving Work usable. HTTP failures, timeouts and missing membership balances are reported on the quota card, rather than being treated as a revoked Work key.

### Several Kimi accounts

Since 0.1.13 each Kimi user signed in here has a distinct account ID (`Kimi Work · ` plus the first six characters of its hashed uid). To add another account, switch Kimi desktop to that user, open Work once and sign in to this provider again. Inference retains upstream's per-user key lookup in `daimon/kimi-code-key.json` (`{"v":2,"keys":[{userId,apiKey,keyId?}]}`): the current user takes `config.json`'s key; another takes its own retained key. A missing or refused retained key prompts switching to that user in Kimi, and a missing share folder is reported without marking it signed out. A reference-only away account cannot read another user's membership quota; it shows the switch-account hint while chat stays usable. An account with an imported membership pair reads its own saved membership quota even after Kimi switches users. Old `Kimi Work (local)` entries remain usable; this upgrade does not rename or delete them. Future sign-ins use the distinct hashed account label.

## Membership renewal and storage

When explicitly imported, the membership pair is saved by Magpie in its account-scoped `plugin-auth.json`, using flushed atomic writes and mode `0600`; OpenCode owns its own auth store. This is a private credential file, not an encrypted vault. No separate token file or desktop credential backup is created. Host-managed renewal is optional for reference-only accounts; a desktop without refresh continues to work in reference mode.

Magpie calls `auth.refresh` before models, usage and requests when access is within one minute of its JWT expiry. The hook returns rotated access/refresh fields. **Magpie owns the commit:** under its auth-store lock it checks that the original pair still stands before saving, so a late renewal cannot restore logout or overwrite a replacement login. The plugin never calls `client.auth.set` from renewal or usage. Pending work and cached rotations use exact credentials, keeping independent same-user reconnects separate. A failed host save can retry the rotated pair in the same plugin process; restarting before it is saved may require reconnecting. A rejected membership refresh gives a reconnect hint and keeps the Work sign-in; it throws a membership-only failure so the host retains retry backoff without marking the provider account expired. Network/429/5xx failures retain the stored login.

RefreshToken uses its own observed desktop User-Agent/platform/version/timezone/language headers, with Connect JSON and no Authorization or Cookie. Browser device/session identifiers and ShieldData are not copied. Work requests keep upstream's Kimi Code 0.36.0/daimon 0.6.10 headers; www.kimi.com keeps upstream's desktop-menu metadata. The [compatibility record](COMPATIBILITY.md) compares the requests and preserves the dated 2026-10-24 single-cycle coexistence evidence; this revision does not claim a second real coexistence cycle.

Usage never rotates, writes or silently imports credentials, for either account format. `auth.refresh` and `auth.usage` are Magpie hooks ignored by OpenCode. Inference still depends on a valid per-account local Work key; membership renewal cannot replace a revoked Work key. Server expiry/revocation can require human sign-in, and automatic renewal does not guarantee a permanent session.

## Origin and provider-id conflict

This submission packages the local desktop-sign-in implementation from [`kupakupar/kimi-work-provider`](https://github.com/kupakupar/kimi-work-provider), whose Git-installed package was version 0.1.2. The community package now starts at 0.1.3. The previously stated preservation of model IDs/account references referred only to that implementation: both use `source: "kimi-work-desktop"` and a hashed account reference.

The separate MIT-licensed [`kimi-work-opencode`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/kimi-work-opencode) by Jared Boynton also uses provider ID `kimi-work`. It is not the source or a dependency of this package, and no migration from its authentication format is implemented. **Do not enable both packages together:** they claim the same provider/auth hooks, so load order can replace model/configuration or sign-in handling. Back up your configuration, keep only the desired plugin enabled, and reconnect it using its own sign-in method. This package does not automatically delete or convert the other package's settings or login data.

## Compatibility and validation

These are undocumented desktop interfaces, not a supported public Kimi API. Windows and Apple-silicon macOS have historical real Work inference coverage, including streaming. The [compatibility record](COMPATIBILITY.md) includes the tested Kimi build, renewal request comparison, observed coexistence interval and test limits; current renewal checks and historical inference coverage are distinguished there. Linux and Intel macOS remain unverified. Changed desktop layouts stop with a sign-in error; changed upstream schemas stop model discovery or usage with an error. Inference failures are returned without retrying against Code or another service. Users remain responsible for their subscription's terms.

```sh
bun test packages/kimi-work
bun scripts/check.mjs kimi-work
```

Tests use synthetic sessions and fake HTTP responses: credential separation/rotation, read-only compatibility for reference-only accounts, concurrent renewal by credential lineage, host-save retry recovery, process restart, rejected/transient refreshes, read-only local import/usage, account changes, endpoint restrictions, streaming/tool preservation, model discovery and monthly shared-usage accounting. No account, token, prompt, conversation or vendor binary is distributed. No runtime dependencies.

@magpie-community/opencode-kiro-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-kiro-auth

Signs in to a [Kiro](https://kiro.dev) subscription (Free, Pro, Pro+,
Power) and makes its requests, in OpenCode and in magpie. Provider id:
`kiro`.

## Signing in

Choose a sign-in method before opening the browser:

- **AWS Builder ID** opens AWS directly for a personal account.
- **IAM Identity Center (organization Start URL)** asks for the organization's
  HTTPS Start URL and AWS region (blank defaults to `us-east-1`), then opens
  that organization's AWS sign-in directly. Use the region of the directory.
- **Kiro sign-in page** retains the portal for Google, GitHub and other Kiro
  sign-in methods. Callers without prompt inputs retain this behavior.

The two direct AWS options skip the portal's first loopback callback. When
Magpie runs remotely or in Docker, sign in and authorize, then paste the
complete final `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/oauth/callback?...` address into Magpie's
Callback URL field. The page need not load on the browser's computer. Local
browsers that can reach the plugin's listener finish automatically. Direct
AWS sign-in still uses authorization code + PKCE, not device authorization.


- **Kiro (Google, GitHub, AWS Builder ID, IAM Identity Center)**: the Kiro
  IDE's own sign-in.
  - Kiro's page (`app.kiro.dev/signin`) sends the browser back to one of
    the ports the IDE listens on (3128, 4649, 6588, 8008, 9091, 49153,
    50153–53153) on `127.0.0.1`. While the IDE is signing in, those ports
    may be busy.
  - Google and GitHub come back with a code. Kiro's auth service trades it
    for tokens.
  - Builder ID and Identity Center come back with an AWS sign-in URL and
    region. The plugin registers a client with AWS's OIDC service, sends
    the browser to AWS, and trades the code AWS returns.
  - The account is named by the email Kiro has for it (`Get-Usage-Limits`)
    and the way it was signed in to: `email (Google)`, `email (GitHub)`,
    `email (Builder ID)`, `email (IAM Identity Center)`, `email
    (Internal)`. Its plan is read from the same call, and its usage names
    it the same way.
  - Kiro keeps a Google, a GitHub, a Builder ID and an Identity Center
    sign-in of one email as different accounts. The sign-in carries a `uid`
    (`google`, `github`, `builderid`, `enterprise`), so magpie keeps each one
    beside the others, and a sign-in again the same way replaces only its
    own account. An account signed in before 0.1.13 is given its `uid`,
    and one named by its bare email before 0.1.14 its name, on its first
    request, model listing, usage read or renewal. Until then, a sign-in
    again the same way goes beside it rather than replacing it: magpie
    matches a sign-in by its name, and the plugin can't see the other
    accounts to match it by `uid`.
  - A company's own identity provider (`external_idp`) is not supported
    here. Sign in with `kiro-cli login` and use the next method instead.
- **Kiro CLI's or Kiro IDE's sign-in**: uses the account kiro-cli is signed
  in to, or else the Kiro IDE's. Nothing is copied. It is read each time
  from where they keep it:
  - kiro-cli: its SQLite database's `auth_kv` table.
    - macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3`
    - Linux: `~/.local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3`
    - Windows: `%APPDATA%\kiro-cli\data.sqlite3`
  - The IDE: `~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json`.

  kiro-cli refreshes its own token first (`kiro-cli debug refresh-auth-token`).
  A token the plugin refreshes itself is written back, so kiro-cli and the
  IDE go on with it.
- **Kiro API key (`ksk_…`)**: sent with `tokentype: API_KEY`, as kiro-cli
  sends it. `GetProfile` is asked in us-east-1, then eu-central-1, for the
  region the key's profile is in; a key it finds none for is used in
  us-east-1, as kiro-cli uses it. Its models are listed with the control
  plane's `ListAvailableModels` and its credits with `GetUsageLimits`, and
  no profile is named in its calls, as kiro-cli names none.

A browser sign-in is kept where OpenCode keeps sign-ins (`auth.json`; in
magpie, `plugin-auth.json`) as an `oauth` entry. The entry holds the
tokens, the profile ARN, the region and, for AWS, the registered client.
Refreshing such a sign-in:

- magpie renews the token 10 minutes before it expires, through the
  plugin's `auth.refresh`, once for the account and before its requests,
  models and usage need it. magpie saves the new token. A failed renewal,
  even one Kiro refused, doesn't mark the account: it is tried again.
  The usage read does: a sign-in Kiro refused there marks the account
  signed out (`signIn: "expired"`), so magpie passes over it and offers
  Sign in again on its row, and a clean read takes the mark off.
- OpenCode doesn't call that hook: there the token is refreshed 2 minutes
  before it expires, before a request, and saved.
- Either way, a token Kiro turns down (a 403) is refreshed and the request
  tried once more.
- Only one refresh runs at a time, magpie's renewal included, and a token
  refreshed but not yet saved is used rather than spending the old refresh
  token again.
- kiro-cli's and the IDE's sign-ins aren't renewed by magpie: they are
  refreshed before a request, as above, and written back.

Tokens are refreshed through:

- Google/GitHub: through `prod.<region>.auth.desktop.kiro.dev/refreshToken`.
- Builder ID/Identity Center: through AWS's `oidc.<region>.amazonaws.com/token`.

## Requests

Kiro has no API OpenCode speaks. The models are declared on Anthropic's
Messages (`@ai-sdk/anthropic`), and the plugin's `fetch` handles each
request:

- It sends the request to `runtime.<region>.kiro.dev/generateAssistantResponse`,
  the API kiro-cli uses, with kiro-cli's headers. The region is the one the
  profile ARN names.
- It turns the request into a Kiro conversation:
  - The system prompt goes at the head of the first message.
  - System messages that end the conversation (Claude Code's environment
    context) are sent as a turn before the question, answered by Kiro IDE's
    "Understood.", so the question is the message answered (#538). After
    tool results they stay with them.
  - Tool calls and results are paired: an unanswered call gets an error
    result, and a result longer than 250,000 characters is cut.
  - Tool ids Kiro wouldn't take are rewritten. A tool name over 64
    characters (an MCP plugin's, in Claude Code) is sent shortened with a
    hash and its calls come back under the full name.
  - A tool's images (a screenshot, Codex's view_image) go with the
    message that answers the call, as Kiro's tool results hold text alone.
  - Only the latest images are sent.
  - An image Kiro would turn away for size (over 5 MiB as Base64, which is
    3.75 MiB of file) is made smaller on the request being sent: its long
    edge brought to 2000 pixels, then WebP or JPEG, smaller each try. One
    that can't be read or brought under is replaced by a short note, so the
    conversation goes on (#428). Smaller images are sent as they are.
  - Tools the history used but the request doesn't offer are declared.
  - A tool's input schema says `type: "object"` at its root, as Kiro
    wants: one that says no type (or object-or-null) is sent saying so, and
    an empty one as an object with no properties. Kiro answers 400
    `REQUEST_BODY_INVALID` to either. Everything under the root (a union
    there, properties, `$ref`s, `nullable`) is sent as given, and a root
    that names another type is left alone.
- It turns the AWS event stream Kiro answers with back into Messages'
  events (streamed) or one message. The reply includes text, thinking,
  tool calls and usage. When Kiro reports only how full the context is,
  input tokens are estimated from that.
- Thinking (Claude models and Auto) is asked for the way kiro-cli asks, in
  the prompt, with a budget: low 10k, medium 20k, high 30k, xhigh and max
  50k (as magpie's built-in Kiro: #120). The
  `<thinking>` block of the reply comes back as thinking.
  A model whose Kiro catalog lists effort levels with adaptive thinking
  (`additionalModelRequestFieldsSchema`) is sent the level instead, as Kiro
  IDE sends it: `additionalModelRequestFields` with `thinking.type:
  "adaptive"` and `output_config.effort` (or `reasoning.effort`), and no
  budget. So xhigh and max stay apart there (#538).
  Thinking is asked for only when the request's `thinking` is `enabled` or
  `adaptive`. An effort with no `thinking`, or with it `disabled` (Claude
  Code's title requests, or a turn with thinking off), is sent with no
  thinking at any level.
- Anthropic's hosted web search is answered with Kiro's own web search
  (see [Web search](#web-search)).
- Kiro's failures keep their meaning:
  - input too long → 400
  - no capacity → 503
  - usage limit → 429
  - throttling → "rate limited"

## Web search

A request offering Anthropic's hosted web search,
`{"type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search", "max_uses": n}`, is
searched with Kiro's own web search, sent as kiro-cli (2.35) sends it:

- The model is offered kiro-cli's `web_search` tool as kiro-cli's agent
  offers it: its description, a `query` (200 characters at most) and the
  `__tool_use_purpose` kiro-cli adds to each tool. A call the model makes to
  it is searched here, never passed to the caller as a `tool_use`. Its
  `__tool_use_purpose` is kiro-cli's alone: it isn't searched for, and the
  caller's `server_tool_use` has the `query` only.
- The search is Kiro's runtime's `InvokeMCP` operation:
  `POST runtime.<region>.kiro.dev/`, `Content-Type:
  application/x-amz-json-1.0`, `x-amz-target:
  AmazonCodeWhispererStreamingService.InvokeMCP`, in the account's region
  with its token. Its body is a JSON-RPC `tools/call` of `web_search` with
  `{query}` and nothing else, and the profile as `profileArn` beside it:
  over AWS JSON 1.0 that member is sent in the body, and without it there
  Kiro answers 400 `profileArn is required for this request`. It goes in
  `x-amzn-kiro-profile-arn` too, as kiro-cli 2.35 sends it. An API key,
  sent as `tokentype: API_KEY`, names no profile in either, as kiro-cli
  names none for one. The answer is
  `{jsonrpc, id, result, error}`, the result being the `tools/call`'s.
- The pages found go back to the model as the call's result (title, URL,
  date, snippet), and it is asked again. The caller is answered as
  Anthropic answers: `server_tool_use` and `web_search_tool_result` blocks
  (streamed or not), then the answer, and `usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests`.
- Each result has the page's `title`, `url` and `page_age`. `encrypted_content`
  is `""`: Kiro has no sealed copy of the page, and none is made up (as
  magpie's own search answers). The answer cites its pages by URL in its
  text; it has no `citations`, which need Anthropic's encrypted index.
- `max_uses` is kept, and no request searches more than 10 times. A search
  past it is a `max_uses_exceeded` error; a model still searching after
  `max_uses` + 2 turns is stopped with `pause_turn`. A `max_uses` that isn't
  a whole number of at least 1 is a 400.
- `allowed_domains` or `blocked_domains` filter the pages Kiro's search
  returns; the search itself isn't told them, so fewer pages may come back.
  A domain takes in its subdomains; with a path (`example.com/Docs`), only
  pages under it, the host matched in any case and the path as written.
  Both at once, or `user_location`, which Kiro's search has no place for,
  is a 400.
- A search that fails (Kiro unreachable, an error, an answer it can't
  read, a query over 200 characters) is a `web_search_tool_result_error`,
  and the model is told why. A token Kiro's search turns down (403) is
  refreshed once, as a request's is. A cancelled request stops searching.
- Kiro failing on a turn after a search is an error: streamed, an `error`
  event after the blocks said; not streamed, the failure's status, not a
  200 holding only the searches.
- A turn that also calls the caller's own tools ends there (`tool_use`),
  with its searches. The conversation sent back, with its
  `server_tool_use` and `web_search_tool_result` blocks, gives the model
  each search's call and result again. A tool of the caller's named
  `web_search` (no hosted `type`) stays the caller's.
- Other hosted tools are not sent, as before.

### Supported scope

Only `web_search_20250305` named `web_search` is searched (Claude Code sends
it). Any other tool whose type begins `web_search` (a newer version such as
`web_search_20260209`, another name, the same tool twice) is a 400 before
Kiro is asked: with `searches: true` magpie hands every such tool to the
plugin rather than searching for it, so dropping it would leave the search
asked for undone. A client that sends a newer version needs
`provider.kiro.searches: false`, so magpie's own search serves it as it did
before; the 400 says so.

The `config` hook says `searches: true` on the provider, so magpie passes a
client's web search (Claude Code's WebSearch) on to Kiro as sent rather than
searching for it. Set `provider.kiro.searches` to `false` to have magpie's
own search used instead.

## Models

The `config` hook declares `auto` (Kiro picks the model). Once signed in,
the `provider.models` hook replaces it with the account's own list from
`List-Available-Models`, with the default first. Each model carries its
context window, output limit and whether it takes images. Claude models
and Auto have the thinking variants.

## Not included

- Usage and quota (credits, the monthly window).
- Switching between several accounts. OpenCode keeps one sign-in per
  provider.
- Signing in with a company's own identity provider in the browser (use
  kiro-cli's sign-in).

@magpie-community/opencode-loomy-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-loomy-auth

[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) / [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) provider 插件：**Loomy（讯飞，`loomyad.xunfei.cn`）**——登录、模型清单、聊天转发、双积分钱包与每日赠送积分刷新（签到）。

请求形态移植自 [aimod-cc/agent2api](https://github.com/aimod-cc/agent2api)（MIT）的 `providers/loomy`，按 magpie 插件 API 重写。

## 安装

```
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-loomy-auth
magpie plugin login loomy     # 选「短信验证码登录」或「手动粘贴 session」
```

## 能力

- **登录**：`短信验证码登录`（发码 → 输入 6 位码完成，session **14 天**）或 `手动粘贴 session`。
- **无续期接口**：session 过期（业务码 `020002`/`100002`）需重新登录（短信或粘贴）。
- **聊天**：`POST {modelBase}/chat/completions`，OpenAI 形态基本透传，两处适配（参照实现 `reasoning_patch` / `images.rs`）：思考档折进 low/medium/high（超档删除）、DeepSeek 系模型的 data-URI 图片转 `<image_base64>` 标记；SSE；请求头必须带 `charset=utf-8`（上游对无 charset 的 body 按 GBK 解码）。
- **模型**：登录前给静态表（2026-10-16 实抓 `/api/v1/models` 的 chat 模型：DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash / deepseek-v4-flash-0731 / MiniMax-M3 / Kimi-k2.6 / qwen-3.8-max / GLM-5.3-Flash / qwen3.8-flash / spark-x / mimo-v2.5 / auto），登录后以 `GET /api/v1/models` 的实时目录为准（能力位读 `capabilities`；展示名尾部倍率 `(x3.0)` 拆为 rate 字段）。
- **余额（usage）**：`GET /api/v2/points/records?...` → 永久积分 + 每日赠送积分两个窗口；每日窗口用厂商自己的 `dailyLimitPoints`/`dailyRemainingPoints` 报「已用/剩余/上限」，厂商未带这一对时按无上限的余额展示（不编造上限）。响应缺余额字段时报 error（"未知"不冒充 0）。
- **签到判定**：`first-login` 接口对"当天首登"与"重复调用"都返回成功，插件用调用前后的每日余额差判定——涨了 = `claimed`（今日首登奖励），没涨 = `done`（已领过/无每日钱包）。
- **每日签到（checkin）**：`POST /api/v1/points/first-login`（body `{}`）——服务端按"当天是否第一次"把每日赠送刷回；按天幂等，重复调=成功。这是厂商客户端自己就会发的那个单请求（判定见上）。

## 账号域签名说明

登录两步（`POST https://account.xfinfr.com/login/phone/{sendMsgCode,checkCode}`）带 HMAC-SHA1 签名头（9 段待签串，AK/SK 为客户端内置常量），插件按参照实现同款实现（见 `index.mjs` 的 `signHeaders`）。

## 环境变量（测试 / 镜像用，与 agent2api 同名）

| 变量 | 默认 |
|---|---|
| `LOOMY_XFYUN_BASE_URL` | `https://account.xfinfr.com`（登录域，HMAC 签名；来自客户端安装包 `app.asar` 内解密的 `.env.prod` 的 `VITE_XFYUN_BASE_URL`，是讯飞账号域 CAccount 自己的 host） |
| `LOOMY_POINTS_BASE_URL` | `https://loomyad.xunfei.cn`（积分/签到/模型网关） |

## 测试

```
bun test packages/loomy
```

测试打到本地假上游（`fake.mjs`），不触网、不使用真实 token。

## 许可

MIT。请求逻辑移植自 aimod-cc/agent2api（MIT）。

@magpie-community/opencode-mimo-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-mimo-auth

Signs in to **Xiaomi MiMo** with a Xiaomi account, the way the MiMo desktop
app does, and makes its model requests. Provider id: `mimo-app`.

## Sign-in

One way, **Xiaomi account**. The plugin opens Xiaomi's sign-in page
(account.xiaomi.com's long-poll ticket). Sign in there, or scan its QR code
with the Xiaomi phone app. The plugin waits on the ticket until Xiaomi says
the account is in, so there's nothing to paste back.

Xiaomi's passToken then signs the account on at the MiMo server. The server
sends the browser through account.xiaomi.com and back through its `/sts`,
which sets the session cookies (`serviceToken`, `userId`, `cUserId`). An
account from Russia or India is moved to that region's server
(`mimo-server-ru` / `mimo-server-in`). Everyone else stays on
`mimo-server-sgp`.

## Requests

Chat completions go to `https://mimo-server-<region>.xiaomimimo.com/api/route/chat/completions`
(`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`). Each request carries:

- the session cookies, with no `Authorization` header
- `X-Mimo-Source: mimocode-cli-free`
- `X-Client-Version: 26.929.292248`
- the app's User-Agent

`mimo-auto`, the app's default model, is requested as `mimo-pro`.

The session is renewed with the passToken a day after it was issued.
magpie (0.1.684 and later) does it ahead of time through `auth.refresh`, ten
minutes before that day is out (`refreshLead`), once for the account and
before its requests, models and usage ask for it; a passToken Xiaomi no
longer takes marks the account for a new sign-in. The check before each
request stays for OpenCode, which doesn't call `auth.refresh`, and one
sign-on at a time serves both. A model
request the server turns away (a 401) is answered as the server answered it,
as magpie's built-in MiMo account did; reading usage renews the session once
when the server turns it away. If the passToken no longer works, sign in
again.

### An account with a Token Plan and no app membership

The app's server answers such an account's requests, every model, with
403 `membership_required` ("未开通会员或会员已到期，请订阅后使用"). The
plugin then asks the account's Token Plan instead. The passToken signs on
at the open platform (platform.xiaomimimo.com, sid `api-platform`), which
gives the plan's `tp-` key (`/tokenPlan/apiKey/raw`) and its endpoint
(`openaiBaseUrl` of `/tokenPlan/apiKey`, e.g.
`https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1`). The request goes there with
`Authorization: Bearer <tp- key>` and no cookies, with `mimo-pro` asked as
`mimo-v2.6-pro` and `mimo-flash` as `mimo-v2.6-flash`. For an hour after,
the account's requests go straight to the plan; then the app is asked
first again, in case a membership was bought. A key reset at the platform
(the plan's 401) is read again on the next request. An account with no
Token Plan, or a plan with no key yet (the platform's Token Plan page
makes one), gets the app's 403 as it is.

## Usage

magpie's Usage card shows the MiMo app's plan and its week's allowance.
A Token Plan bought at the open platform (platform.xiaomimimo.com) is a
plan of its own, spent by its `tp-` API key at
`token-plan-<region>.xiaomimimo.com`. The same passToken signs on at the
platform (sid `api-platform`), so the card shows the Token Plan too. With
an app plan, its credits are an aside beside the week's allowance: this
account's requests go to the app. With no app plan, the Token Plan is the
card's plan and its credits are the account's allowance, since its
requests go to the plan (above).

## Where the sign-in is kept

In OpenCode's `auth.json`, or magpie's `plugin-auth.json`, as an OAuth sign-in:

- `refresh`: the Xiaomi account as JSON (`userId`, `cUserId`, `passToken`, `deviceId`, `region`, `base`)
- `access`: the session cookies as JSON
- `expires`: when the session is renewed
- `accountId`: the Xiaomi user id

## Models

| Model | Name | Context | Output | Input |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mimo-pro` | MiMo Pro | 1,000,000 | 128,000 | text, image |
| `mimo-flash` | MiMo Flash | 1,000,000 | 128,000 | text, image |

@magpie-community/opencode-minimax-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-minimax-auth

Signs in to MiniMax Code (mcode) accounts so their credits and M Plan can be
used. That covers the free credits and the daily check-in's credits. There is
one provider for each of MiniMax's two sites:

| Provider id | Site | API |
|---|---|---|
| `minimax-code` | MiniMax Code, China (minimax.cn / minimaxi.com) | `https://agent.minimax.cn/mavis/api/v1/llm/v1` |
| `minimax-code-global` | MiniMax Code, international (minimax.io) | `https://agent.minimax.io/mavis/api/v1/llm/v1` |

The package exports `MiniMaxCodeAuthPlugin` (`minimax-code`) and
`MiniMaxCodeGlobalAuthPlugin` (`minimax-code-global`).

## Risk

Read this before you use the package:
- **The credits are for MiniMax's services.** MiniMax gives them for use in
  MiniMax Code, and its terms decide where else they may be used. This
  package uses them from other agents. MiniMax hasn't approved that.
- **The risk to the account is yours.** MiniMax may limit, suspend or close
  an account that uses them this way.
- **This is a community package.** It has nothing to do with MiniMax.

## Signing in

You sign in with MiniMax Code's own device sign-in: the same OAuth device
flow, PKCE S256 and client `mcode-public` that `mcode /login` uses.
- magpie opens MiniMax's page and shows the code to confirm there.
- The plugin then waits for the sign-in and finishes by itself.

MiniMax Code's own sign-in is never read or changed. That is
`~/.minimax/auth/…`, so signing in here doesn't sign `mcode` out.

The sign-in is kept as an OpenCode `oauth` auth:
- what it holds: the access and refresh tokens, their expiry, and the
  MiniMax user id and email;
- OpenCode keeps it in `auth.json`;
- magpie keeps it in `plugin-auth.json`.

Each account signs in on its own, so magpie can hold several and switch
between them.

Refreshing:
- MiniMax spends a refresh token once. Sent a second time it is
  `invalid_grant`, which signs the account out, so the plugin never sends
  one twice.
- magpie renews the token ten minutes before it ends, through the plugin's
  `auth.refresh`, once for the account and before its requests, models and
  usage need it. OpenCode doesn't call that hook: there the access token is
  refreshed two minutes before it ends, before a request. Either way the
  new token is saved.
- When MiniMax turns the token away (HTTP 401), the request goes again with
  a newer token if one was saved meanwhile, else after a refresh.
- Only one refresh runs at a time for an account. Requests that arrive
  meanwhile wait for it and use its token. When saving the new token
  fails, the plugin keeps it in memory and goes on with it, rather than
  with the spent one on disk.
- A refresh token someone else spent first (another magpie process) isn't a
  sign-out when the new one they saved is there: that one is used.
- The account counts as signed out only when MiniMax answers the refresh
  with `invalid_grant` (HTTP 400). Any other failure keeps the sign-in, and
  the current token is used while it lasts.

## Requests

Chats are Anthropic messages (`@ai-sdk/anthropic`) sent to
`<API>/messages`. Each one carries MiniMax Code's headers:
- `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`;
- `x-api-key: sk-xxx`, the placeholder key MiniMax Code gives its SDK;
- `User-Agent: MiniMaxAgent`;
- `X-Mavis-Agent-Id: main`;
- `X-Mavis-Timezone-Offset`;
- `X-Mavis-Session-Id`. This is the conversation's id when magpie or
  OpenCode passes one, and a fixed id for the plugin's run otherwise.

A refusal that says the credits or quota ran out goes on as a 429. The 402,
403 or 429 statuses count, when the body says so. That way magpie can move
the conversation to another account.

## Models

When you are signed in, the models come from MiniMax Code's live model
config (`GET /mavis/api/v1/models`). The list includes each model's context,
image input and thinking options. If the live list doesn't answer, this
built-in list is used instead:

| Model | Context | Output | Images | Reasoning levels (variants) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview | 1M | 512K | yes | low, medium, high, xhigh, max |
| MiniMax-M3 | 1M | 512K | yes | none, high |
| MiniMax-M2.7 | 200K | 128K | no | — (always thinks) |
| MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed | 200K | 128K | no | — (always thinks) |

MiniMax Code's own list reports 512K/128K for the M3 family, but the
endpoint accepts 1,048,576 input tokens and 524,288 output tokens for
every one of them, so those are the limits given here. An agent that
believed the advertised ones would compact its history about half way too
early.

Variants map to what MiniMax Code sends:
- a level is adaptive thinking at that effort, which becomes
  `output_config.effort`;
- `none` turns thinking off.

## Usage

The usage card shows:
- the credits left;
- a Credits window: how much of the credits not yet expired is used, and
  when the soonest of them runs out, from the credit details MiniMax's own
  client lists (`/minimax-cloud/api/v1/credit/details`); beside an M Plan
  it is aside, since the plan's windows come first;
- the plan: Free, or the M Plan's tier and when it ends;
- for an M Plan, its windows (5 hours, 7 days, and any model's own) from
  `coding_plan/remains`.

These are read the way MiniMax Code reads them, with its signed account API.

## Check-in

The account's daily check-in (每日签到) is claimed through the same sign-in:
the plugin reads the panel (`/minimax-cloud/api/v1/signin/status`) and
claims the day's credits (`/minimax-cloud/api/v1/signin/claim`) with the
same signed account API, asked as MiniMax Code's own `/checkin` asks them:
as the account (its MiniMax user id, looked up first when the sign-in
didn't keep it), from the desktop client, on MiniMax Code's own hosts
(agent.minimax.io, agent.minimaxi.com). A check-in turned away with 401 is
renewed and asked once more, with the user id read again, as MiniMax Code
does. magpie can run it once a day per account, when its
MiniMax check-in switch is on; Settings → Usage → Plugins has that switch
and a *Check in now* button, and the outcome — claimed, done, inactive,
ineligible, with the streak — lands on the account's Usage card.
OpenCode doesn't call this hook: there, check in from MiniMax Code or
MiniMax's site.

## Not here

- **No sign-out.** Signing out doesn't revoke the token on MiniMax's side.

@magpie-community/opencode-nous-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-nous-auth

Signs in to [Nous Portal](https://portal.nousresearch.com) with its OAuth
Device Authorization flow and sends model requests in
[magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) and [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai). Provider id:
`nous-portal`. This is separate from magpie's `nous` API-key preset.

## Signing in

Once the package is available from magpie's plugin registry:

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-nous-auth
magpie plugin login nous-portal
```

Magpie displays a verification URL and a code. Open the page, sign in and
approve the code there; finish any CAPTCHA in your browser. The plugin polls
for approval and completes sign-in without a local callback server.
Hermes Agent does not need to be installed or running.

In OpenCode, add `"@magpie-community/opencode-nous-auth"` to the `plugin`
array in `opencode.json`, then run `opencode auth login`.

The flow uses Nous Portal's `/api/oauth/device/code` and `/api/oauth/token`
with public client `hermes-cli`, scope `inference:invoke`, and no client
secret. Device polling follows [RFC 8628](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628.html#section-3.5),
including the server's interval and `slow_down` responses. Nous has not
confirmed whether independent clients may use the public `hermes-cli`
OAuth client ID.

For ChatGPT plan sharing, see [Nous Portal's documentation](https://portal.nousresearch.com/help/chatgpt-plan-sharing).

## Where the sign-in is kept

Magpie keeps the account in its plugin credential store; OpenCode uses its own
sign-in store. The saved OAuth fields are `access` (inference JWT), `expires`
(epoch milliseconds) and `refresh` (versioned JSON containing the refresh
token, scope, token type and inference endpoint). **The entire `refresh` value
is secret**, even though it looks like JSON.

Expiry uses the earlier of the token response's lifetime and the JWT's `exp`.
If both are absent, renewal is scheduled one hour after the exchange, with
the same two-minute lead. This is a local fallback, not a Nous lifetime
guarantee; a 401 can still trigger renewal sooner. Explicitly expired or
malformed lifetimes are not extended.

Nothing is read from or written to `~/.hermes/auth.json`. A separate device
sign-in is intentional: Nous refresh tokens are single-use, and copying one
from Hermes could invalidate Hermes's session when either program renews it.

Magpie uses `auth.refresh` with a two-minute lead and saves the rotated
tokens. OpenCode does not call that hook, so the plugin also checks before
each request and persists renewals through `client.auth.set`. Concurrent
refreshes within one plugin instance share one exchange. A rotated pair is
kept in memory before a save is attempted, so a failed save does not cause
that instance to reuse the old refresh token.

**Do not run multiple hosts against the same saved account.** The per-request
save is not an atomic cross-process operation; a crash during an unsaved
rotation may require signing in again. Only explicit `invalid_grant`,
`invalid_token` or `refresh_token_reused` errors mark the grant expired.
Other refresh refusals, including HTML or empty 401/403 responses, keep the
credentials and allow a later retry.

## Requests

Models use OpenAI Chat Completions (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`) at
`https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1`. Magpie translates requests from
other agent protocols. Every request uses the current inference JWT as a
Bearer token; the refresh token is sent only to Portal's token endpoint in
`x-nous-refresh-token`, never to inference.

The plugin accepts only known inference paths (`/models`, `/chat/completions`,
`/completions`, `/embeddings`) at the production Nous inference or welcome
host. A Portal response cannot redirect Bearer tokens to an arbitrary host;
HTTP redirects are refused. Caller-supplied credentials and magpie-internal
headers are removed before forwarding.

A 401 triggers at most one refresh and retry. Other upstream errors keep
their status, and streaming responses pass through without buffering or
rewriting their content. The upstream `content-encoding` and `content-length`
headers are removed because fetch may already have decoded the body.

## Models

After sign-in, the account's live `/v1/models` list replaces the single
bootstrap entry (`Hermes-4-70B`). Model ids are preserved, including the
vendor prefix such as `openai/gpt-6-luna`. In magpie an exposed model is
addressed as `nous-portal/openai/gpt-6-luna`.

Magpie may initially expose only part of the catalog. To choose a model
listed for your account and test it:

```sh
magpie provider refresh nous-portal
magpie provider models nous-portal +openai/gpt-6-luna
magpie provider test nous-portal openai/gpt-6-luna
```

The `provider test` command takes the upstream id (`openai/gpt-6-luna`), not
the magpie-prefixed id. Model availability and billing depend on the account;
a model appearing in `/models` does not guarantee access. The plugin does
not guess model prices, context limits or vision/reasoning capabilities when
the catalog does not provide them. A failed catalog read does not become an
empty entitlement list.

## Not included

- Nous Portal API keys (`nous` remains magpie's separate built-in preset).
- Importing Hermes credentials or running Hermes's subscription proxy.
- Direct ChatGPT/Codex OAuth, billing or quota reporting, or daily check-in.
- An arbitrary inference URL override or cross-process token coordination.

## Test

Run the offline checks from the repository root with a temporary HOME:

```sh
h=$(mktemp -d)
HOME="$h" node --test packages/nous/index.test.mjs
HOME="$h" bun test
rm -rf "$h"
bun scripts/check.mjs
```

Before publication, try the local package with magpie's isolated test script:

```sh
export MAGPIE=/absolute/path/to/magpie
sh scripts/try.sh nous
sh scripts/try.sh nous login nous-portal
sh scripts/try.sh nous provider refresh nous-portal
sh scripts/try.sh nous provider test nous-portal openai/gpt-6-luna
```

`try.sh` uses `.sandbox/nous` rather than your real magpie sign-ins. It clears
ordinary environment variables, including proxy settings; configure a proxy
inside the sandbox if needed. Do not use a portable Windows magpie binary
that ignores HOME isolation. Sign-in and `provider test` contact Nous Portal;
the latter may consume account credits. Test a model your account can use,
and never share the sandbox's credential files.

Protocol reference: Hermes Agent's
[device flow](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/8b9ac5773ea07189f23aa9dfcdba1e59fd759c21/hermes_cli/auth_device_flow.py),
[refresh handling](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/8b9ac5773ea07189f23aa9dfcdba1e59fd759c21/hermes_cli/auth_nous.py)
and [Nous Portal proxy adapter](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/8b9ac5773ea07189f23aa9dfcdba1e59fd759c21/hermes_cli/proxy/adapters/nous_portal.py).

@magpie-community/opencode-opendesign-au.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-opendesign-auth

Open Design (open-design.ai) Cloud as a magpie / OpenCode provider: sign in
with the Open Design account, use the models its **Design Plan** entitles the
account to, and watch the plan's **5-hour and 7-day allowance** and wallet
balance where every other subscription's usage shows.

Works in [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) (which runs OpenCode provider plugins)
and in OpenCode.

```
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-opendesign-auth
magpie plugin login opendesign
```

In OpenCode, `opencode.json`:

```json
{ "plugin": ["@magpie-community/opencode-opendesign-auth"] }
```

then `opencode auth login`.

## What it signs in to

Open Design's cloud is two planes:

| Plane | Host | Key | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Control | `amr-api.open-design.ai` | `vela_ctrl_…` | plan, wallet balance, the Design Plan's allowance windows, the workspace |
| Model | `amr-link.open-design.ai/v1` | `sk-amr-…` | `/models`, `/responses` (the OpenAI Responses API) |

A sign-in is the same device authorization the Open Design CLI
(`vela login`) runs:

1. the plugin POSTs `/api/v1/cli/device-authorizations` and gets a code
   (`4HYFNA`) and an activation page (`open-design.ai/cloud/cli/activate?…`);
2. magpie opens that page; approving it says the CLI is signing in;
3. the plugin polls it and receives both keys for that account, with the
   account's email and id.

Nothing else is needed, and nothing of the desktop app's own sign-in
(`~/.amr/config.json`, a different machine-issued pair of keys) is read or
written.

## Sign-in methods

| Method | What it stores | Allowance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Open Design account** | the account's control + runtime keys | 5-hour and 7-day windows, wallet balance, plan |
| **Open Design API key** | a pasted `sk-amr-…` key | not readable: `amr-api` doesn't take API keys |

The account sign-in is the one that shows the allowance; the API key one
is there for a machine that can't open the approval page.

## Models

Nothing is listed per account at request time from anywhere but the vendor:
magpie calls the plugin's `provider.models`, which reads `amr-link`'s live
`/v1/models` at that account's key on every listing, so what a signed-in
account is offered is what its plan entitles it to right now. Limits, input
modalities and the vendor's own cost words (`rate`, e.g. `x0.5` for "low")
come from that same catalog.

Reasoning levels are not in the catalog, so `models.mjs` records the ones
measured against `amr-link` (#137): every model took `reasoning_effort`
`low` and `high`, and all but GPT-6 Luna thought at them, the ones the
catalog calls `standard` too. Those models reason at `low` and `high`;
GPT-6 Luna has no levels. A model the seed doesn't know reasons when its
vendor tier is `advanced`, with no levels until it is measured.

`models.mjs` is the seed the provider has *before* anyone signs in. Refresh
it from the live catalog with:

```bash
magpie plugin login opendesign            # once, so the key is on hand
bun refresh-models.mjs                    # or OPENDESIGN_KEY=sk-amr-… bun …
```

The script keeps the names and measured levels already there — the catalog
carries neither — and reads nothing else: no secret is written to the file or
printed.

Requests go to `https://amr-link.open-design.ai/v1`, each model on the API
amr-link answers its thinking on (measured, plugins#141): chat completions
(`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`) for most, the Responses API (`@ai-sdk/openai`)
for `claude-haiku-5.5` and `deepseek-v4-pro`, and Anthropic's messages
(`@ai-sdk/anthropic`) for `glm-5.3-flash`. Every model reasons at `low`,
`high` and `max`.

## Where the sign-in is kept

magpie's `plugin-auth.json` (mode 600), as an oauth account:
`{ type: "oauth", access: <runtime key>, control: <control key>, accountId:
<email>, uid: <account id> }`. Neither key expires, so there is nothing to
renew and `refresh` is empty.

## Use

```
magpie plugin                         # opendesign (Open Design, 11 models) signed in
magpie provider test opendesign
magpie quota                          # opendesign · Design Plan Go · 5h 32% ↻3h
```

### Replacing a custom provider

The plugin signs in to the provider id `opendesign`. A **custom provider**
of that same id (Providers → the host and key by hand) takes the id first,
so the plugin's provider is then listed as `opendesign-plugin`, with no
models of its own. Delete the custom provider — `magpie provider rm
opendesign` — and the plugin's provider takes the plain id, so agent
configs pointing at `opendesign/<model>` keep working, now with the
allowance card.

## The allowance in routing

The windows are gating windows (magpie's `aside` is left off), so magpie's
own routing reads them like any subscription's:

* a window magpie reads as used up makes the account count as used up, so
  routing groups skip it and a direct call to `opendesign/<model>` is refused
  with a 429 until that window renews;
* `magpie provider account-cap opendesign <account> [percent|off]` holds the
  account at a share of each window, and `--window "5 hours" 70` caps one
  window alone, which is how to leave headroom instead of spending the plan
  to the last credit.

Since Open Design falls back to the wallet balance once the Design Plan
allowance is out, an exhausted window holds the account rather than spending
the wallet. Set the account to spend its credits, or cap the windows, to
choose which of the two magpie does.

@magpie-community/opencode-orcaterm-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-orcaterm-auth

Signs in to **Tencent Cloud OrcaTerm** (腾讯云遨驰终端) and serves its AI assistant's models —
DeepSeek, Hunyuan, GLM and Kimi — in OpenCode and magpie. Provider id: `orcaterm`.

> **Unofficial.** This package is not affiliated with, authorised or endorsed by Tencent; its
> names and marks belong to their owners. It talks to the non-public APIs the OrcaTerm web
> client uses and identifies itself the way that client does, which may not be allowed by
> Tencent's terms, and those APIs may change at any time. Use it at your own risk, including
> the risk of restrictions on your account — see [Before you use this](#before-you-use-this-the-terms).

## Install

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-orcaterm-auth
magpie plugin login orcaterm
```

or install it from magpie's Plugins tab and sign in there.

QR sign-ins use the OrcaTerm user ID as the account identity, so signing in to the
same user again updates that account even when the token or nickname changes.
Older duplicate cards without this identity are not removed automatically.

## Before you use this: the terms

**This plugin uses OrcaTerm's built-in AI allowance from outside OrcaTerm, and Tencent's terms do
not clearly permit that.** Read this part before signing in.

### What the cookie pair actually is

`uin` and `skey` are **not an OrcaTerm token**. They are the **full Tencent Cloud console session**
— the same pair that gets you into the console, your CVM and Lighthouse instances, your billing,
your API keys. Anything holding them can act as you across Tencent Cloud, not just in OrcaTerm.

So the account you risk is not "an OrcaTerm account". It is **the account that holds your servers
and your billing**, and Tencent Cloud's service agreement 5.8 lets Tencent limit, suspend or
terminate that account and freeze it. **Do not use an account that owns production resources.**
If you want to try this, use a separate account with nothing behind it.

**The QR sign-in below does not have this problem.** It yields OrcaTerm's own OAuth access token,
which is confined to this product and expires in two hours — it is not a console session and cannot
reach your servers or billing. Nothing in this section applies to it. The cookie pair is the
fallback for when scanning is not possible, and it is the one that carries the risk above.

**Every host it touches, and what for:**

| Host | When | What goes there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lightai.cloud.tencent.com` | every chat | the credential, the message text |
| `api.orcaterm.cloud.tencent.com` | reading the allowance (cookie sign-ins only) | the credential |
| `orcaterm.com` | QR sign-in, token renewal, and OAuth account allowance reads | the credential, and the OAuth `code` |
| `res.wx.qq.com` | QR sign-in page | nothing — it serves WeChat's `wxLogin.js` |
| `open.weixin.qq.com` | the QR widget's iframe | the `appid`, `redirect_uri` and `state` OrcaTerm issued |

Three of those are Tencent's own; the last two belong to WeChat, and only the QR sign-in page loads
them — a cookie sign-in never does. Nothing goes anywhere else. The plugin does not share, resell or
pool quota, and it makes no attempt to evade anti-abuse checks. None of that changes the paragraph
above.

### Why the terms do not clearly allow it

OrcaTerm's user agreement reserves everything it has not explicitly granted:

- **2.3** — "本条及本协议其他条款未明示授权的其他一切权利仍由腾讯保留，您在行使这些权利时须另外取得腾讯的书面许可。"
- **2.1** — defines the service as OrcaTerm itself (remote connection, sign-in, file management).
  The built-in AI allowance (1000 questions a month on the basic edition, 6000 on professional) is a
  resource entitlement attached to the product; it is never described as an API callable from
  elsewhere.

Related clauses that this use touches: 3.5.3 (using data without permission), 3.5.5 (probing or
testing the platform), 3.5.7 (gaining advantage through a bug), 6.5(4) (using the service in a way
Tencent has not authorised). Tencent Cloud's service agreement 5.7(3) covers unauthorised access and
interference.

The consequences are concrete: 4.4.1 and 7.2 allow Tencent to limit features, suspend the account
or terminate the service, and Tencent Cloud's agreement 5.8 allows the same plus freezing the
account.

**One detail worth weighing:** OrcaTerm's official OpenAPI exposes session and sign-in calls —
`DescribeInstancesFeatureStatus`, `GenerateAuthLoginUrl`, `GetUserInfo`, `StartSSHTerminalSession`,
`StartRDPTerminalSession`, `VerifyOAuthUser` — and **no AI question endpoint at all**. The allowance
is not built to be called from outside the product.

What is clearly allowed: asking OrcaTerm's assistant questions inside OrcaTerm's own web, desktop or
mini-program clients; and attaching **your own** API key through OrcaTerm's custom-model setting
(officially: "自定义 AI 模型不会消耗 AI 问答次数额度").

**So: if you use this plugin, the risk is yours.** This project does not claim Tencent permits it,
does not resell or share quota, and is not affiliated with Tencent. If your account matters to you,
use the custom-model path with your own key instead, or ask Tencent for written permission first.

### On the assistant's own tools

The assistant is attached to the user's servers, and it runs in RE_ACT mode. This plugin sends no
tools, no MCP servers and no approved tools, which is what keeps it to answering questions — but
that is the request being empty of tools, not proof the assistant can do nothing on its own side.
`hideToolMessage` is therefore left `false`, so that if anything does run, its trace stays in the
reply where you can see it.

## Sign-in

Two credentials can drive the assistant, and they are **not** equal in scope:

| Credential | Comes from | Lifetime | Authority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **WeChat OAuth access token** (recommended) | scanning a QR code | 2 hours, renewed automatically | OrcaTerm only |
| `uin` + `skey` | your Tencent Cloud **console session** | until you sign out of the console | your whole Tencent Cloud account |

The QR route is preferred: it is the same sign-in the OrcaTerm clients use, and the token it yields
cannot touch anything outside OrcaTerm. Either kind is accepted — the plugin tells them apart by the
key's shape.

### Scan a QR code (recommended)

```sh
magpie plugin login orcaterm     # choose the first entry
```

magpie opens a page with a WeChat QR code on it — by default
<http://127.0.0.1:4080/login>, or another port if 4080 is taken, in which case the URL it shows is
the real one. Scan it and the plugin carries on by itself; there is no URL to copy.

How the callback is captured: the page embeds WeChat's `qrconnect` widget through the official
`wxLogin.js` with `self_redirect: true`. After a scan, the return to
`orcaterm.com/oauth/wechat/bridge?code=…&state=…` happens inside the widget's **own inner iframe**,
so that page's `window.parent` is still our page and its `postMessage` arrives. Without
`self_redirect`, WeChat navigates the top window instead, which replaces the page and loses the
message — that is the one detail the whole flow hangs on.

Behind a remote deploy the page listens on the server's loopback and your browser cannot reach it:

```sh
ssh -L 4080:127.0.0.1:4080 <server>
```

`ORCATERM_CAPTURE_PORT`, `ORCATERM_CAPTURE_HOST` and `ORCATERM_CAPTURE_BASE` override the address.
`ORCATERM_CAPTURE_HOST` is what the socket binds to, and it defaults to the loopback; setting it to
`0.0.0.0` means anyone who can reach the machine can load the sign-in page, and the `state` it carries
is in that page's HTML — so only do that behind something that restricts who can connect. A wildcard
bind accepts the page from this machine's own interface addresses, so reaching it by LAN address
works; every other origin is refused.

The token is renewed before it expires through `OAuthRefreshToken`, so a normal session never asks
you to scan again.

### Paste the cookie pair (fallback)

1. Sign in at <https://cloud.tencent.com> in a browser (the AI allowance follows the Tencent Cloud
   sign-in, not a separate OrcaTerm one).
2. Open DevTools → **Application** → **Cookies** → `https://cloud.tencent.com`.
3. Copy the values of **`uin`** and **`skey`**.
4. In magpie, run `magpie plugin login orcaterm` and pick the paste entry, as
   `uin=o1234567890; skey=AbCdEf…`.

Both halves are required. The AI endpoint reads the pair as one credential: with only `skey`, or
with `p_uin`/`p_skey` under those names, it answers `NEED_UIN_AND_SKEY` and never looks further.

## Models

Use only what OrcaTerm's own model picker offers. The ids are **namespaced** — `TokenHub/<model>`
and `Hunyuan3/<model>` — and that prefix is the whole difference: sent bare, `glm-5.3` answers
`LLM(glm-5.3) is not loaded`, while `TokenHub/glm-5.3` answers.

| id | label in the picker | reasoning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TokenHub/deepseek-v4-pro` | Deepseek-V4-Pro | ✓ |
| `TokenHub/deepseek-v4-flash` | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | |
| `TokenHub/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | |
| `TokenHub/glm-5.3` | GLM-5.3 | ✓ |
| `TokenHub/glm-5.3-flash` | GLM-5.3-Flash | |
| `TokenHub/glm-5.2` | GLM-5.2 | |
| `TokenHub/kimi-k3` | Kimi-K3 | |
| `Hunyuan3/hy3` | Hy3 | ✓ |
| `Hunyuan3/hy4-preview` | Hy4-preview | ✓ |

**Do not use the others.** A few more ids answer on the endpoint but **cannot be selected in
OrcaTerm's own model picker** — `glm-4.7-thinking`, `kimi-k2-thinking`, `kimi-k2.5`,
`kimi-k2.5-thinking`, `kimi-latest`, `hunyuan-turbos`, `qwen3`, `deepseek-reasoner`. Calling them
means going around the product's own interface, which the service may treat as abnormal use, and
**your account may be restricted for it**. They are therefore **not offered in `provider.models`**;
they resolve only so that a config written against them keeps working. A new config should use the
nine above.

Aliases work too (`deepseek`, `kimi`, `glm`, `hunyuan`), as do the picker labels themselves
(`Deepseek-V4-Pro`, `GLM-5.3`, `Hy3-preview`…), and the older ids (`deepseek-chat-latest`,
`glm-4.7`, `kimi-k2`, `hunyuan-t1`) resolve to their current equivalents.

Context and output limits are estimates: the upstream publishes no window size per model.

## When the upstream refuses

OrcaTerm answers a refusal **inside the stream** — `data: [ERROR]: …` — with HTTP 200 still on the
status line. Taken at face value a used-up allowance would look like a normal reply, and magpie
would neither fail over to another account nor let this one rest. So the plugin reads the head of
the stream first (`peekAnswer`, as `packages/codearts` does) and answers with a real status.

A rate limit is the one refusal that arrives **outside** the stream as well: a burst is answered
`HTTP 200` with a plain JSON body, `{"code":429,"data":null,"message":"Rate limit exceeded:
chat-rpm"}`. That path is classified by the same table, so it is a 429 and not a 502 — and it also
puts this account's pacer into its cool-down.

| Upstream says | Status returned | What magpie does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quota`, `额度`, `次数已用完`, `余额不足` | **429** | fail over to the next account, rest this one |
| `rate limit`, `频繁`, `限流`, or the JSON body `{"code":429,…}` | **429** | same, and this account's pacer cools down |
| `NEED_UIN_AND_SKEY`, `VERIFY_SKEY_UIN_FAILED`, `VERIFY_LOGIN_FAILED`, `VERIFY_USER_FAILED` | **401** + `X-Magpie-Sign-In: expired` | mark the account, stop sending to it |
| anything else (model unavailable, internal error) | **502** | fail over |
| the connection dies mid-stream | the stream is errored, `statusCode` 499 (cancelled) or 502 | fail over |
| the connection dies without streaming | **499** / **502** | fail over |

A refusal that arrives after the answer has started is delivered as a stream error rather than as
text, so it still counts as a failure.

### Rate limit

Ten chats a minute per account. The budget is the account's, not the plugin's, so it paces itself:
a sliding window holds a request until there is room, a 429 puts **that account's** pacer into a
cool-down rather than every account's, and `maxConcurrency` is 1. `ORCATERM_CHAT_RPM` lowers the
budget to leave room for the desktop client; `ORCATERM_NO_PACE=1` turns pacing off.

## Requests

magpie's gateway turns whatever protocol the agent speaks into a Chat Completions body and hands it
to this plugin's `fetch`. That body becomes one assistant turn: a conversation id, a user id, the last
user message as `input.input`, and any system text as a prefix, since the assistant has no system
role.

The earlier turns are **not** sent as `historyMessages` — they go in as a plain transcript inside
`input.input`, and `historyMessages` is always empty. Two reasons, both measured: a history entry's
kind lives in `type` (`human`/`ai`), not `role`, and the wrong shape fails inside upstream's own
handler with `[type] is not a function`; and with the right shape the text comes back echoed into the
answer. A transcript is what the assistant reads reliably.

Every request goes up as a new upstream conversation. OrcaTerm keeps a conversation's turns by its
id, so an id used twice put upstream's copy of the earlier turns — the assistant's own output format
and its JSON envelopes — in front of a transcript that already had them, and two sessions that
shared an id read each other's (#564).

The upstream answers in SSE frames whose `content` is that frame's addition (and whose
`fullContent`, when present, is everything so far); those become OpenAI deltas, with reasoning kept in
`reasoning_content`.

If a reply starts like the assistant's JSON envelope, its text is held until the reply ends so a
JSON example followed by more explanation cannot be mistaken for metadata. Plain prose and
reasoning still stream normally. Leading whitespace and JSON fences are accepted, and so is an
envelope whose answer has bare line breaks or quotes, which isn't JSON. A reply that comes only as
thinking, and an earlier reply an agent sends back in the envelope's shape, are read for their
answer the same way.

Two consequences worth knowing:

- **No tool calls.** The assistant runs its own tools server-side and never emits `tool_calls`, so
  the models are declared with `tool_call: false`. A client's tool calls and their results are
  written into the conversation as text so nothing is lost, but the agent does the calling itself.
- **No images.** `image_url` parts become an `[image]` note.

Token counts are not reported: the upstream returns none, and an estimate passed off as real usage
would make both cost and context accounting wrong. A caller that asks for `include_usage` gets the
answer without a usage block.

## Quota

`auth.usage` reads `DescribeUserBillingStatus` and reports the `hunyuan_ai` row — the AI answer
allowance, 1000 questions a month on the basic edition — as `amount / limit` with its reset date.
The other rows there (session sharing, secrets, space) are not shown: they are unrelated resources,
and session sharing's unlimited `-1` would read as an exhausted account.

QR accounts use the same access token as the official client's `ot_session` cookie, sent only to
`https://orcaterm.com/cgi/api`. Console-cookie accounts use `api.orcaterm.cloud.tencent.com`.
Both sign-in methods can show the allowance; scanning does not require console credentials.

## Tests

```sh
bun test
```

101 tests over nine files. No test signs in and none talks to Tencent: the chat tests replace `fetch`, and the only sockets are the loopback listeners used by the callback tests.

| file | what it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `signin.test.mjs` | the cookie shapes, and what each refusal means for the account |
| `request.test.mjs` | the Chat Completions → assistant body translation |
| `stream.test.mjs` | the SSE → OpenAI chunk conversion |
| `chunks.test.mjs` | frames that look cumulative but aren't; a frame split across chunks; a reset mid-stream; cancelling reaching the upstream |
| `peek.test.mjs` | a refusal read from the head of the stream becoming 429/401/502, and a real answer surviving the peek |
| `usage.test.mjs` | which `usageStats` row is the AI allowance |
| `audit.test.mjs` | invalid callback bodies; envelope whitespace and examples; EOF error frames; JSON error codes; reader cleanup; read failures and cancellation |
| `identity.test.mjs` | stable identity across QR re-sign-ins with rotated tokens or changed nicknames; distinct users staying separate; token user ID fallback; refusing missing identity; renewal and account-scoped backfill preserving credentials and metadata |
| `leak.test.mjs` | #564: the reported envelope, hand-written envelopes that aren't JSON, an envelope sent as thinking or kept in the history, a new upstream conversation on every request, and nothing added to another provider's request |
| `review.test.mjs` | the cases the reviews turned up: a reply containing `{"action": …}` is not truncated (including one character at a time, and one that ends mid-envelope); the JSON 429 is a 429; pacers are per account; only nine models are listed; a chat makes exactly one request and it is not `/conversation`; and `/cb` refuses a foreign `Origin`, a rebinding page, and a `state` it did not issue |

`chunks.test.mjs`'s cancel case fails if `releaseUpstream()` is removed, so the leak stays fixed.

## 中文

在 OpenCode 和 magpie 里使用**腾讯云遨驰终端（OrcaTerm）** AI 助手的模型：DeepSeek、混元、
GLM、Kimi。provider id：`orcaterm`。

> **非官方插件**：与腾讯、腾讯云及 OrcaTerm（遨驰终端）没有任何关联，也未获其授权或认可。
> 插件调用的是 OrcaTerm 网页端使用的非公开接口，并以与官方客户端相同的方式标识自己，
> 这可能不符合腾讯云的服务条款，接口也可能随时变更。使用风险（包括账号受限）由使用者自行承担。

- **登录**：首选**微信扫码**（`magpie plugin login orcaterm` 第一项），拿到的是 OrcaTerm 自己的
  OAuth accessToken —— 两小时有效、自动续期、只能用于 OrcaTerm。备选是粘贴 `uin` + `skey`：
  这两个是**腾讯云控制台的完整会话 cookie**，不是 OrcaTerm 专用令牌 —— 拿到它们就能在腾讯云范围内
  以你的身份操作，包括你的服务器和账单。**不要用持有生产资源的账号**，想试就用一个名下没有东西的独立账号。
- **条款**：OrcaTerm 用户协议 2.3 保留所有未明示授权的权利，2.1 把服务限定为 OrcaTerm 本身；
  内置 AI 额度是绑在产品上的资源权益，从未被授权为可外部调用的接口。相关条款还有 3.5.3、
  3.5.5、3.5.7、6.5(4) 与腾讯云服务协议 5.7(3)，后果见 4.4.1、7.2 与 5.8（可限功能、封号、终止服务）。
  一个细节：官方 OpenAPI 有会话与登录接口，**唯独没有任何 AI 问答接口**。
- **模型**：只用 OrcaTerm 模型选择器里能选到的那九个 —— `TokenHub/deepseek-v4-pro`、
  `TokenHub/deepseek-v4-flash`、`TokenHub/deepseek-v4.1-flash`、`TokenHub/glm-5.3`、
  `TokenHub/glm-5.3-flash`、`TokenHub/glm-5.2`、`TokenHub/kimi-k3`、`Hunyuan3/hy3`、
  `Hunyuan3/hy4-preview`。**id 必须带命名空间前缀**，否则上游答 `LLM(x) is not loaded`。
  **其余 id 不要用**（如 `qwen3`、`deepseek-reasoner`、`kimi-latest`、`hunyuan-turbos`、
  `glm-4.7-thinking` 等）：它们在选择器里选不到，属于绕过界面调用，**有封号风险**。
- **会连到哪些主机，以及发送什么**：`lightai.cloud.tencent.com`（每次对话：凭据和消息文本）、
  `api.orcaterm.cloud.tencent.com`（仅控制台 cookie 账号读额度：凭据）、
  `orcaterm.com`（扫码登录、令牌续期及扫码账号读额度：OAuth 凭据与 OAuth `code`；
  其中额度查询将 token 作为 `ot_session` cookie 发送到硬编码的 `https://orcaterm.com/cgi/api`，拒绝重定向）。
  另有 `res.wx.qq.com`（提供微信的 `wxLogin.js`，不发送登录凭据）与 `open.weixin.qq.com`
  （二维码 iframe，只接收 OrcaTerm 签发的 `appid`、`redirect_uri` 和 `state`，不发送登录凭据）；
  这两个只在扫码登录时加载，cookie 登录不会碰。除此之外不发往任何地方。
- **额度**：`magpie quota` 显示每月问答次数（基础版 1000 次）与重置日期。微信扫码账号通过
  `orcaterm.com` 的产品接口读取额度，使用已有 OAuth token 的 `ot_session` cookie，无需控制台凭据；
  控制台 cookie 账号继续通过 `api.orcaterm.cloud.tencent.com` 查询。
- **失败会如实报错**：上游把失败写在 SSE 里（`data: [ERROR]: …`），HTTP 状态仍是 200。
  插件会先读流头，把配额用完/限流回成 429、登录失效回成 401 并标记账号，这样 magpie 才会换账号
  或让账号歇着，而不是把失败当成一次正常回答。限流还有一条**不走 SSE** 的路径：HTTP 200 +
  `{"code":429,…}` 的 JSON，同样回成 429，并让该账号的限流器进入冷却。
- **多轮上下文**：之前的轮次以 transcript 形式写进 `input.input`，`historyMessages` 恒为空；
  每个请求在上游都是一个新会话，不复用会话 id —— 复用时上游会把它自己存的旧轮次（助手的输出格式和
  JSON 信封）再加一遍，两个会话共用一个 id 时还会读到对方的（#564）。
- **回复信封**：上游回复是助手自己的 JSON 信封（`{"action":"completion","taskCompletion":"…"}`），
  插件只把 `taskCompletion` 交出去；信封里有未转义的换行或引号、只出现在思考里、或被 agent 当作历史
  回复再发回来时，也一样只取答案。
- **不做工具调用、不支持图片**：助手在服务端跑自己的工具，插件只做文本往返。
