@magpie-community/opencode-qoder-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-qoder-auth

Your [Qoder](https://qoder.com) subscription in OpenCode and
[magpie](https://usemagpie.ai). The package serves Qoder's two sites, whose
accounts exist only on their own:

| Provider id | Site | Accounts | Plugin export |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qoder` | qoder.com (international) | Google, GitHub or email | `QoderAuthPlugin` |
| `qoder-cn` | qoder.cn ([Qoder CN](#qoder-cn)) | Alibaba Cloud or phone number | `QoderCNAuthPlugin` |
| `qwenwork` | gateway.qwenwork.cn ([QwenWork](#qwenwork-千问办公)) | phone number or email | `QwenWorkAuthPlugin` |
| `qwenwork-enterprise` | the enterprise's own domain ([QwenWork](#qwenwork-千问办公)) | email OTP or enterprise SSO | `QwenWorkEnterpriseAuthPlugin` |

What follows is about `qoder`. Qoder CN works the same way on its own
hosts; [its section](#qoder-cn) says what differs.

## Sign-in

**Sign in with Qoder** is the sign-in Qoder's desktop client uses:

1. A PKCE device flow opens qoder.com's account page.
2. openapi.qoder.sh is polled every 2 s until you authorize, for at most
   15 minutes.
3. The device token is traded for a job token, and the account's email and
   name are read.

The page is asked for no `redirect_uri`, as Qoder's CLI asks for none, so
the sign-in ends in the browser tab even when Qoder.app is installed
(before 0.2.25 it sent the desktop app's `qoder-app://`, which handed the
page to Qoder.app).

**Sign in with Qoder PAT** (and **Sign in with Qoder CN PAT**) skips the
device flow: a Personal Access Token from `<site>/account/integrations` is
posted to `/api/v1/jobToken/exchange` (`personal_token`), which answers a
job token, its refresh token and its expiry. The PAT is kept on the
credential, so a lapsed job refresh is exchanged again instead of asking
for the sign-in; PATs last up to a year. The job token signs the model list
and chat calls with the same COSY envelope either sign-in's does.

On Qoder CN this is the plugin's own reading of the protocol rather than
the CLI's path: qoder.cn's CLI signs requests with its device token and
never asks for a job token. Verified against a live qoder.cn account — the
exchange answers 200 with a `jt-` token, the signed model list answers 200
with that account's own models, and a chat completion returns its text.

A PAT account keeps the name its browser sign-in takes (`email || uid`): magpie
replaces an account on a new sign-in when both the accountId and the uid
match, so a renewed PAT sign-in names the same account rather than adding a
row beside the lapsed one.

A PAT account has no device token, so its usage read, campaigns pages and
daily check-in go out on the job token instead. The check-in works on it: a
live PAT account answered 200 to the campaigns list and `CLAIMED` to a claim,
so it earns the daily credits the browser sign-in does. That path has no
second token to rotate, so a refused call is the answer rather than a retry.

What is kept: the job token, its refresh token and expiry, the uid, the
device token and a machine id made for this sign-in. OpenCode keeps them in
`auth.json`; magpie keeps them in `plugin-auth.json`.

Refreshing:
- Qoder spends a refresh token once, so the plugin never sends one twice.
- magpie renews the job token 10 minutes before it runs out, through the
  plugin's `auth.refresh`, once for the account and before its requests,
  models and usage need it; magpie saves the new pair. OpenCode doesn't
  call that hook: there the job token is refreshed 5 minutes before it runs
  out, before a request, and the new pair is saved straight away.
- Only one refresh runs at a time. A request that reads the sign-in before
  magpie saved a renewal uses the renewed pair, and a renewal handed a pair
  a request already spent gives what that request got.
- A job token's end is what Qoder says: `expire_time` or `expires_at` (a
  date, or an epoch in seconds or milliseconds), then `expires_in`
  (milliseconds), then a day.
- A chat Qoder answers 401 or 403 with no other code ("Login expired") is
  sent again once: with the pair saved since, when another request, magpie
  or another process renewed it meanwhile, else after one refresh, under the
  same lock. A token renewed less than 5 minutes ago and refused again isn't
  renewed again; the refusal is the answer.
- A model Qoder serves that the account's listing has off or leaves out is
  asked for the same way: the job token is renewed once (or the pair saved
  since is used) and the list read again, before the request is answered
  `unknown or disabled model`. On a job token Qoder no longer honours in
  full, the listing can have only the free models on (#484). The same
  5-minute rule holds, and an id Qoder has never served is said unknown at
  once, with no renewal.
- The device token, which reads usage, has no end on record: it is rotated
  when Qoder refuses it. On a [Qoder CN](#qoder-cn) device-token account it
  is the chat token too, and is renewed as above.
- When Qoder refuses a refresh (401 or 403), the account needs signing in
  again. Any other failure is tried again later.

## Requests

Qoder serves its models on the API its client talks to:
`api3.qoder.sh/algo/api/v2/service/pro/sse/agent_chat_generation`. The
plugin's `fetch` takes the chat completion OpenCode sends and does the rest
itself.

**Writing the request**

- It writes the chat completion as Qoder's request:
  - Qoder's own system line comes before yours.
  - Messages become text and image blocks.
  - Tool calls and results become OpenAI tool turns. Images a tool returned
    follow in a user turn.
  - A result whose id the client lost answers its turn's call in order
    (since 0.2.22, #277): Qoder refuses a whole request with a result that
    answers no call before it. A result with no call left to answer goes
    as text in the user's turn.
  - Your tools become Qoder's native function tools.
  - A call the client sent without an id gets one made from its turn, its
    place and its arguments, so it goes out the same on every request.
- It marks the prompt for Qoder's cache as Qoder's own client does (since
  0.2.26, #290): the last block of the last user turn carries
  `cache_control: ephemeral` (nothing is marked when the last turn is a
  tool's result), user turns carry their blocks as `contents` too, and each
  request names its conversation in `session_id`. That id is a hash of
  the session the agent names (since 0.2.31, #330: DSH's
  `x-deepseek-harness-session-id` and the other agents' own session
  headers, which magpie hands the plugin's `chat.headers` hook, and
  OpenCode's session), else of Codex's thread (`prompt_cache_key`) when
  magpie sends one, else of the conversation's start, so every turn of one
  conversation names the same session; the key itself never goes out.
  Each request has its own `request_id` and `chat_record_id`.
- Every call that answers one user prompt goes out as one task, as Qoder's
  own client sends it (since 0.2.31, #330): one `request_set_id`, which is
  also `business.id`, and one `business.begin_at` for every call of the
  tool loop, `business.stage` "start" until a call is answered and
  "processing" after. A new user prompt in the session is a new task. The
  plugin keeps at most 512 tasks, each for 2 hours after its last call.
  Before 0.2.31 each call was a task of its own.
  - The model's own configuration from Qoder's list goes with it.
- It picks the reasoning effort from the model's own levels:
  - The nearest level to the one asked, the higher one on a tie.
  - The model's default when none is asked.
  - The lowest level for "none", when the model can't turn thinking off.
- It picks the context window (`context_length`) from the model's own
  windows (Qoder's Context setting: 200K, 400K, 1M): the default while the
  request fits it, else the smallest that holds it, else the largest. A
  larger window may cost more, so it is asked for only when needed.
- It encodes the body with the client's codec and signs the call with the
  client's COSY envelope. The envelope carries:
  - the account, AES-encrypted, with the key wrapped by Qoder's RSA key;
  - an MD5 signature;
  - the machine id and the client's headers.
  - `Cosy-Version`: the worker runtime version that Qoder's desktop app
    ships (1.1.69 in app 0.4.8, since 0.2.23, #281), because
    `Cosy-ClientType` says the desktop app.

**Reading the reply**

- Qoder's SSE comes back as a chat completion, streamed or not, with
  reasoning and usage.
- Tool calls Qoder writes as XML or JSON in its text become tool calls.
  Tool calls it sends the OpenAI way keep Qoder's id.
- A call written in the text that can't be read, or that the stream ends
  inside, is never sent on as the answer (since 0.2.16, #132): the turn
  ends as an error, a 502 or the stream's error frame with no finish, so
  the agent or magpie can try again. A call whose JSON is whole when the
  stream ends without its close is still the call; a tag in code or prose
  stays text.
- A call written in Anthropic's or Qwen's tags with no `<tool_call>`
  around it (since 0.2.36, #323), `<function_calls>` around one or more
  `<invoke name="…"><parameter name="k">v</parameter></invoke>`, or
  `<function=name><parameter=k>v</parameter></function>`, is a call too,
  but only for a tool the request declared; for any other, or in
  backticks or a code fence, it stays text. A parameter's value is JSON
  unless the tool's schema says string, in these and in `<tool_call>`.

**Errors**

| What Qoder says | What the request returns |
|---|---|
| A refused sign-in (no code, or code 105) | 401 |
| A quota (codes 110, 112–119, 122) | 429 |
| Busy or queued for the model (code 10605) | Since 0.2.28 the request waits in Qoder's queue as Qoder's client does (below), then is sent again; past the wait, 503 with `Retry-After` from Qoder's `retryAfterSeconds` (30s when it gives none). Since 0.2.40, when magpie has another candidate after this request (`x-magpie-fallback: 1`), the 503 comes at once, saying the queue and how many are ahead, and magpie asks the next. The sign-in is untouched |
| A refusal of the request itself (codes 406, 416, 430, 80411, 80412, 100400–100403) | 400, with Qoder's words |
| "Error in upstream response", the model's own vendor behind Qoder failing, which Qoder sends as a 400 (since 0.2.24) | 502, so magpie asks again or another account; the sign-in is untouched |
| A failure before the answer starts | Qoder's status |
| A failure after the answer has started | The stream ends with an error |

## Models

Chat responses report the display name from the same model-list entry
used to build the request, in both JSON completions and every SSE chunk
(including usage). A blank name or a name equal to the slot key falls
back to the requested model ID. This shared behavior applies to Qoder,
Qoder CN, QwenWork and QwenWork Enterprise, including tier labels.

Reporting the name does not fetch the model list again. The existing
cache and model-list refresh behavior remain in place: a model missing
from the cache still forces a refresh, and normal list refreshes update
the configuration and name together. Model-list keys, API IDs,
`X-Model-Key` and `model_config` are unchanged; slots with the same display
name remain independently selectable. The name describes the catalog
entry used for the request, not an attestation of the backend that
executed it.

The `provider.models` hook reads the account's own list, as Qoder's client
asks for it (`/algo/api/v2/model/list`). It keeps the enabled models of the
listing's `app` scene, the list Qoder's app shows and the one a request
names (`session_type: "app"`), and adds any model only the `chat` scene
still lists after the model it follows there, so a model picked before
stays served (since 0.2.13, #97: the app listed Fast, 0.8×, where chat
lists Performance, 1.1×). It leaves out "auto" and "default", which route
inside Qoder. It takes
each model's reasoning levels from its `thinking_config`, and its context
from its `context_config`: the largest window it offers (Qoder's docs
give Qwen3.8-Flash 200K, 400K and 1M), not `max_input_tokens` (180K
there), which is only what a request naming no window gets. A model listed
with no windows keeps `max_input_tokens`.

The `config` hook declares the list as it was on 2026-09-30, with the
app's Fast from 2026-10-12:

- Ultimate, Fast, Performance, Efficient
- Sonus, Cantus
- Qwen3.8-Max, Qwen3.8-Flash, Qwen3.7-Max, Qwen3.7-Plus
- Kimi-K3, Kimi-K2.8-Preview
- GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro, DeepSeek-Flash
- MiniMax-M3

Every model speaks chat completions (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`).

Every model a site ships also says, either way, whether it takes images:
`attachment` and `modalities.input` are set on every `config` entry, image
or no image. A kind left out is not "text only" to magpie but "the vendor
didn't say", and magpie then falls back to models.dev's vote by bare model
ID — where a same-named model of another vendor may take images, so this
one gets sent them. QwenWork's three models and Qoder CN's Lite shipped no
image key; since 0.2.47 they say text alone.

## Qoder CN

`qoder-cn` is for accounts on [qoder.cn](https://qoder.cn), the China site.
Those accounts sign in with Alibaba Cloud or a phone number and can't sign
in through `qoder`. Qoder CN speaks the same protocol as qoder.com:

- the same device flow, poll, job token and refresh paths;
- the same COSY envelope and body codec;
- the same model list, chat and usage paths.

Only the hosts and the sign-in's client id differ. The plugin uses the ones
Qoder CN's own CLI builds in for its `cn` build (`@qodercn-ai/qoderclicn`
1.1.65):

| | `qoder` | `qoder-cn` |
|---|---|---|
| Sign-in page | qoder.com | qoder.cn |
| Accounts: poll, tokens, user info, usage | openapi.qoder.sh | openapi.qoder.com.cn |
| Models and chat | api3.qoder.sh | gateway.qoder.com.cn |
| Device-flow client id | Qoder's desktop client's | Qoder CN's CLI's (production) |
| `redirect_uri` on the sign-in page | none, as Qoder's CLI sends (since 0.2.25) | none, as the CLI sends |

Qoder CN's CLI chats with the device token itself and never makes a job
token. The plugin asks qoder.cn for a job token first, as it does on
qoder.com. If qoder.cn refuses it (a 4xx), the account works the way the
CLI does:

- the device token signs the model calls;
- it is renewed with `/api/v1/deviceToken/refresh`, the chat and account
  tokens being one pair;
- a refused renewal (401 or 403) means signing in again.

Until you sign in, the `config` hook declares the tiers Qoder CN's CLI names
(Ultimate, Performance, Efficient, Lite). Once you are signed in, the
account's own list from gateway.qoder.com.cn replaces them.

Neither magpie's built-in Qoder CN nor this plugin has been checked against
every kind of qoder.cn account. If a sign-in or a chat fails, please open
an issue with the error.

### Enterprise VPC

A Qoder CN enterprise on its own VPC instance signs in with **Sign in with
Qoder CN Enterprise (VPC)** (since 0.2.8). It asks for the instance: its
name (`acme`) or one of its addresses (`acme.vpc.qoder.com.cn`,
`https://acme.vpc.qoder.com.cn`). Only https and hosts under
`vpc.qoder.com.cn` are taken.

The account then uses the instance's own hosts, as Qoder CN's CLI
(`@qodercn-ai/qoderclicn` 1.1.64) does once a VPC instance is set. The
paths, client id and protocol are the public ones:

| | Public Qoder CN | VPC instance `acme` |
|---|---|---|
| Sign-in page | qoder.cn | acme.vpc.qoder.com.cn |
| Accounts: poll, tokens, user info, usage | openapi.qoder.com.cn | acme-openapi.vpc.qoder.com.cn |
| Models and chat | gateway.qoder.com.cn | acme-gateway.vpc.qoder.com.cn |

- The instance is kept with the account, so its refreshes, models, usage
  and check-in go to the instance too. An account kept with an instance
  that isn't one is asked to sign in again; it is never sent to the public
  hosts.
- The account is named `<email> (<instance>)`, so it is listed apart from
  the same person's public account.
- An enterprise's usage shows as the Enterprise plan.
- **Sign in with Qoder CN** is unchanged and still the first way. An
  account signed in without an instance works as before.

The hosts and reply shapes come from a real VPC account's report
(yetone/magpie#312). This plugin has not been tried with a VPC account.

## The card's name

An account signed in with a phone is shown by that phone — masked, `138****8000` — not by
its `accountId`, which is a uuid. Qoder CN's user info answers the number as `security_mobile`
(measured `13800138000`), so that is what the card takes.

QwenWork's phone accounts answer only the last four digits, as `name`, beside a synthetic
`phone_<uuid>@phone.local` email (measured): the card shows `****8000` and never that email.
An email sign-in keeps its email.

`accountId` stays the account's identity — what magpie keys the user's own name for
it, its proxy, model picks, caps and a gateway key's account list by — so it never
changes: it is what a sign-in and every renewal give back. The card's name is usage's
`user`, a field magpie shows and never keys by.

A sign-in reads the user info, and a renewal reads it again (outside the token lock),
so an account stored by an earlier version shows the phone on the card at its next
renewal. A failed read changes nothing and never costs a sign-in.

## QwenWork (千问办公)

`QwenWork` and `QwenWork 企业版` serve Alibaba's own QwenWork (qwenwork.cn)
on this same protocol, with the desktop client's client id, an RSA key the
Qoder one's equal, its own `qwork` scene, and the device token as the chat
token. The public cloud's sign-in is the desktop app's device flow, with
`redirect_uri=qwenwork-cn://`; usage reads the sign-in's account-context.
A personal account's quota there has `total` and `used` null, only
`remaining`, so the card shows what is left as its balance, with each pool
(daily, monthly, long-term) from `/api/v1/adapter/user/wallets`, as
QwenWork's own client reads them; no share used is made up. An account
with a total keeps its used / total window, and a biz account (or the
enterprise flagship) never asks for the wallets.
There is no PAT and no daily check-in on it: the `pat: false` and
`checkin: false` site fields turn both off, so Qoder's device identity is
never sent there.

The enterprise flagship (企业旗舰版, a VPC / private deployment) serves
web/openapi/api on the enterprise's **own single domain**, and its device
flow sends **no `redirect_uri`** (`/device/selectAccounts` refuses one).
Its sign-in asks for that domain — the host the admin console lives on,
like `your-company.vpc.qwenwork.cn`; `QWENWORK_ENT_DOMAIN` presets it so
the sign-in asks nothing. Every call — chat, models, refresh, usage —
routes to that host, and the account is named `<email|uid> (<domain>)`.
The login page expires in 5 minutes; a member signing in by email OTP
must have their email bound to their account in the admin console, or the
page answers 用户不存在.

The flagship deploys no model-catalog service (`/algo/api/v2/model/list`
answers 503 there), so its list falls back to the public cloud's qwork
models shipped in this package: flash, pro and qwen3.8-max-preview. A 503
falls back; any other error doesn't.

## Daily check-in

Qoder gives credits for a daily claim (the Qoder client's campaign
`CLAIM_BENEFIT`, 100 Credits a day as reported), on both sites. magpie can
claim it for each account when its Qoder check-in switch is on
(Settings), through `auth.checkin`: an already claimed campaign is `done`,
a campaign not available is `inactive`, and a claimable one is `claimed`
with its benefit amount. It asks these pages through this plugin's own
campaigns path (since 0.2.7),
which sends them as the account, on the device token (`Bearer`,
`Cosy-ClientType: 10`) as usage is read; a refused device token is
rotated once and the page asked again.

International campaigns also need Qoder's native device identity:
`Cosy-MachineToken` and `Cosy-MachineType`. Without them, the server can
return HTTP 200 but omit the daily claim. The plugin reads them from
Qoder's own `runtime-info` helper for the signed-in uid, sharing an
in-flight read and caching it in memory for an hour. The same identity
goes on the list, the claim and a device-token retry; it is not saved in
the account's credentials.

- Install Qoder desktop, or sign in to Qoder CLI once, to make its native
  runtime available. The plugin finds the desktop's `resources/umid`
  (`Qoder.app` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Qoder` or, since
  0.2.26, `%ProgramFiles%\Qoder` on Windows, `/opt/Qoder` on Linux) or the runtime the CLI caches in `~/.qoder/.bin`
  (`runtime-info-<platform>-<arch>-*` on macOS and Linux,
  `umid-win32-x64-*\runtime-info.exe` on Windows; `QODER_CONFIG_DIR`,
  `QODER_CLI_HOME` and `QODER_CONFIG_DIR_NAME` move it as they move the
  CLI's folder).
- For another installation location, set `QODER_RUNTIME_INFO` to the
  absolute path of Qoder's installed `runtime-info` executable
  (`runtime-info.exe` on Windows), with its accompanying SDK files.
- With no helper anywhere (a machine that never had Qoder desktop or
  Qoder CLI), the check-in is `ineligible` for the day, with a message
  saying to install one (or set `QODER_RUNTIME_INFO`); magpie asks again
  the next day rather than every 30 minutes (#304). The identity comes
  only from Qoder's own helper: the plugin never makes one up, so such an
  international account gets no daily claim until Qoder is installed.
- A helper that is there but can't be read, or gives an invalid identity,
  is `failed` and asked again later, rather than a false "no activity"
  result.
- With the identity read and sent, a list with no daily claim is
  `inactive`, with a message (since 0.2.32) saying Qoder offered this
  device's identity no daily credits campaign, that Qoder decides that per
  device, and that the credits can be claimed in Qoder desktop when it
  shows them (#304: a Linux CLI identity was offered none while the same
  account's desktop identity was). The plugin never sends another
  device's identity.

Qoder CN (since 0.2.30) sends its own device identity the same way when
Qoder CN is installed: its desktop 0.4.9 and CLI (`qoderclicn`) both ask
Qoder CN's `runtime-info` for environment `0` (the international one is
`3`) and send it on the campaigns pages (yetone/magpie#2911, #304).

- The plugin finds Qoder CN desktop's `resources/umid` (`Qoder CN.app` on
  macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Qoder CN` or `%ProgramFiles%\Qoder CN`
  on Windows, `/opt/Qoder-CN` on Linux) or the runtime its CLI caches in
  `~/.qoder-cn/.bin` (`QODERCN_CONFIG_DIR`, `QODERCN_CLI_HOME` and
  `QODERCN_CONFIG_DIR_NAME` move it). `QODERCN_RUNTIME_INFO` names
  another location; `QODER_RUNTIME_INFO` is only the international one's.
- Without it the requests go out as before, as Qoder CN's desktop does
  when it can't read the identity, and a claim the list still offers is
  made. When the list then offers no daily claim, the check-in is
  `ineligible` for the day with a message to install Qoder CN desktop (or
  sign in to its CLI); a helper that is there but can't be read makes it
  `failed`, asked again later.
- Not tried with a real Qoder CN account: whether Qoder CN now hides the
  daily claim from a request without the identity, as the international
  site does, is inferred from its clients, not seen.

- **List:** `GET <openapi>/sash/api/v1/me/campaigns`: `campaigns[]` with
  `campaignId`, `actionType`, `claimStatus` (`CLAIMABLE`, `CLAIMED`),
  `startAt`, `endAt`, `benefit.amount`.
- **Claim:** `POST <openapi>/sash/api/v1/me/campaigns/{id}/claim`, body
  `{}`: `status` `CLAIMED` (or under `data`).
- `<openapi>` is `openapi.qoder.sh` (Qoder) or `openapi.qoder.com.cn`
  (Qoder CN). Other pages on those hosts are still refused.

**When it is asked (0.2.43).** The daily 100 credits are a campaign of
their own each day, listed from 10:00 (UTC+8) to 09:59 the next day
(`startAt`/`endAt`; the campaign's own text says "Daily reset: 10:00
(UTC+8)", a live list on 2026-10-28). A check-in before 10:00 meets the day
before's campaign: it claims that one if it is still open. Every answer
that knows the window carries `until`, the next campaign's opening (a day
after this one's start, or its end when it runs longer) plus a minute, and
magpie (with `until` support) asks again then, so today's credits are
claimed a minute or two after 10:00 (UTC+8), whatever the computer's time
zone, with nothing to set. Between the old campaign's end at 09:59 and
10:00 the check-in is `failed` with `until` 10:01. An older magpie ignores
`until` and asks once a Beijing calendar day, as before.

Taken from [wallechfox/qoder-checkin](https://github.com/wallechfox/qoder-checkin),
which a user reports works, and Qoder desktop 0.4.3's campaign requests.
International campaign discovery was checked with a real account on
2026-10-08: the native identity exposed the claimable 100 credits, and
omitting either header hid them. This verification only queried the
activity; a live claim was not performed.

## Credits available, but a request is refused

A positive credit balance does not guarantee a queue slot or access to
every model. Use the model ids listed for that particular account and
region. Do not infer another account's permission from its balance.

Qoder code **10605**, including `RESOURCE_LIMIT`, `serviceAvailable` or
`isQueued` details, is a resource/queue answer. Keep its suggested retry
delay; repeatedly signing in does not free that queue. Since **0.2.18**
([#185](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/pull/185)), a 10605 led
by a BOM or wrapped in an outer message is read as busy too; see
[#167](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/issues/167) for the broader report.
That parser fix does not remove the provider's limit or prove that every
live 401 had the same cause. A timeout likewise does not establish an
empty wallet or an expired login.

Since **0.2.28** a queued request waits its turn as Qoder's own client
(Qoder.app 0.4.3's agent worker) waits it: it asks
`/api/v2/service/ask/queue/status` with the request's `requestSetId`, the
model and the plan's `queueType`, at once and then every
`retryAfterSeconds` (held to 0.5–30s, 30s when unsaid), and once
`isQueued` is false it waits that state's `retryAfterSeconds` and sends the
same request again (up to 10 times). Qoder's client waits up to an hour;
the plugin waits at most 4 minutes from the request's start, since nothing
reaches the agent meanwhile (magpie keeps a stream alive with comments for
5 minutes of silence). Three failed status asks in a row, a 404, or a
cancelled request end the wait early. Qoder's client also reports the end
of its turn to `/api/v2/service/ask/finish`; the plugin doesn't, and
Qoder releases that lease on its own TTL. `queue.test.mjs` has the wait.

Since **0.2.40** the wait is only for the last candidate: when magpie says
another account, provider or routing group member follows this request
(its `x-magpie-fallback: 1` header, which the plugin host keeps from Qoder),
a queued request is answered at once with the 503 above, e.g. "Qoder queued
the request for dfmodel (this plan's queue: p3, 3 ahead); try again in
30s", and magpie asks the next instead of keeping the agent in Qoder's
queue.

For a bounded offline reproduction, run `packages/qoder/busy.test.mjs`
from #185 in an isolated temporary HOME. It compares plain queue JSON,
BOM-prefixed JSON and known message wrappers, keeping explicit login and
credit failures distinct. Extracting a JSON body from a translated log
cannot recover the original wire bytes; synthetic wrappers demonstrate
parser behavior, not which wrapper a historical request actually used.
After selecting a local fix with magpie's `plugin use`, confirm which spec
serves `qoder` in `plugin list`; a patched checkout alone does not change
the running provider.


For native check-in, an existing `CLAIMED` result is not a new credit grant.
The host's recheck/cache behavior is tracked in
[magpie#2696](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/2696). Verify a new
claim against the vendor record; a successful activity query alone is not
proof that credits arrived.

## protocol

`export const protocol = { makePlugin, deviceSignIn, openapi, siteOf }` is
the plugin factory and its pieces, for another service on this same
protocol (QwenWork ships here; a future one can too). Its shape is not a
stable API — it changes as the packages on it need.

## Free models when the credits run out

Qoder serves its free models after the credits are used up: "When Credits
run out, you can continue using free basic models, subject to daily and
monthly limits" ([docs.qoder.com/Credits](https://docs.qoder.com/Credits);
the zh page says the same). So the credit windows the usage hook gives
(Qoder and Qoder CN, since 0.2.46) name the account's free models in
`notModels`: a model listed at 0× (not a discount's 0 for a while), from the
account's own model list. magpie then doesn't count those models as spent
on a used-up account, or on a free account's "0 credits left". A list that
can't be read leaves every model counted. QwenWork reads its usage
elsewhere and is not changed.

## Not here

- Qoder's usage and quota display.
- Several accounts at once.
- magpie's web-search stand-in.

## Credits

The protocol (endpoints, COSY envelope, body codec and device flow) comes
from [CLIProxyAPI](https://github.com/ufec/CLIProxyAPI)'s Qoder support, by
way of magpie. Its MIT license is in `LICENSE-CLIProxyAPI`.

@magpie-community/opencode-raccoon-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-raccoon-auth

OpenCode & Magpie provider plugin for **SenseTime Raccoon (商汤小浣熊, `xiaohuanxiong.com`)**.

## Features

- **Sign-in methods**:
  1. Browser OAuth with automatic loopback return: confirm authorization in the browser; no desktop client or pasted code is needed.
  2. Manual callback URL / token fallback (paste `office-raccoon://auth/callback?code=...`, or raw JWT `access_token` / JSON token pair).
  3. Raccoon desktop live session reuse (strictly read-only, reading the `auth.json` the desktop app keeps — `<profile>/agent/config/auth.json` in current builds, where the profile is `~/Library/Application Support/office-raccoon` on macOS and `%USERPROFILE%\.office-raccoon` on Windows, and `~/.box-agent/config/auth.json` in older ones — without writing or spending desktop refresh tokens). A desktop seat keeps the token it was signed in with on its own record, so it is never answered with, and never reports, another account's credentials or credits; once its own token is refused or runs out it asks to be signed in again. The app's own refresh token is still never spent.
- **Token renewal**: single-flight proactive refresh 5 minutes before expiration for browser logins.
- **Dynamic model catalog & credit rates**: real-time synchronization from `/api/web/llm/v2/model_catalog` with context window, output limit, vision/reasoning tags, credit multipliers, and limited-free markers.
- **Usage & allowances**: reports available credits, unexpired grant bills, daily expiration timestamps, and Pro/Free subscription plans.
- **Daily check-in & desktop onboarding grant**: supports Magpie automatic daily check-in (`+300` credits/day) and one-time desktop onboarding grant (`+3000` credits).
- **SSE model rewrite**: transparently rewrites internal upstream model names back to requested downstream models for client compatibility.
- **The card's name**: the account's own phone number (`138****8000`), read once per token from `/api/web/auth/v1/user_info` with the JWT the sign-in holds. `accountId` stays the account's identity (the JWT's `Raccoon-pu-<uuid>`, or the desktop app's name) — magpie keys the user's own name for the account, its proxy, model picks and a gateway key's list by it, so it never changes. The card shows usage's `user`, which is the phone once a sign-in or renewal has read it. A failed read changes nothing and never costs a sign-in.

## 中文

商汤小浣熊（SenseTime Raccoon / `xiaohuanxiong.com`）OpenCode & Magpie 提供商插件。

### 功能特性

- **多种登录方式**：
  1. 浏览器 OAuth 授权登录：确认授权后自动返回，无需安装官方桌面客户端，也无需输入短信验证码或粘贴网页地址。
  2. 手动回调 / Token 备用入口：粘贴 `office-raccoon://auth/callback?code=...` 完整回调链接，或 `access_token` / JSON；普通授权网页地址和单独授权码不能代替完整回调。
  3. 直接只读复用本机商汤小浣熊客户端实时登录态（客户端保存的 `auth.json`：新版在客户端配置目录下的 `agent/config/auth.json`（macOS 为 `~/Library/Application Support/office-raccoon`，Windows 为 `%USERPROFILE%\.office-raccoon`），旧版在 `~/.box-agent/config/auth.json`）。桌面端席位会把登录时读到的 token 保存在自己的账号记录里，因此它不会拿到、也不会**上报**另一个账号的凭据或积分；一旦自己的 token 被拒或用尽，就提示重新登录（客户端自身的 refresh token 依旧不会被动用）。
- **Token 自动续期**：浏览器登录账号过期前 5 分钟自动单飞刷新。
- **动态模型目录与积分倍率**：实时同步 `/api/web/llm/v2/model_catalog`，展示模型上下文、最大输出、视觉/思考能力、积分倍率与限免（`Free`）标识。
- **积分余额与套餐查询**：展示可用积分、未过期发放额度、每日积分过期时间与 Pro/Free 套餐状态。
- **每日签到与桌面端登录奖励**：支持 Magpie 每日自动签到（`+300` 积分/天）及首次桌面端 `+3000` 积分登录奖励领取。
- **SSE 模型名重写**：将上游响应中的内部模型名重写为下游请求的 `model`，确保 Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode 等客户端兼容。

### Browser callback lifecycle

The browser flow uses the authorize page's `desktop_callback=loopback` contract, a random 64-character hex state and `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/auth/callback`. The listener accepts only the matching host, GET path and state. Invalid callbacks leave the pending login intact; success, authorization refusal, exchange failure or the ten-minute deadline close it. A browser page says success only after the code exchange succeeds; response pages contain no code or token and disable caching. Closing/cancelling the host UI does not notify this plugin through the OpenCode callback contract, so an abandoned listener expires at that deadline. When a remote browser cannot reach that machine's loopback, Magpie can forward a pasted final callback URL; the separate manual method remains available as well.

### Desktop seats

The desktop app is signed in to one account at a time and keeps only that account's JWT in `auth.json`. A desktop seat therefore saves the token it was signed in with on its own record and uses it for every request, reading the app only to pick up a newer token for that same account. A seat whose account the app no longer holds is never answered with the app's current token: it keeps using its own until that token is refused, and then asks to be signed in again, rather than being billed to an account it does not name. Adding a seat takes only the account the app holds at that moment.

Note that signing in to a second account in the desktop app **revokes the first account's session on the vendor's side**, so the first seat's token stops being accepted then — its `exp` notwithstanding — and is answered `401 {"code":200003}` by the credits and check-in endpoints, with every refresh endpoint answering 404 for it ([#166](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/pull/166), measured on a real pair of accounts). Two desktop seats are therefore one live account plus one seat waiting to be signed in again, never two working seats. For two accounts that both work, sign in twice through the browser method.

@magpie-community/opencode-river-auth.readme:
# river

River ([river.ai](https://river.ai)) with your API key, in
[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai). River serves an
OpenAI-compatible inference API at `https://api.river.ai/v1`; this plugin signs every
request with your key, so agents reach its models like any other provider —
multi-account, fallback, quotas and all.

**Provider id:** `river`

## Sign-in

A River API key, created on the [API Keys](https://console.river.ai/keys) page of the
River Console (`rv_…`). The key is stored as `{ "type": "api", "key": "rv_…" }` in
OpenCode's `auth.json` and magpie's `plugin-auth.json` (permissions 600); a key River
refuses marks the account for sign-in again.

## Models

The models your key can use, listed per account from `GET /v1/models`. Context and
output limits come from [River's docs](https://docs.river.ai/guides/inference-models/),
prices from [River's public pricing endpoint](https://console.river.ai/api/public/pricing)
(the same rates billing uses), and the documented reasoning efforts
(`reasoning_effort`) from [API controls](https://docs.river.ai/guides/inference-controls/):

| Model | Efforts |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash(-1017) | `none` / `low` / `high` / `max` |
| Kimi-K3 | `none` / `max` |
| Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL | `none` / `high` |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | `low` / `high` / `max` (reasoning required) |
| Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 | `none` / `low` / `medium` / `xhigh` |

Every inference model streams, reasons and calls tools. Image input is limited to
the models the docs list for it (Kimi-K3, DeepSeek ×2, Nemotron, GLM-5.3-Flash,
Qwen3.8-27B-FP8); GLM-5.3 is text-only, and a model the docs don't list yet
defaults to text-only rather than being assumed to see images.

## Usage

River meters a prepaid balance per request and publishes no endpoint that reads it,
so the usage card shows the sign-in state and "Pay as you go" rather than invented
numbers; spend and balance live in the [River Console](https://console.river.ai/).

## Install

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-river-auth
magpie plugin login river
magpie provider test river
```

In OpenCode, add the same package under `plugin` and sign in with `opencode auth login`.

## Development

```sh
bun test
bun scripts/check.mjs river
```

MIT. Not affiliated with River.

@magpie-community/opencode-trae-auth.readme:
# @magpie-community/opencode-trae-auth

Two providers, one package: **Trae CN** (trae.cn, ByteDance's AI IDE, provider
id `trae-cn`) and **Trae Global** (trae.ai, the international deployment,
provider id `trae-global`). Each signs in with its own Trae account, the way
the IDE does, and makes its model requests. The free tier works as well.

The two are separate services — different domains, a different client's
catalog, barely overlapping model lists — so they are two providers rather
than a setting. They share one implementation: the request, stream and
tool-call machinery is the same code, and each realm is a table (hosts,
client, versions, usage page, fallback models, error codes) in `index.mjs`.
A fix to that machinery reaches both.

| Provider id | Signs in to | Endpoints |
|---|---|---|
| `trae-cn` | Trae CN (trae.cn) | `api.trae.cn`, `trae-api-cn.mchost.guru` |
| `trae-global` | Trae international (trae.ai) | `growsg-normal.trae.ai`, `coresg-normal.trae.ai` (SG) / `coreva-normal.trae.ai` (US) |

> **Experimental (both).** The CN protocol was worked out from two
> open-source relays, [wangqi233/trae2api](https://github.com/wangqi233/trae2api)
> and [autumnsentiment/Trae2api-cn](https://github.com/autumnsentiment/Trae2api-cn),
> and the international one from the same relays' realm table. Neither has
> been run against a real account here: Trae CN has not been tried at all, and
> Trae Global has been tried on one Free account in the SG region only — no
> Pro and no US account. Paid-account behaviour (which models a plan lists,
> what its allowance shows) is implemented from the interface's shape, not
> confirmed on a live one. If something fails, open an issue and include the
> error magpie shows.

## Sign-in

One way per provider, **Trae CN account (browser)** or **Trae Global account
(browser)**. The plugin opens that realm's authorization page
(`www.trae.cn/authorization` or `www.trae.ai/authorization`, the IDE's client
`ono9krqynydwx5`). Sign in there and allow the sign-in; the page then sends the
browser back to a callback on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/authorize` — it accepts
no other kind of callback. The callback carries the account's Cloud-IDE-JWT,
refresh token and account. Nothing needs pasting back.

An account of one realm does not sign in to the other: trae.cn's accounts are
not trae.ai's.

At sign-in the plugin creates the account's device and names it to the
authorization page: `device_id` and `machine_id` (32 hex). Every
request then sends that same device. The relays saw requests dropped when the
device was new each time. A Trae CN `device_id` is 16 digits since 0.2.16, the
shape of the ids Trae's device service gives its clients (15 or 16 digits);
Trae Global's stays 19.

### Enterprise (SaaS) accounts

Since 0.2.10 the authorization page also offers Trae's enterprise (SaaS / SSO)
sign-in; before, the plugin asked the page to hide it (`hide_saas_login`), so
an enterprise subscription could only sign in as a personal account. A host
the sign-in names for the account is kept when it is an https host on Trae's
own domains (`trae.cn`, `trae.ai`, `mchost.guru`): a model host other than the
consumer site's own (`www`, `api`, `grow…`) takes the account's model
requests, and a token host the callback names (`authHost`) takes its
renewals. Any other host is ignored and the consumer hosts are used, as for a
personal account, which is unchanged. The account's tenant and login-type
fields are kept with the sign-in; nothing sends them.

**Not tried with a real enterprise account.** Which hosts and fields an
enterprise sign-in sends back is not known yet; if yours doesn't work, open an
issue with what the sign-in page showed.

### The international realm's region

Trae Global has two deployments. The sign-in's `AIRegion` (or a US auth host
such as `api-us-east.trae.ai`) selects the US one; anything else uses the SG
one. The US account's model requests go to `coreva-normal.trae.ai` and its
usage page to `api-us-east.trae.ai`; the SG account uses
`coresg-normal.trae.ai` and `api-sg-central.trae.ai`. Nothing has to be
configured: the region rides in the saved sign-in.

## Requests

Chat completions (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`) are translated for the IDE
agent's `POST https://trae-api-cn.mchost.guru/api/agent/v3/llm_utils_chat`:

- **Request:**
  - The messages go as `{role, content: [{type: "text", text}]}`.
  - The model goes as `config_name` and `model`, and as `model_name` the
    `__dev` model the function's list names for it, when it names one.
  - The function is the one whose model list has the model, the first that
    names a `__dev` model for it (in the order `chat_v3`, the classic IDE's;
    `solo_work_lite`, SOLO's Work mode; `solo_agent`, the TRAE agent's;
    `solo_agent_lite`; `solo_coder`, SOLO's coder roster). If Trae answers
    4001, 4023 or 1005, the plugin tries the others once and remembers which
    one worked.
  - `session_id` is the conversation's, as the IDE keeps one per conversation:
    the session magpie (or OpenCode) names the request by, else the chat's
    first user message, which every later turn repeats, together with the
    account the request is made as. Trae counts a conversation by it, so a
    fresh one per request made one user send that takes several steps (a tool
    result sent back, a retry, another function answering) count as a
    conversation of its own — several rows in the usage detail, each under no
    title. One conversation answered by two accounts (magpie failing over, or
    rotating, inside it) is named twice then, as two conversations, so Trae
    never reads one account's conversation as another's; that costs the two
    halves of such a conversation their single row. `request_id` is the
    request's own, fresh on every one.
- **Headers:** TRAE SOLO CN 0.1.69's (`x-ide-version`/`x-app-version`
  0.1.69, version code 20260917; Trae offers a model only to clients new
  enough for it): `Authorization: Cloud-IDE-JWT …`, `X-Cloudide-Token`,
  `x-app-id`, the device headers and `x-uid`.
- **Answer:** Trae always answers in its own SSE events:
  - `output` gives `response`/`content` and `reasoning_content`/`reasoning`.
    Text under `message`, `delta` or an event with no name is the answer's
    too.
  - `token_usage`, `done` and `error` mark usage, the end and failures.
    What `token_usage` says the prompt cache read and wrote
    (`cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`) goes on under
    those names, and `reasoning_tokens` as
    `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`. DeepSeek's
    `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` and `cached_tokens` are read as cache reads
    too. A `token_usage` that names no cache count at all goes on with
    `magpie_cache_unknown: true`, so magpie shows the cache as unknown,
    not as a 0% miss (0.2.26).
    `done`'s `finish_reason` `length`/`max_tokens` is OpenAI's `length`.
  - Queue events are ignored.
  - A `{"reasoning_content": …}` object written into the text is reasoning,
    and reasoning Trae sends again is sent once.

  The plugin turns these into an OpenAI stream or a single body. A reply
  that fails (an `error` event, or Trae's stream breaking off) ends with the
  error and `[DONE]`, with no finish.
- **Tools:**
  - The tools go natively in `tools`, with `parameters` as a JSON string.
    A past call goes back as the turn Trae made it: an assistant
    `tool_calls` message carrying it (each call
    `{id, type: "function", function_call: {name, arguments}}`) and a
    `tool` message after it answering it. Trae answers such a history with
    native calls; asked for its calls in text instead — a system prompt
    describing a `<tool_call>` block, earlier calls written out as one —
    models write them as blocks, and a block the stream cuts short is an
    error (plugins#38). Trae takes no two messages of one role in a row,
    so an assistant turn's text is folded into the calls turn after it
    and consecutive calls turns join one `tool_calls` list.
  - For a Kimi (Moonshot) model the tools' schemas are first rewritten for
    Moonshot's "moonshot flavored json schema", which Trae's 4027 "tool call
    failed" quotes when it refuses them: an `enum` or `const` with no `type`
    gets the one its values have, a `$ref` beside a `type` and a `type` beside
    an `anyOf` are written as Kimi holds them (the same rules as kimi-work's).
    The request's own tools are not changed, and a schema Kimi takes as it is
    goes byte for byte. Other models' tools go as they are.
  - A call with no name is dropped, and the `tool` result answering it
    with it: Trae requires the name, and an empty `tool_calls` list with a
    result naming no call is not a turn it takes.
  - A result with no text goes as `(no output)` (`(the result's image
    follows)` when it had only an image): Trae refuses the whole request
    with 4027 when a result's text is empty, reading the calls turn as
    unanswered (measured on Trae CN in #251). A result answering no call
    the history sends goes back as text in a `user` turn.
  - A request that names no tools to Trae (none sent, or `tool_choice:
    "none"`, such as a summary) sends its past calls and results as text,
    as before: every live run of the native turns carried the tools.
  - GLM also writes its own template, `<tool_call>name<arg_key>k</arg_key>
    <arg_value>v</arg_value></tool_call>` (a string kept as written, other
    types read as JSON), and sometimes a whole call into a native call's
    name; both are read as the call. A name that holds the wrapper with
    GLM's tags where its service stopped mid-call — `{"name":"bash",
    "arguments":{"command</arg_key><arg_value>ls</arg_value>` — is read too:
    the tags are the service's own handoff, so what stands between them is
    the model's text (a quote left unescaped read as the quote it is, a
    comma inside a value kept, a field's closing tag ending the value before
    it), and the fields the native call did carry are kept beside the ones
    the name's own text fills in. A name whose tool the request doesn't
    have, or one no field can be read from, goes on as written, as any other
    unknown tool does.
  - A block is read as models get it wrong too: every quote escaped
    (`{\"name\":…}`), quotes or backslashes in a string left unescaped, an
    opener with the name as an attribute (`<tool_call name="bash">` with
    `<parameter name="k">v</parameter>`), or JSON that is whole when the
    stream ends without `</tool_call>`. A block that still can't be read,
    or is cut short, is never sent on as the answer: the reply ends with an
    error (a 502 without a stream), so the gateway can try again
    (plugins#38). A `<tool_call>` in backticks or a code fence is text.
  - Kimi and MiMo sometimes write a call in the tags they were trained on:
    Qwen's `<function=name><parameter=k>v</parameter></function>` (bare or
    inside `<tool_call>`), or Anthropic's `<function_calls>` around one or
    more `<invoke name="…"><parameter name="k">v</parameter></invoke>`.
    Each is read as a call, a parameter's value as JSON unless the tool's
    schema says string, and one cut short is an error as above. These
    tags are read only for a tool the request declared; for any other, or
    in backticks or a code fence, they stay text.
  - Calls from either source become OpenAI `tool_calls`. A name matching a
    requested tool but for case or punctuation (`Read`) goes on as the
    request's (`read`); any other goes on as written, so the agent can say
    the tool doesn't exist.
  - Trae requires the message answering a call to follow the call: the
    results of parallel calls go out as consecutive `tool` messages, with
    nothing between them, or the later ones lose their answer (11148).
  - Images: Trae's lists mark each model `multimodal` true or false (the
    Doubao-Seed models, Kimi K3 and K2.6, Qwen 3.7 Plus and MiniMax M3 take
    images; GLM-5 and DeepSeek V4 don't). A model marked true is listed
    as one that takes images, and an image sent to it goes in the
    message's content as an OpenAI `image_url` part beside the text, as
    TRAE's own agent sends one (plugins#161). A model marked false gets
    "[an image, which this model can't see]" in its place. A model whose
    list hasn't been read is sent its images, unless the fallback list
    says it takes none.
    A tool result's images go in a `user` message after the whole run of
    results, not in the `tool` turn: measured on the live endpoint, an
    `image_url` part in a `tool` turn reaches Kimi K2.6 but not
    Doubao-Seed (it answered "Blue"/"Black" to a red image), while the
    user-turn placement is read by both. The results of one turn stay
    consecutive — nothing may go between them (11148) — so the images
    wait for the last of them.

The model list is the account's own, from
`/api/ide/v1/batch_get_detail_param`, every function's list in one ask, as
TRAE SOLO CN asks it (`/api/ide/v1/get_detail_param`, one function at a
time, when the batch gives none). The lists are put together: SOLO and the
TRAE agent list models `chat_v3` doesn't (deepseek-v4.1-flash is the TRAE
agent's, `solo_agent`), and SOLO's coder roster lists models no other chat
function does (`glm-5v-turbo`, `kimi-k2.5`, `minimax-m2.7`,
`qwen-3.6-plus`, each answering through `solo_coder`). Left out are the
IDE's helpers (`usage` other than
`chat_completion`: summary, fast_apply…), configs switched off and the
custom-model slots. Context is the list's `context_window_tokens.dev`,
output the `__dev` model's `max_tokens`. A model with a `__max` model and
a bigger `context_window_tokens.max` is listed again as its Max,
`<id>-max` ("… (Max)"), with that window and the `__max` model's
`max_tokens`; the two can come from different functions' lists (chat_v3
can name the `__max` model, a SOLO list the windows). It asks the
`__max` model through the function that names it, with `max_tokens` set
and `user_message_context.model_info.prompt_max_tokens` the window less
it, as Max mode does. The lists needn't agree on a model's *name*: chat_v3
calls deepseek-v4.1-flash "DeepSeek-V4-Flash 正式版", as it once called
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Official, where the SOLO lists call it
"DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash" (yetone/magpie#681). Trae's usage page books a
request under the name of the list it was served through, so the plugin
takes the name most of a model's lists give — the one Trae's own client is
served under — and asks that model, and its Max, through a list carrying
it. Trae renamed its official entries on 2026-10-09, leaving the name its
lists mostly agree on the only thing that tells a misnamed entry apart.

Reasoning: the models reason, and each entry of the account's list says
which levels it takes — its `reasoning_effort_config`, with the options
(`light`, `high`, `extra_high`) and the default. The request takes the same
names as `reasoning_effort`, so a level an agent picks is sent as Trae
spells it: the plugin offers each model's own levels as `variants`
(`low`/`high`/`xhigh` for `light`/`high`/`extra_high`; `medium` and `max`
keep their names, offered only where the entry names them, as for DeepSeek
V4.1 Flash's `max` in Trae's app), and sends nothing
for a level the model doesn't name, or for a model whose entry names none —
Trae then serves it at its own default. An entry naming levels this map
can't spell offers none, rather than being sent one Trae would reject. A
request that wants levels for a model the list hasn't named reads the list,
and that read is remembered for five minutes whether it produced an entry or
not: a list that fails, or one that doesn't name the model, costs one read
rather than one per request. (A read costs up to two 20s timeouts when Trae's
list endpoint is slow, while the chat itself needs no list to answer.) A read
in flight is shared, not skipped: requests that arrive together — a title
request beside a session's first turn, subagents — ride the one read and all
see what it named, so a Max asked that way is still sent under its base
model's name rather than the agent's own `-max` id. The host's own catalog
refresh rides the same read, so a refresh and a request never ask twice.
A request's read swallows an expiry (the chat can still answer); the
catalog's refresh raises it, so a lapsed account is still marked — including
when the refresh merely rides a read a request started, which is why the lapse
travels on the read's record instead of being thrown from it. The host's
refresh is strict, so it reads again rather than serving a cached lapse: a
re-sign-in is asked afresh instead of being told again that the account lapsed.

The entry kept for a model is the one the request is asked through, and so
the one whose levels the request is held to, so the lists' disagreement
about a model's levels matters: `computer_use_subagent`, for one, is named
with `light`/`high` by `solo_agent` and `solo_agent_lite` and with none by
`solo_work_lite`. The three signals that pick the entry — its `__dev`
model, its not carrying another model's name, its carrying the name the
lists agree on — decide first; of entries that tie on all three, one that
names levels is kept, so a model Trae serves with levels is not left
without them by a sibling entry that names none.

Every model it lists also says it reasons in its `capabilities`
(`reasoning: true`, with `toolcall`, `temperature`, `attachment` and the
input and output modalities), the fallback list's own capabilities kept
where it has an entry: magpie reads `capabilities.reasoning` alone for a
model a plugin lists, and a model without it is shown as one that doesn't
reason (0.2.4).

When no
list can be read, the plugin uses the realm's own fallback list. Trae CN's
`chat_v3` is known to serve GLM-5.2, GLM-5, Kimi K2.6, Qwen 3.7 Plus,
DeepSeek V4 Pro and DeepSeek V4 Flash; Trae Global's serves GPT-5.4,
Gemini 3 Flash, Kimi K2.5, MiniMax M2 and DeepSeek V3.2. The live list
replaces either.

## Renewal

Trae CN (since 0.2.3) renews the JWT as its clients do, bound to the
account's device:

- **Where:** `POST api.trae.cn/trae/api/v3/oauth/ExchangeToken`, with the
  refresh token, the device (`DeviceInfo`: its id, machine id and public
  key) and a `DeviceProof`.
- **The device key:** an ECDSA P-256 key pair made for each account at
  sign-in (or at the first renewal of one signed in before 0.2.3), kept
  with the sign-in.
- **The proof:** the key's ECDSA-SHA256 signature (base64) of
  `POST\n/trae/api/v3/oauth/ExchangeToken\n{ClientID}\n{RefreshToken}\n{Timestamp}\n{Nonce}`.
- **As whom:** TRAE SOLO CN (`en1oxy7wnw8j9n`, `SOLO_PC`) first, then
  Trae CN's IDE (`ono9krqynydwx5`, `IDE_PC`).
- **The refresh token:** kept; this renewal doesn't spend it.

A token the sign-in page gives is renewed this way at once. When Trae
turns the device-bound renewal away, the plugin renews as before 0.2.3.

Trae Global, and Trae CN as a fallback, renew at the realm's auth host's
`/cloudide/api/v3/trae/oauth/ExchangeToken` (`api.trae.cn`,
`growsg-normal.trae.ai`). There Trae issues a new refresh token each time
and spends the old one, so only one renewal runs at a time.

magpie renews the JWT ten minutes before it ends (`refreshLead`) through
`auth.refresh`. Each request also checks it, two minutes before the end, for
OpenCode.

The account is marked for a new sign-in in these cases:

- the refresh token is turned away;
- a request is answered 401, or with a code that means the sign-in lapsed:
  1001 for both realms, and 20101 for Trae Global.

Trae signs other clients out of an account when its token is renewed. The
IDE may therefore ask you to sign in again after magpie renews.

## Errors

| Trae's answer | What the agent gets |
| --- | --- |
| 401 / code 1001 (both), 20101 (Global) | 401, and the account is marked for a new sign-in |
| code 4008 / 1005 (quota, plan; both), 4011 (Global) | 429 |
| Anything else | Trae's message and code, as a 502 or Trae's own status |

## Usage

magpie's usage card shows the account's plan and allowance, from whichever
page the realm bills on:

**Trae CN** — the credits page:

- **Source:** `api.trae.cn/trae/api/v2/pay/ide_user_ent_usage`.
- **What it adds up:** each entitlement pack's `credits_limit` (-1 means
  unlimited) and what the pack has used.
- **What it shows:** one Credits window: the credits used of the packs'
  total, with the share, which magpie shows as used or left like
  WorkBuddy's.

**Trae Global** — the dollar billing's entitlements:

- **Source:** `POST api-sg-central.trae.ai/trae/api/v1/pay/user_current_entitlement_list`
  (a US account asks `api-us-east.trae.ai`).
- **What it adds up:** the pack's allowance in dollars
  (`basic_usage_limit` plus `bonus_usage_limit`) and what was used of each
  (`basic_usage_amount`, `bonus_usage_amount`).
- **What it shows:** one Dollar Usage window, the dollars used of the
  allowance, resetting when the pack ends.

A 200 carrying an error code is shown as Trae's own message rather than as
an empty answer.

## Daily check-in

Trae CN gives credits for a daily check-in (每日签到); Trae Global has no
such page, so this is CN only. magpie can press it
once a day for each account (Settings, or the switch on the usage card),
through `auth.checkin`: `claimed` when the status says today's is in after
the claim, `done` when it said so before it, `inactive` when the page is
disabled, `ineligible` when the claim answers 9095 (this device has
checked in today) or 9074 (Trae did not take it for this account's
device) or answers code 0 while the read-back still says the day is out,
and `failed` for a turned-away sign-in or any answer that got nowhere,
which is tried again later that day. An `ineligible` is the day's answer:
magpie asks that account no more until tomorrow, and only reads its
status.
It asks Trae CN's own pages through
this plugin's fetch, which sends them as the account, as Trae CN's IDE
(3.3.104) sends them: its Cloud-IDE-JWT (renewed first when near its
end), its device (`x-device-id`, `x-device-brand`, `x-device-type`,
`x-os-version`, `x-app-version`) and a client's User-Agent (TRAE SOLO
CN's Electron shell). Since 0.2.1: Bun's own User-Agent and the chat's
headers got 9074 「当前参与用户太多，请稍后再试」 every time
(yetone/magpie#808). Since 0.2.3 the JWT is also bound to the device (see
Renewal): a JWT renewed at `/cloudide/…` carries no device, and the claim
answered it 9074 even with the client's headers.

- **Status:** `POST api.trae.cn/trae/api/v2/ug/checkin_credits/status`,
  body `{"req_source":1}` (magpie's `{}` is sent as that): `enable`,
  `checked_in`, `credits`.
- **Claim:** `POST api.trae.cn/trae/api/v2/ug/checkin_credits/claim`,
  the same, only while it is on and today's isn't in.
- **The device, when Trae CN's own client is here (0.2.14):** the
  account this machine's Trae CN desktop client is signed in as checks in
  on the client's own device, the one Trae's device service registered:
  `x-device-id` is the id in the client's
  `globalStorage/storage.json` key `iCubeAuthInfo://icube-dc:<id>`,
  `x-device-type` and `x-os-version` are this machine's, and no
  `x-device-brand` is sent. The account is matched by the `userId` in the
  client's sign-in (`iCubeAuthInfo://icube.cloudide`, plain JSON or the
  client's fixed codec, as dingminhua/dsh-connect-trae reads it). The file
  is only read: nothing in it is written, and the client's token is never
  used. On one account the client's claim went through while the
  plugin's, on its own device, got 9074 (yetone/magpie#808, #1920); that
  this header is what changes it hasn't been tried on a real account
  yet. Every other account keeps its own device, and a file that can't be
  read or made out, or holds no single device, changes nothing.
- **Every profile is read (0.2.21):** a machine can hold more than one
  Trae CN client profile — the IDE's and TRAE SOLO CN's each write their
  own `storage.json`, and each names the account that profile is signed in
  as, with that account's device. So every profile is read and the one
  signed in as the account answers with its device, which is how two
  accounts can each check in on a real client's device. Before, only the
  first profile was read and it decided for all of them: a second
  account's own profile was never seen, and one profile signed in as
  someone else (or one file that didn't parse) hid every profile after it.
  A profile that isn't signed in as the account, or that names no single
  device, is passed over rather than ending the search. Files: macOS
  `~/Library/Application Support/Trae CN/…` and `…/TRAE SOLO CN/…`, Windows
  `%APPDATA%\Trae CN\…`, `…\TRAE SOLO CN\…` (or `trae-cn`), Linux
  `~/.config/trae-cn/…`, `…/Trae CN/…`, `…/TRAE SOLO CN/…`. The IDE's
  folder has been seen in a real install (macOS and Windows); TRAE SOLO
  CN's name and its `iCubeAuthInfo://` keys are read as the same client
  of the same realm writes them, which hasn't been checked against real
  files — harmless if they differ, since a folder that isn't there, or a
  key that isn't named, is simply not read. A client started with its own
  `--user-data-dir` is not found: there is no list of those to read.
- **Every other account's device (0.2.16):** its own device id, in the
  client's shape. Trae CN answered a claim on the plugin's 19-digit id
  9074, while the same account and token on a 16-digit id were taken
  (magpie-community/plugins#194). An account signed in since 0.2.16 has a
  16-digit id and checks in on it. One signed in before checks in on a
  16-digit id made from its own device id and uid: the same id every day,
  never rotated, and no other account's. Its chat requests and renewals
  keep the 19-digit device it signed in with.
- **What comes back:** Trae's answer as it is. A 401 or code 1001 marks
  the account for a new sign-in. Code 9095 means this device has checked
  in today, and that holds for the day. Code 9074 means Trae did not take
  the claim for this account's device: its own words say the pool is busy,
  which two measurements do not bear out — the same account, token and
  headers were taken on a 16-digit id where a 19-digit one got 9074
  (plugins#194), and on 2026-10-23 the same account and headers were taken
  on a device id Trae had never seen while this account's own id answered
  9074. The message says so, and does not send people to Trae CN's app,
  which is not where the problem is. Signing the account in to a Trae CN
  client on this machine is the one thing seen to change a 9074, but it
  hasn't been tried on a real account, so it isn't named in the message;
  nor is it named when the claim already rode a client's device, where it
  would only tell the user to do what they did. No device id is ever
  changed or rotated to get round a 9095 or a 9074, and no account is
  given another account's device or its own client's device unless a
  client is signed in as that account.
- **Which device, said (0.2.25):** a 9074 or 9095 message ends with
  the device the claim went on: this machine's Trae CN client's, signed in
  as the account, or magpie's own for it, with how many client profiles
  were found and that none is signed in as the account. A client device
  that another profile, signed in as another account, also has is said
  too: both accounts check in on one device, which Trae takes once a day.
  No uid or device id is named. On plugins#436 two accounts shared one
  machine whose two profiles (`Trae CN`, `TRAE SOLO CN`) were both the
  first account's; it checked in and the second got 9074, which took
  running `clientDevice` by hand to explain. A profile started with its
  own `--user-data-dir` is not read, and there is no reason to: on
  2026-10-29 TRAE CN 3.4.4 (Windows 11) kept a second account's sign-in
  apart in such a folder but gave it the same device id as the default
  folder, and the client itself said 「本设备今日已签到」 for that
  account. The check-in is counted per device, so on one machine only the
  first account to check in gets the day's credits; the others' usage,
  models and requests are unaffected (plugins#436, closed as not
  planned).
- **A claim's code 0 is not the answer (0.2.22):** Trae answers a
  claim code 0 for one that registered nothing, so the status is read back
  after every claim and only a day that is in is reported as `claimed`.
  Since 0.2.22 one that isn't is an `ineligible` — the day's answer, not a
  `failed` to be tried again: a `failed` is retried with backoff for the
  rest of the day and each retry is another claim, which for an account
  Trae keeps answering code 0 would turn one claim a day into many, and a
  status that lags a claim that did land would read as not in once and
  claim again. Nothing is claimed again that day; the status alone is
  read, so a lag that catches up is still reported as `done`. The credit a
  claim granted is its `credits`, or its `extra_credits` when it names
  only that; Trae CN's claim usually names neither
  (`{"code":0,"message":"success"}`), and then the read-back's `credits`
  is the credit. The two are never added: the status carries
  `extra_credits` beside `credits` (100 and 100 on a real account) while
  the day gives 100.

Only `api.trae.cn`'s `/trae/api/` pages are sent this way; any other URL
that isn't a chat request is still refused (400). Needs 0.1.4 or later.
