# Agent Office · 我的 Agent 在干嘛

[![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/QingJ01/magpie-agent-office)](https://github.com/QingJ01/magpie-agent-office/releases)
[![magpie ≥ 0.1.1318](https://img.shields.io/badge/magpie-%E2%89%A5%200.1.1318-4f46e5)](https://usemagpie.ai)
[![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-167%20passing-22a35a)](#test)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)

**一个住在 magpie 窗口里的实时 Agent 办公室。** 直接读取各 Agent 自己的会话记录，把正在思考、执行工具、等待批准或已经完成的工作，变成真 3D 办公室里的小人；也可以切到等距画布、俯视 2D 或分组列表。

A live activity dashboard for your coding agents inside [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai). Every session becomes a worker in a real WebGL office, an isometric canvas room, or a grouped workbench — driven by the agent's own session files, not guesses from network traffic.

![Agent Office in magpie's window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QingJ01/magpie-agent-office/main/docs/in-magpie.png)

![The real 3D office, six scenes, orbit camera](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QingJ01/magpie-agent-office/main/docs/office-3d.png)

## 快速开始 · Quick start

**magpie 插件（推荐）**

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/page-agent-office
```

安装后打开 **插件 › Agent 办公室**。第一次没有会话时会看到空办公室；想预览完整效果，可在 **设置 › 示例 Agent** 临时打开示例。

**独立运行（没有 magpie 时）**

```sh
bun bin/agent-office.mjs          # 本地页面，默认 127.0.0.1:4545
bun bin/agent-office.mjs --json   # 一次性快照，适合让 Agent 在聊天里汇报
```

独立服务会打印带随机访问令牌的完整 URL，请用该 URL 打开；固定的 `/live.js` 和数据 API 不公开。服务拒绝不匹配的 Host、跨站请求和缺少同源 Origin 的写入。端口占用时会报错，可用 `--port 0` 自动选择空闲端口。

仓库也带 `SKILL.md`，可放进 Claude Code / Codex 的 skills 目录，用 `/agent-office` 启动。

### 主要功能

- **真 3D（WebGL）**：等距相机、拖拽旋转、滚轮缩放、实时光照与阴影；办公室、空间站、咖啡店、城堡、海盗湾、幽灵谷六种程序化场景。
- **ISO / 2D**：不依赖 WebGL 的等距画布与俯视图；相机拖拽、滚轮缩放、昼夜窗光、办公室猫和五个活动点。

![The isometric canvas office, with venues and the cat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QingJ01/magpie-agent-office/main/docs/office-iso.png)
- **分组工作台**：按 **需要你 → 工作中 → 已结束** 分组；可按 Agent、子 Agent、摸鱼 Agent 过滤。
- **今日面板**：今天的轮次、tokens、按 Agent 与目录汇总，以及上下文使用率条（60% 黄、85% 红）。

![Today usage and context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QingJ01/magpie-agent-office/main/docs/today.png)
- **最近对话**：点击 Agent 查看任务、当前步骤、最近消息、模型、目录、上下文和续接命令。
- **页内提醒**：新出现的「需要你」或错误会在页面右下角弹出提示；标题栏显示需要你的数量。magpie 的 iframe 没有系统通知权限，所以不调用浏览器通知。
- **9 种语言**：English、简体中文、繁體中文、日本語、한국어、Español、Français、Deutsch、Português。自动按最近提问的语言选择，也可手动指定。
- **画中画**：可拖动、可缩放的页内悬浮小窗，✕ 或 Esc 放回。

## 支持哪些 Agent

直接读取会话文件：

| Agent | 文件 |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl`（以及 `subagents/*.jsonl`；`sessions/*.json` 只用来判断进程是否还在） |
| Codex | `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`（+ `session_index.jsonl`） |
| Copilot CLI | `~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl` |
| Kimi Code | `~/.kimi-code/sessions/*/*/agents/*/wire.jsonl` |
| DeepSeek Harness | `~/.dsh/sessions/*/*/session.v4.jsonl[.zstd]` |
| Gemini CLI · Qwen Code | `~/.gemini/tmp/*/chats/session-*`, `~/.qwen/tmp/*/chats/session-*` |
| Pi · omp | `~/.pi/agent/sessions/*/*.jsonl`, `~/.omp/agent/sessions/*/*.jsonl`，以及 `~/.omp/profiles/*/agent/sessions` |
| Grok Build | `~/.grok/sessions/*/*/updates.jsonl` + `summary.json` |
| Qoder · WorkBuddy · CodeBuddy | 各自的 `projects/*/*.jsonl`（Claude Code 格式） |

`*_HOME` / `*_CONFIG_DIR` 覆盖变量都支持。Claude 子 Agent、Kimi 子 Agent、Grok 子 Agent 会标为子 Agent，并带父会话；OMP profiles 带 profile 名。其他 Agent（Cursor、OpenCode、Copilot 等）在通过 magpie 的模型工作时，仍会由异步网关钩子看到。

## 状态与办公室

| 状态 | 在哪里 | 标记 |
|---|---|---|
| Thinking · 思考中 | 工位 | … |
| Running tools · 执行中 | 工位，屏幕亮着 | 工具名、已运行时间 |
| Replying · 回复中 | 工位 | 正在写入的回复 |
| Waiting for you · 等你回应 | 紫色区域，挥手 | **!** |
| Done · 已完成 | 沙发、书架、咖啡台、乒乓球、街机、白板或电话亭 | ✓ / 摸鱼 |
| Error · 错误 | 故障终端 | × |

工作 8 分钟没有新动静标 **No progress**，工具运行 10 分钟标 **No progress · 10m**，仍留在「工作中」；20 分钟后的完成会话进入摸鱼状态。办公室有五个活动点、可撸的猫、随本地时间变化的窗光，以及可拖拽缩放的相机。

## 怎么知道

每个 Agent 自己写在本机的会话文件是唯一事实来源。host 每 1.5 秒读取变化，页面每秒加载一次 `page/live.js`：

- 工具有调用没结果 → **执行中**
- 请求批准 / 提问（Codex、DSH、Gemini、Kimi 等）→ **需要你**
- 本轮结束 → **完成**；中断 → **已结束**；错误 → **错误**
- 会话文件 8 / 10 分钟没动 → **No progress**

通过网关看到、没有本地文件的 Agent，按请求推断；它不会因为一次请求结束就冒充「完成」。hook 返回空 body，不修改任何请求。

**它会读取什么：** 本机的会话文件，包括提问、回复、工具命令、最近 8 条消息和用量字段，并在插件目录生成 `page/live.js`。设置里关闭「显示提问和回复」后只保留状态与工具名，不写入提问、回复、消息或命令参数；配置读不到时默认关闭文本（fail closed）。

## 隐私

- 只读本机 Agent 会话；默认只看最近两天、最多 40 个会话，CLI 可放到 200 个。
- `live.js` 保存在插件自己的目录，不发送到任何地方；页面 `permissions` 为空，不读 magpie 的会话 API。
- `text:false` 同时由 host 和页面执行：标题回退到目录名，步骤只留工具名，最近对话整段清空。即使 `live.js` 是旧的，页面也不会把被关闭的文本画出来。
- 独立 CLI 只监听 `127.0.0.1`；`--private` 与插件里的开关等价。

## 设置

```json
{
  "mode": "office",
  "dim": "3d",
  "scene": "office",
  "quality": "medium",
  "demo": false,
  "showDone": true,
  "hideAfter": "6h",
  "text": true,
  "agents": [],
  "showSub": true,
  "showIdle": true,
  "side": true,
  "lang": "auto",
  "remote": false
}
```

| Key | |
|---|---|
| `mode` | `office` 或 `list` |
| `dim` | `3d`（WebGL）、`iso`（等距画布）或 `2d`（俯视） |
| `scene` | `office`、`station`、`cafe`、`castle`、`pirate`、`graveyard` |
| `quality` | `low`、`medium`、`high`（3D 阴影与 DPR） |
| `showDone` | 保留已完成的 Agent |
| `hideAfter` | 完成后多久离开：`1h`、`6h`、`24h`、`never` |
| `text` | 保留提问、回复和最近对话（`false`：只留状态与工具名） |
| `agents` | 只显示这些 Agent；空数组为全部 |
| `showSub` / `showIdle` | 显示子 Agent / 摸鱼 Agent |
| `side` | 显示分组侧栏 |
| `lang` | `auto` 或九种语言代码 |
| `cleared` | { 会话 key: 时间 }：被「清除」的会话，文件再动就回来 |
| `remote` | 网关部分也记录其他电脑的请求 |
| `approvalAfterSec` | 只有网关记录时，工具运行多久算等你批准（90） |

## 独立 CLI

```sh
bun bin/agent-office.mjs [--port 4545] [--hours 48] [--private] [--json] [--no-open]
```

`--json` 输出与页面相同的快照，方便 Agent 在聊天里总结；不带 `--json` 时启动同一个页面，数据来自同一个扫描器。需要 Bun（DSH 的 zstd 解码用到 `Bun.zstdDecompressSync`）。

## What it cannot know

- **完全不读文件、也不经过 magpie 的 Agent**：没有任何记录。
- **逐 token 的模型进度**：会话文件按消息写入，回复中只表示文件在动。
- **系统通知**：magpie 的页面 iframe 没有通知权限，本插件用页内提示取代。
- **超过 40 个会话 / 两天**：默认不进入页面；CLI 可调大。
- **3D 需要 WebGL**：不可用时自动退回 ISO 画布，功能不丢。

## Files

- `lib/readers.mjs` — 各 Agent 会话格式转成状态、步骤、消息、用量；无 I/O。
- `lib/scan.mjs` — 找到会话文件，只重读变化；支持子 Agent、OMP profiles、DSH zstd 节流。
- `lib/track.mjs` — 网关请求 / 回复的推断；无 I/O。
- `office.hooks.mjs` — 插件 host：每 1.5 秒扫描、看网关请求、写 `page/live.js`。
- `page/model.js` — 状态、分组、过滤、Today、九语言、续接命令、隐私裁剪。
- `page/scene.js` — Canvas 等距 / 2D 办公室、五个活动点、猫、相机、昼夜。
- `page/scene3d.js`, `page/three.min.js` — WebGL 真 3D、六场景、光照阴影；three.js r169，MIT。
- `page/app.js`, `page/index.html`, `page/style.css`, `page/icons.js`, `page/icons/` — 页面、面板、侧栏、提醒和图标。
- `bin/agent-office.mjs`, `SKILL.md` — 没有 magpie 时的独立页面、`--json` 和 skill 包装。

## Test

```sh
bun test
```

167 项测试覆盖会话解析（含新客户端）、隐私、路径与朝向、沙发合成、2D 活动点、相机、昼夜、3D API、CLI 与独立服务。3D 回归测试执行随包 THREE 的真实场景、几何、动画和矩阵路径，仅替换 GPU 边界；另有真实 magpie 页面宿主的浏览器回归脚本 `test/browser.mjs`，覆盖 Retina 窄视口、菜单边界、标签碰撞、切换与关闭文本后的 DOM。

```sh
# 可选浏览器测试（另行安装 Playwright 与浏览器，先启动 magpie web）
OFFICE_PLAYWRIGHT=/path/to/playwright/index.mjs \
OFFICE_HOST_URL="http://127.0.0.1:4571/?k=YOUR_LOCAL_KEY" bun test/browser.mjs
```

在 macOS 15.7.9（24G830，arm64）、Playwright 1.56.1 的 WebKit 26.0（build 2215）上，测试的无协议数字主机 CSP 源会阻止脚本加载，补全 `http://` 后同一 sandbox 内可执行。维护者使用 Linux WebKit build 2336 未复现，因此这不是对所有 WebKit / Safari 的结论；原生 Safari / WKWebView 未自动化测试。受影响的 Mac 环境可显式设置 `OFFICE_NORMALIZE_WEBKIT_CSP=1`，仅规范化测试响应里的协议，保持原域名、目录白名单和 sandbox。可用 `OFFICE_PLAYWRIGHT=/path/to/playwright/index.mjs bun test/webkit-csp.mjs` 收集本机版本、实际 CSP 和控制台错误；详见 [后续验证](docs/follow-up-validation.md)。

JSONL 首次打开会重放一次，后续轮询保留字节偏移、UTF-8/JSON 分帧和各 reader 的解析状态，只解析追加的完整记录。截断、替换和同尺寸重写会重建状态；每次增长额外检查最多 128 字节的前缀/旧末尾，识别常见的两次轮询间截断再增长。未变化时不读取日志。metadata/usage sidecar 仅在其版本变化时重读；Codex 标题索引也采用追加游标。

可用合成数据复现实测（不会读取真实会话或调用模型）：

```sh
bun scripts/bench-scan.mjs 100 1 # 一份 100 MiB 日志
bun scripts/bench-scan.mjs 100 4 # 四份并发日志
bun scripts/bench-scan.mjs 100 1 1 # 每 30 条文本后包含 1 MiB base64 图片
```

普通 JSONL 按追加日志处理；任意修改中部、同时保留 inode 与两处检查片段又增长的非追加编辑无法在不重读整个文件的前提下完整识别。初次读取或重建仍有 O(文件大小) 成本，但完整记录即使跨读取块也直接解析，只有 EOF 未完成的记录需要词法分帧。完整 JSON 文档、压缩 DSH 和发生变化的 usage sidecar 仍按各自快照格式读取。

修改页面资源后运行 `bun scripts/stamp-page.mjs` 更新内容指纹；`--check` 可验证没有旧指纹。画质切换调整像素比和阴影，抗锯齿在 WebGL 上下文创建时固定。人物使用 InstancedMesh 批量绘制，保留四肢动画与各 Agent 颜色。

## Prior art

The office metaphor and several interaction ideas were inspired by
[**whatsmyagentdoing**](https://github.com/Charonyuu/whatsmyagentdoing) by
[Charonyuu](https://github.com/Charonyuu) — a standalone Claude Code / Codex
skill that renders a live 3D office in the browser. It is an independent
project under the MIT license; this plugin is a magpie-native implementation
with its own renderer, session readers and privacy model. Thanks to its author
for showing how much life a small office can have.

## License

MIT. The bundled three.js is MIT; see the notice in `page/three.min.js` and
`page/scene3d.js`.

@magpie-community/page-chat.readme:
# @magpie-community/page-chat

A chat page in [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai)'s window. Talk to magpie's own models with your MCP servers, instructions and skills, with images and LaTeX, without starting an agent.

Made by **Magic_zero** ([Magiczerowxy](https://github.com/Magiczerowxy)), from [Magiczerowxy/magpie-chat](https://github.com/Magiczerowxy/magpie-chat) (0.1.21). This package is that code, with the changes listed under [Changes from the original](#changes-from-the-original).

![Chat inside magpie's window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Magiczerowxy/magpie-chat/main/screenshots/23-math-and-layout.png)

## Install

From magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or:

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/page-chat
```

It then has a tab, **Chat** (对话, 對話, チャット), under Plugins in the sidebar.

## What it does

- **magpie's models.** The list comes from the gateway's `/v1/models`. Models with reasoning levels get an effort picker. Each model shows its brand icon (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, MiniMax and more) in the picker and next to its name in the transcript. The icons come from [@lobehub/icons](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-icons) (MIT); see `chat/icons/models/NOTICE`.
- **magpie's library.** Tick instructions and skills from `~/.config/magpie/library/` (folded into the system prompt), and MCP servers from `library.json` (their tools run as real `tool_calls`, at most 8 rounds, Streamable HTTP and stdio). The switch "使用 magpie 的全部 MCP 服务器" at the top of the MCP list uses every server in the library instead, one added to magpie later too; it is off by default, and turning it off brings back the servers you ticked. magpie's own MCP servers (web search, image recognition, image generation, plugin tools) are in the list beside the library's while they are on in magpie (asked of the gateway's `/v1/magpie/mcp`, magpie v0.1.2397 and later; an older magpie lists none); one turned off in magpie's Settings is left out, and a library server of the same name, such as an installed `magpie-image`, is used in its place.
- **Images and files.** Pick, drop or paste them. Images go to the model as `image_url`. Replies can carry base64 data-URI images, which render inline and open full size on click. Remote `![alt](https://…)` images are shown as a link instead of being loaded — fetching them automatically would let a reply make the page request an arbitrary URL.
- **Streaming.** Reasoning unfolds while it arrives, then collapses. While the answer streams, the page follows it down unless you scroll up yourself; scroll back to the bottom and it resumes.
- **Model status.** Every reply ends with a line saying what the model is doing: `Magpie正在觅食ing… · 2s` with a running timer while it generates, green `Magpie找到了食物！ · 2s` when done, red `Magpie没有找到食物` on failure. The elapsed time is kept with the conversation.
- **Math.** `$…$`, `$$…$$`, `\(…\)` and `\[…\]` render with a bundled KaTeX 0.16.11. No CDN.
- **Conversations kept**, pinned, renamed or deleted, under `~/.config/magpie/magpie-chat/`. Clicking "+" starts a draft row in the sidebar; it becomes a real conversation as soon as you send, and disappears if you switch away without writing anything. The pencil button on each row renames it inline.
- **Layout.** Conversation width and composer width are adjustable in the sidebar; a **Sync** switch keeps the two equal — move either one and the other follows.
- **System prompt switch.** The text you write under 系统提示词 can be turned off without deleting it; ticked instructions and skills still apply.
- **Looks like magpie.** Colors and fonts come from the window's theme.

It registers no provider, asks for no sign-in and stores no credentials of its own. Every request goes out through magpie's gateway, so usage, routing and failover are the same as an agent's.

## How it works

A plugin page runs in a sandboxed frame with no network (`connect-src 'none'`). Its only way out is to navigate itself. So this plugin has two parts:

1. `page/index.html` and `page/boot.js`: a launcher magpie hosts. It reads the window's theme and the `port` option through `_magpie/bridge.js`, then sends its frame to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`. It makes no request of its own.
2. `index.mjs`: an OpenCode v1 plugin (`export default {id, server}`). When magpie's plugin host calls `server()`, it starts a local service on `127.0.0.1:3477` (the `port` option). `lib/server.mjs` serves the chat UI in `chat/` and `/api/*`, and forwards chat to magpie's gateway.

### What the service reads and sends

- From magpie's config folder (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/magpie` or `~/.config/magpie`): `caller-keys.json` (the first gateway key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer` to the gateway, so the chat's usage is counted on that key), `providers.json` and `routing.json` (icons), `settings.json` (fonts, and the gateway `port` when the build writes one there), `library.json` and `library/` (MCP servers, instructions, skills).
- To magpie's gateway: `MAGPIE_CHAT_GATEWAY` if set, else `MAGPIE_ADDR`, else the `port` from magpie's `settings.json` (the portable build writes its real port there, e.g. `18086`), else `http://127.0.0.1:3425`. The key goes there, so set `MAGPIE_CHAT_GATEWAY` only to a gateway you trust.
- To your MCP servers: what the model asks their tools, with the headers you configured for them. A stdio server's command is run as you configured it. magpie's own MCP servers are on the gateway, and get the gateway key.

### Who can use the service

Only the chat page it served:

- Every `/api/` route needs `x-magpie-chat-token`, a random token made each time the service starts. The service writes it into the chat page's HTML, which it sends without CORS headers, so another page can't read it. `/api/ping`, `/api/fonts.css` and `/api/icon/*` are open; they give nothing secret.
- `Host` must be `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`, so a DNS-rebound page is turned away.
- `Origin` must be `null` (the sandboxed frame) or the service's own.

## Options

```json
{ "port": 3477 }
```

The launcher and the service both read it. Change it if something else holds 3477.

## Starting it without magpie's host

`serve.mjs` (`node serve.mjs`, or `start-server.cmd` / `start-server.vbs` on Windows) starts the same service on its own, and `install-autostart.cmd` puts it in Windows' Startup folder. See [SERVE.md](SERVE.md). None of these runs unless you start it.

## Changes from the original

- The service answered `Origin: null` and requests with no Origin, and didn't check `Host`. Any website's sandboxed iframe sends `Origin: null`, so it could chat on your gateway key, read and change conversations and settings, and drive your MCP tools. A DNS-rebound page could read conversations. The token and the Host check above close it.
- The service started when `index.mjs` was imported, on 3477 whatever the `port` option said, while the launcher went to the option's port. It now starts when the host calls `server()`, on the option's port.
- A remote provider icon answered 302 with no `Location`. It has one.
- `/api/bootstrap` said version `0.1.0` whatever the version. It says the package's.

## Known limits

- The page opens the service on this computer's 127.0.0.1, so `magpie web` used from another machine won't reach it.
- MCP has no legacy GET SSE stream and no reconnect.
- Images go inline as base64, at most 24MB each.
- Built-in provider icons live inside magpie's binary; when one can't be read, the service draws a letter badge.

## Test

```sh
bun test packages/chat
```

The test starts the service on a free port against a fake gateway, in a temporary config folder.

## License

MIT, © 2026 Magiczerowxy. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

@magpie-community/page-fingerprint.readme:
# Magpie Fingerprint

[简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie) · [lm-detector](https://github.com/Ikaleio/lm-detector)

Investigate suspected model substitution directly in Magpie. Compare numeric
response fingerprints across providers or repeat a run after a service changes.
The page reuses Magpie’s configured models and gateway; the pinned
`lmfpd-sdk` detector ranks nearby reference-bank models. Rankings are evidence
for investigation, not proof of model identity.

![Fingerprint workspace (explicit demo data)](docs/preview.png)

- Select up to 24 models across providers, with the same three challenges per batch.
- Reuse Magpie authentication and native endpoint metadata; optionally pin an account.
- Follow live sample counts, cancel work, and inspect the actual response route.
- Compare ranked candidates, including partial and unscorable outcomes.
- Keep raw replies and data versions in local history; export or copy JSON.
- Magpie's native page bridge, controls and design tokens; follows the host's theme and language.
- Compact model lists, keyboard-accessible view tabs, and narrow-screen layouts.

## Install

Install **Fingerprint** from **Plugins → Discover**, or use the CLI. Requires
a current Magpie release with `page.service` support and Bun 1.4.2+:

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/page-fingerprint
```

Open **Fingerprint** in the sidebar, or choose **Fingerprint** from a provider's menu.
Starting a detection sends three requests per selected model and uses that provider's quota.

## Development

Run these commands from `packages/fingerprint/`. Source, tests and the built
`dist/` assets are checked in. Installation and the offline tests do not need
package downloads: `vendor/lmfpd-sdk` pins the MIT SDK at 0.2.0. Only rebuilding
the UI and running the type checker require the development dependencies.
Direct build-tool versions are exact in `package.json`; `bun.lock` fixes the
complete dependency graph using `registry.npmjs.org`. Builds use Bun 1.4.4.
There are no install/pack lifecycle scripts. After a source change, rebuild
and commit the resulting `dist/` files.

The standalone project and release history are at
[KaranocaVe/magpie-fingerprint](https://github.com/KaranocaVe/magpie-fingerprint).

```sh
bun run rebuild
bun start
```

`rebuild` installs with `--frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` in an isolated
copy, runs typecheck/tests/build, and copies `dist/` back. This avoids Bun
resolving the parent monorepo's workspaces; its temporary directory is removed
on completion. In a standalone copy of this package, `bun install
--frozen-lockfile --registry https://registry.npmjs.org` and `bun run check`
produce the same build.

The plugin page service listens on `3488` by default and uses Magpie's gateway
at `http://127.0.0.1:3425`. Opening or refreshing the page never downloads
reference data. **Download reference data** explicitly fetches a fresh snapshot;
starting a run downloads one only when no usable snapshot is cached. There is
no background refresh. The default primary source is
`https://lm.ikale.io/data/`; its fallback is
`https://cdn.jsdmirror.com/npm/lmfpd-data@latest/`. These hosts see the client's
IP address. Reference downloads carry no provider credentials, model ids,
prompts or replies. Only an explicitly started job sends sampling prompts
through the configured gateway. See [integration.md](integration.md) for gateway
authentication, `magpie web`, environment variables, local reference sources,
and the explicit `--demo` fixture.

## Scope and limits

The first release supports numeric fingerprinting. Each run retains its loaded
reference snapshot and records its `builtAt` value. The remote reference data
is not version-pinned or authenticated by a locally pinned hash; the fallback
uses `@latest`. Runs use three shared challenges per batch, bounded work, and
cancellation. It records proposed, observed, and failed evidence separately;
it does not prove provider identity, authenticate a model, or infer hidden
tokenizers. `--demo` runs an isolated illustrative workflow without model calls.

Magpie middleware and protocol adapters still apply. A changed actual provider/model
invalidates that target's aggregate score. Account pinning is optional; it does not
turn a routed channel into an upstream identity guarantee. Tokenizer probing is deferred.

MIT licensed. Third-party notices are in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

# @magpie-community/page-usage

A page in [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai)'s window with your usage at a glance. It shows calls, errors, tokens and cost for today, 7 days or 30 days, and the models that took them.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/page-usage`. It then has a tab, **Usage glance** (titled in the window's language: 用量速览, 用量速覽, 使用量の概要, Nutzung im Überblick), under Plugins in the sidebar, in the app and in `magpie web`.

## What it reads

Only `usage:summary`, the one permission its `package.json` declares (`magpie.permissions`). That is magpie's totals for a period, and the top models in it. magpie refuses any other read the page asks for.

Like every plugin page, it runs in a sandboxed frame. It has no network (`connect-src 'none'`), no inline scripts, and no access to magpie's API except through `_magpie/bridge.js`.

## Options

```json
{ "period": "today", "sort": "tokens" }
```

The page saves the period (`today`, `7d`, `30d`) and the model sort (`tokens`, `calls`, `cost`) you last picked, so it opens the same next time.

## Files

- `page/index.html`, `page/style.css`: the page. It takes magpie's theme from the `--magpie-*` variables, light or dark.
- `page/view.js`: what the numbers and rows say, in English and Chinese, with no DOM. The test loads it.
- `page/app.js`: reads through the bridge, draws, and refreshes every minute.

## Test

```sh
bun test packages/usage
```

@magpie-community/tools-calc.readme:
# @magpie-community/tools-calc

Exact arithmetic, unit conversion and date math, as tools [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) offers every agent it connects. Models get arithmetic wrong (`0.1 + 0.2`, big powers, days between two dates across a DST change), so this gives them a calculator. It needs no network, no key and no dependency.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with:

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/tools-calc
magpie plugin            # lists its tools
```

magpie serves the tools on its MCP server, `/mcp/magpie/tools`, to every agent it has connected. Each tool's name starts with the plugin's short name, `calc`: `calc_eval`, `calc_convert` and `calc_date` (magpie v0.1.1260 or later; earlier versions named them `tools-calc_eval` when installed from npm).

## Tools

**`eval`** `{expression, places?}` evaluates an expression exactly, in fractions, with no floating point.

- Operators: `+ - * / % ^` (or `**`), parentheses, and unary minus.
- Numbers: decimals, `1e9`, `0x`/`0b`/`0o` literals, and `1_000`.
- Functions: `abs floor ceil round trunc min max gcd lcm fact`.
- It answers `{exact, decimal}`, plus `rounded: true` when the decimal was cut at `places` (20 by default).

```
0.1+0.2          → {"exact":"3/10","decimal":"0.3"}
2^128/3          → every digit, exact
1/0              → an error: division by zero
```

**`convert`** `{value, from, to, places?}` converts a quantity exactly. `value` can be an expression, such as `3*1024`.

| Kind | Units |
|---|---|
| Data | `bit B kB MB GB TB` (1000s), `KiB MiB GiB TiB` (1024s), `kb Mb Gb` |
| Time | `ns us ms s min h d wk` |
| Length | `nm um mm cm m km in ft yd mi nmi` |
| CSS | `px pt pc` |
| Mass | `mg g kg t oz lb` |
| Angle | `deg turn grad` |
| Temperature | `C F K` |

```
1 GiB → MB       → {"exact":"16777216/15625","decimal":"1073.741824","unit":"MB"}
```

**`date`** `{date?, add?, to?, timeZone?}` does date math on the real calendar.

- `date` is ISO 8601, unix seconds or milliseconds, or `now` (the default). It answers the ISO time, weekday, ISO week, day of year and unix time.
- `add` is a duration, such as `3d 4h`, `-90m`, `1y2mo` or ISO `P1DT2H`. Years, months and days count on the calendar, so Jan 31 + 1mo is the last day of February, and a day across a DST change is still a day.
- `to` is a second date. The answer then also has `between`, the time from `date` (after `add`) to `to`, in days, hours, minutes, seconds and calendar years, months and days.
- `timeZone` is an IANA zone, such as `Asia/Shanghai`. Dates with no offset are read as that zone's wall time, and the answer shows the local time. Without it, they are UTC.

## Test

```sh
bun test packages/calc
```

中文：给 magpie 连接的每个 agent 提供精确计算工具：`eval` 用分数精确计算表达式，`convert` 换算数据、时间、长度、质量、角度和温度单位，`date` 按真实日历做日期加减和间隔（支持时区与夏令时）。不联网，不需要 key。

# GoAnyAPI for Magpie

Official website: [goanyapi.com](https://goanyapi.com/)

GoAnyAPI's complete, publicly advertised **read-only MCP API catalog** as Magpie tools. No API selection list is maintained in this plugin. It supports OAuth login through GoAnyAPI's remote MCP server and API-key login through its REST API.

## Install

Use **Plugins → Discover → Tools for agents** or:

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/tools-goanyapi
```

Sign in with **GoAnyAPI → Sign in** (OAuth, recommended):

```sh
magpie plugin login goanyapi oauth
```

Alternatively choose **GoAnyAPI API key** or use `magpie plugin login goanyapi api`. Existing API keys can also be supplied with `GOANYAPI_API_KEY` in the Magpie gateway process or through the `apiKey` plugin option. OAuth credentials are kept in Magpie's sign-in storage, and requests use the remote `https://mcp.goanyapi.com/mcp` server; no privileged backend secret is distributed.

## Connecting to agents

Magpie exposes plugin tools at its local Streamable HTTP endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:3425/mcp/magpie/tools`. Add this endpoint to your agent's MCP configuration using the URL shown in Magpie's Plugins page. Installing the plugin alone does not modify an agent's configuration.

All current read-only API definitions come from the public `https://api.goanyapi.com/api/v1/mcp/catalog` JSON Schema directory, with GoAnyAPI's built-in catalog as a failover. New published APIs do **not** require a new PR or changes to this package. **Magpie captures the named tool set when its plugin host loads**; restart/reload the plugin to show newly added tools as individual names. The permanent `catalog` and `call_dynamic` tools read the live catalog at invocation time, allowing access to a newly published API without updating the plugin itself.

## Authentication and credits

- **OAuth**: browser consent and OAuth 2.1/PKCE through GoAnyAPI's authorization server. API calls are sent to the remote MCP server, which validates the user's token.
- **API key**: REST requests to GoAnyAPI API endpoints using the user's API key, no backend-only secrets.
- API calls may consume GoAnyAPI account credits. Tool discovery reads the public catalog and is free.
- Never put API keys, access tokens, refresh tokens, or server-only secrets into public source or issues.

## Development

```sh
node --check packages/goanyapi/index.mjs
bun scripts/check.mjs
bun test
```

Tests are in `packages/goanyapi/tests`. Authentication tests use stubs, not live user credentials.

Source of truth: [GoAnyAPI MCP](https://github.com/GoAnyAPI/goanyapi-mcp). Magpie community repository: [magpie-community/plugins](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins).

@magpie-community/tools-layerfs.readme:
# LayerFS for Magpie

[LayerFS](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs) workspaces for every
agent [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) connects: instead of each agent copying
a project tree to work on it, agents share one durable, deduplicated history
and work through **stable filesystem paths**. Forking a branch for a
parallel agent copies **no file bytes**; a checkpoint stores **only what
changed**; any agent can resolve, read and build on what the others
committed.

给每个 agent 的 LayerFS 工作区：多个 agent 共享一份可去重的持久历史，而不是
各自复制整棵项目树。给并行 agent 开分支不复制任何文件字节；存检查点只写
变化的部分；路径稳定，任何 agent 都能定位、读取并接续其他 agent 的提交。

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/tools-layerfs
magpie plugin            # lists layerfs_provision, layerfs_checkpoint, ...
```

## Tools

Served on magpie's MCP server as `layerfs_<tool>`:

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `provision` | Gives the agent a workspace for a project branch and answers the path to work in. The first provision imports the source directory — a required argument, the directory the user chose for the project — as the project's first checkpoint; later provisions of the same branch answer the same path without copying the tree again. |
| `checkpoint` | Saves the workspace's state on its branch, storing only the blobs the store has not seen; answers added / modified / deleted counts and the new-bytes vs saved-bytes accounting. |
| `fork` | Forks a branch for a parallel agent: a pointer at an existing checkpoint, ready immediately, 0 bytes copied. |
| `publish` | Publishes a branch's head as main's new Layer, so finished work becomes what new work forks from. Guarded: main's head must be in the branch's history, so a publish can only move main forward — if main moved on its own, the publish is refused (a real dsh run lost main's 238 tests to a stale publish; this is that lesson, encoded). `force: true` overwrites deliberately and reports what it replaced. |
| `exec` | Runs a shell command in a branch's workspace and checkpoints whatever it changed as one commit — the dsh shape, where every bash call is mount, run, commit. A no-change command commits nothing; a failing command's changes are still checkpointed, with its exit code reported. **Disabled by default** (see Safety defaults): it runs only when the user has opted in. |
| `history` | Lists a branch's checkpoints, newest first, with each one's logical tree size and the bytes it actually stored. |
| `resolve` | Resolves a project / branch / file to a real filesystem path, its checkpoint and content hash — an O(1) lookup, no copying. |
| `status` | Backend in use, projects and branches held, and the storage accounting: logical bytes of all checkpoints vs bytes the store occupies. |

Only the workspace path is persistent. Every workspace carries two
scratch directories, `.tmp/` and `.cache/`, created at provision;
`exec` runs commands with `TMPDIR` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` redirected at
them, so toolchains keep their temporary files and caches inside the
workspace instead of the host's real `/tmp`. Both directories are
workspace-local scratch: checkpoints and publishes never capture them,
and they live and die with the workspace directory itself. Files a
command writes to the host's real `/tmp` are likewise outside LayerFS
management — if it matters, it belongs in the workspace.

## Backend

- **sim** — a local content-addressed store implementing the LayerFS
  model: immutable blobs named by SHA-256, branches as manifest
  pointers, checkpoints as deduplicated manifests, under
  `MAGPIE_LAYERFS_HOME` (default `~/.layerfs-tools`; a
  `~/.magpie-layerfs` from 0.7.2 or earlier is moved there once, with a
  link left at the old path). It runs anywhere, which is what the tests
  and the benchmark below use.

**This package is sim-only.** The native backend — the real LayerFS
through its JavaScript SDK — is developed in the standalone repo,
[Mola-maker/magpie-layerfs](https://github.com/Mola-maker/magpie-layerfs),
and is not part of this package: shipping it here needs a pinned,
integrity-checked npm dependency, and `@layerfs/sdk` is not
published to npm, so there is no version to pin. It returns in a
follow-up PR once the SDK is published. Asking for it
(`MAGPIE_LAYERFS_BACKEND=native`, `MAGPIE_LAYERFS_NATIVE=1`, or the
old `"native"` plugin option) is an explicit error that says so.

`MAGPIE_LAYERFS_BACKEND=auto|sim` selects explicitly; both mean sim
here.

## Safety defaults

magpie serves plugin tools on its MCP server to any caller holding a
gateway key, and the plugin host runs with the user's rights — so the
defaults here are set for that room, not for a private library:

- **`provision`'s `source` is required.** There is no default: an
  earlier version defaulted it to the host's `directory`, which in
  magpie is the *config* directory (`~/.config/magpie`) — it holds
  `plugin-auth.json`, every signed-in plugin's token. The config
  directory, the credential stores (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`),
  the home directory, the filesystem root, and the plugin's own store
  are refused as a source — as the source, inside it, or containing
  it. The comparison runs on real paths (`realpathSync`, case-folded),
  so neither a symlink pointing at a refused directory nor a
  case-variant spelling of one (`~/.Config/Magpie`, `~/.AWS`) gets
  past it.
- **Secret-shaped files never enter the store from an import**:
  `.git`, `.env*`, private keys (`id_rsa`, `id_ed25519`, `*.pem`,
  `*.key`, …), `.ssh`, `.aws`. The sim backend skips them and reports
  how many. Imports are
  also bounded (20,000 files / 512 MiB) and fail loudly past the limit
  instead of sweeping a disk.
- **The store is private.** Its root and directories are created
  `0700`, its record files `0600`, whatever the umask says; a file's
  own mode is preserved through the sim store (a `0600` file is stored
  and materialized as `0600`).
- **`exec` is disabled by default.** It runs a shell with the plugin
  host's privileges; a model key should not silently become host
  shell access. The user enables it with the plugin's `"exec"`
  option (set to `true` in magpie's plugin options) or
  `MAGPIE_LAYERFS_EXEC=1` in the host's environment.
- **Re-provisioning a moved branch keeps the workspace.** When a
  branch has moved since its checkout, re-provisioning keeps the
  workspace's files and reports `stale: true` instead of wiping the
  directory.

## Benchmark

[`bench/bench.mjs`](https://github.com/Mola-maker/magpie-layerfs/blob/main/bench/bench.mjs)
(run from a checkout of this repo) — a 184-file, 26.8 MB project; 6
parallel agents, each keeping 3 checkpoints (sim backend, this machine):

| | naive copies | this plugin |
|---|---|---|
| fork one more agent | 321 ms, 26.8 MB copied | **~1 ms, 0 bytes** |
| keep 18 checkpoints | 482.6 MB of snapshots | **27.2 MB** of store for 509.4 MB of logical checkpoints (**18.7× dedup**) |
| resolve a file path | walk the copy's tree | **138 µs**, with its checkpoint + SHA-256 |
| total disk for the run | 643.5 MB | **188.1 MB** (store + the 6 live workspaces) |

![test run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mola-maker/magpie-layerfs/29b52fb98fc2e9c20fb9e5c3c85a05f80cd01754/docs/assets/tests.png)
![benchmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mola-maker/magpie-layerfs/29b52fb98fc2e9c20fb9e5c3c85a05f80cd01754/docs/assets/benchmark.png)

Honest limits: a first provision still materializes the tree once, and the
sim backend rehashes the tree at each checkpoint (the native engine tracks
changes through its daemons instead). What the plugin removes is the
per-agent copy, the per-snapshot copy, and the bytes they waste — the
engine's own benchmarks are at
[layerfs.ai/benchmarks](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/).

Against the real engine
([`bench/bench-native.mjs`](https://github.com/Mola-maker/magpie-layerfs/blob/main/bench/bench-native.mjs),
native backend, same scenario, generated-text fixture of 184 files /
27.0 MB): import
3.6 s once; a fork plus its checkout 1.8 s (the branch itself is
metadata; the checkout pays the file reads); a checkpoint 1.9 s (the
checkout diff reads the branch back through the fs surface, then one
`fs.apply` lands it); the engine's store file held **5.6 MB for
513 MB of logical checkpoints** on this compressible text fixture —
the sim fixture above is random bytes, the incompressible extreme, so
read the two ratios as the ends of a range, not a single number.

## The page: watch the trajectory

The package also declares a magpie page, **LayerFS trajectory**
(轨迹), which replays how the agents' worktrees grew, drawn the way
LayerFS's own History picture draws them: main is the green middle
bough, each branch a bough of its own, a checkpoint a badge bearing
its agent's own icon — the marks magpie itself ships for them, in
that agent's colour — a fork a split, and a publish a graft back
onto main that adds a Layer band (L0, L1, …). Two running totals
carry the argument — what those checkpoints would have cost as
plain copies against what the deduplicated store actually wrote,
with a store.stats line in LayerFS's own accounting words. Play it,
scrub it, click a badge for its checkpoint's message and byte
split, or click a branch's name tag to focus that branch alone:
that is what the plugin does for an agent's edits, made visible.

The page is drawn in magpie's own design language and built the way
magpie builds pages — plain HTML, CSS and scripts, no build step and
no dependencies, styled by the host's `--magpie-*` theme tokens with
its tiles, seg controls and indigo accent. The replay runs on
requestAnimationFrame through magpie's own `--ease` curve
(cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)): the boughs draw themselves as the
playhead passes, each badge lands with a pulse while its icon
draws its own outline and fills in, a publish pops its Layer badge
(L1, L2, …) onto main, and the stat tiles count up with the same
easing; with reduced motion preferred, the page simply shows the
finished picture, every icon fully drawn.

A magpie page cannot fetch, and the bridge's reads are a fixed host
list (`usage:summary`, `providers:list`) with no entry a plugin can
serve its own data through — but magpie lets a page navigate its
frame elsewhere, and pulls a plugin's host part up the moment its
page is requested, waiting up to 7 seconds for it (pageHost /
plugin.Warm). So the page's live channel is the host's own
localhost-only service (`page-service.mjs`), the way page-chat
serves its chat page:

- **The installed page only jumps.** `page/index.html` does one
  thing: it reads the port from the plugin's options
  (`pagePort`, default 43717) and `location.replace`s its frame to
  `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`. The install's folder is never
  renamed, linked, or written into. A user with no store gets no
  service and nothing written anywhere.
- **The service returns the page with its data inside.** Each
  request rebuilds `backend.trajectory()` on demand and answers one
  route, GET /, as HTML: the trajectory UI with the recording
  embedded as `<script type="application/json" id="data">`, which
  the page reads from the DOM — never by fetch. The page reloads
  itself every few seconds, keeping its view across each reload (the
  project, the scroll, and the replay position ride in
  `location.hash`), so the picture stays live. With no store there
  is no service at all, so the frame shows the browser's
  refused-to-connect page until the first project is provisioned;
  a store with no recorded checkpoints yet shows the page's honest
  empty state.
- **The service is closed to other sites.** It emits no CORS
  headers and refuses any request carrying an Origin (a sandboxed
  iframe's fetch sends `Origin: null`); it serves no `.js` data
  file another site could `<script src>` — only `text/html` with
  `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; and it checks Host, answering
  only `127.0.0.1:<port>` and `localhost:<port>`, so a
  DNS-rebinding name is refused. Another site can at most frame
  the page; it cannot read it.
- **An Agent activity table** under the replay lists every recorded
  tool call — the calling agent, the tool, the project, the branch and
  the time, newest last. With no recorded calls the table gives way
  to an empty note; all four locales carry the strings.

`backend.trajectory()` itself is computed on demand from the store's
records whenever it is asked for (`tools/gen-trajectory.mjs` uses it
to make the sample). No recording file is maintained in the store: an
earlier version refreshed one in the store after every call, which
cost a branch-chain walk per call — growing with the project's
history — for a file the page cannot read, so the refresh was removed
in 0.7.1. The page declares no `magpie.read` permissions, and its
test asserts it asks for none.

## Develop

From a checkout of [this repo](https://github.com/Mola-maker/magpie-layerfs)
(the registry package ships only the runtime files):

```sh
bun test                 # the suite (bun:test): tools end to end, plus the page's layout math
bun bench/bench.mjs      # the benchmark above; writes bench/results.json
node tools/gen-trajectory.mjs   # regenerate the page's bundled sample trajectory
```

Zero runtime dependencies; the arguments are JSON Schema, like the other
tools packages. MIT.

## Changes in 0.10.0

The page's live channel comes back, out of the plugin's own folder. The
0.9.0 review was right that nothing may write into the installed
package's folder — an update replaces that folder, two hosts with one
install race on the same file, and an install can be read-only — but its
conclusion, a page that only ever shows the bundled sample, threw away
the real trajectory every desktop had been watching. This version
answers both sides at once, the way page-chat serves its page:

- **The host serves the page itself.** The installed `page/` is
  never renamed, linked, or written into: `page/index.html` only
  navigates its frame to a localhost-only service the host starts
  (`page-service.mjs`, port `pagePort`, default 43717), which
  returns the trajectory UI with the live recording embedded in
  the HTML. The page reloads itself every few seconds, so the
  picture stays live without any file channel.
- **The page gains an Agent activity table** — every recorded tool
  call, with the calling agent, the tool, the project, the branch and
  the time — so each round's work is visible per agent, not only as
  commits on a graph.
- **The service starts only once a store exists** (two read-only
  gates: a projects folder that holds entries, and a non-empty
  answer from the backend that will serve the calls), so an upgrade
  shows the user's real work on the first open, and a user with no
  store gets no service and nothing written anywhere.
- `startPageService` lives in `page-service.mjs`, not the entry
  module: the plugin host takes every function the entry exports for
  an OpenCode plugin factory and calls it at load, so the entry
  exports `LayerfsTools` alone (the standalone repo shipped 0.10.0
  with the helper in the entry and the whole plugin failed to load
  — this is that lesson, applied here from the start).

## Changes in 0.9.0

The registry package is sim-only now. The native backend — the
standalone repo's LayerFS 1.1.0 port, with the SDK split into
`@layerfs/agent`, `@layerfs/backend` and `@layerfs/runtime`, the
`LayerFS.open` / `LayerFS.init` factories and the child-process
worker — stays in the standalone repo until the SDK is published
to npm and this package can pin it; the registry review asked for
the native path to stay out until then, so `native-worker.mjs`
and the fake SDK are gone from this package, the `"native"` plugin
option is gone, and a native request is refused instead of
silently running sim.

The page's live file is gone with it: the registry review asked
for no writes into the installed plugin's folder, so the tools no
longer write `page/trajectory-live.js` at runtime and the page is
back to the bundled sample (the 0.7.1 position — a magpie page
cannot read plugin-private data, and the bridge's reads are a
fixed host list). The live trajectory stays available through the
tools and through `backend.trajectory()`, which now caches every
commit's summary (everything but the manifest, which it never
uses) per project/id: a rebuild reads only commits it has never
seen, and a rebuild with nothing new reads no records at all (a
test counts the reads to pin that). Between branches the walk
yields, so even a first build over a large store never holds the
shared plugin host's event loop for its whole duration.

## Changes in 0.8.0

0.8.0 gave the page the real trajectory. The 0.7.x page could only
animate the bundled sample — a magpie page cannot fetch, and the
bridge's reads are a fixed host list — so the live picture the tools
held never reached it. The channel was there all along, though:
magpie serves a page's files from the plugin's folder as they sit on
disk, per request. So:

- **The page's live file.** After any provision, fork, checkpoint,
  publish or exec lands, the tools rebuild the trajectory on demand
  (`backend.trajectory()`) and write it, tmp-then-renamed, to
  `page/trajectory-live.js` in the plugin's own folder — debounced,
  off the tool calls' path, errors swallowed (the page keeps its
  last file; the calls are untouched). The page loads it after the
  bundled sample and prefers it. An empty store writes an empty
  live file, and the page shows its honest empty state instead of
  the demo; the sample remains what a store the tools have never
  written shows.
  Registry review (PR #365) asked for no writes into the installed
  plugin's folder, so 0.9.0 removes the live file again and the
  page is back to the bundled sample.
- **The real agent on every commit.** The tools record the calling
  agent — the tool host's `ctx.agent`, the gateway's name for the
  agent that made the call — on the events and commits each call
  creates. The page prefers it over the branch-name token guess: a
  claude badge lands where claude actually checkpointed, even on
  `main`, and the detail card names the agent.

## Changes in 0.7.1

The second round of the PR #318 review — the holes it found in
0.7.0's own new code, plus its smaller items:

- **The source guard compares real paths now.** 0.7.0 compared
  `resolve()`d strings, which a symlink to a refused directory — or
  a case-variant spelling of one on a case-insensitive volume —
  walked straight past (the review imported `plugin-auth.json`
  through `~/.Config/Magpie` and through a symlink). Both sides are
  canonicalized with `realpathSync` and case-folded; refused roots
  that do not exist are canonicalized through their nearest existing
  ancestor. Regression tests cover the symlink and the case variant,
  unit-level and end to end.
- **Breaking on-disk change: workspaces moved, branch encoding
  widened.** Workspaces now live at `workspaces/<project>/<encoded
  branch>` — the flat `<project>--<branch>` name was not injective
  (project `a` branch `b--c` and project `a--b` branch `c` shared one
  directory, and a checkpoint crossed the projects). The branch
  encoder now percent-encodes every character outside `[a-z0-9._-]`,
  uppercase included, so `Main` and `main` no longer share a head
  file or a workspace on case-insensitive volumes either. Stores are
  **not migrated**: branch head files are unchanged for names the old
  encoder already spelled the same way (lowercase, `_`, `-`, `.`,
  and `/`→`%2F`); a branch whose name contains uppercase or `%`
  keeps its commits but its old head file (`branches/Main.json`)
  and old workspace (`workspaces/<project>--Main`) are not picked
  up — re-fork such branches, and remove the old workspace
  directories by hand.
- **No per-call trajectory refresh.** The `trajectory.json` the
  tools maintained in the store after every call is gone: keeping it
  current cost a walk of the touched branch's whole chain per call,
  for a file the page cannot read. `trajectory()` still builds the
  same data on demand.
- **`exec`'s plumbing**: stdin is closed (a command reading it gets
  EOF instead of waiting out the timeout), the child runs detached
  in its own process group and a timeout kills the group, and the
  call resolves on `exit` plus a short drain instead of `close` —
  a background child holding the stdout pipe can no longer hold the
  call open past its shell.
- **Manifests are counted.** `storedBytes`/`dedupRatio` now include
  the commit records — each checkpoint's full manifest — which for
  a wide tree are a real share of the store (the review measured
  128 MB of manifests for 200 checkpoints of a 5,000-file tree,
  previously uncounted, under a description claiming history "costs
  little more than the changes themselves"; the description now
  states the real cost model). Stores written before 0.7.1 keep
  their incremental record, which undercounts by the records written
  before this version until the record is rebuilt (delete
  `accounting.json` to force the rebuild walk).
- The page's README images are pinned to a commit instead of the
  moving `main`.

## Changes in 0.7.0

A safety pass over the whole package (prompted by the PR #318 review):

- `provision` requires `source` explicitly and refuses magpie's config
  directory and the credential stores as sources; imports skip
  secret-shaped files (sim) or refuse them (native), and are bounded.
- `exec` is off by default; the user's `"exec"` plugin option or
  `MAGPIE_LAYERFS_EXEC=1` turns it on.
- The native backend is off by default (the `"native"` option or
  `MAGPIE_LAYERFS_NATIVE=1`) and runs entirely in a child process
  (`native-worker.mjs`); the host process imports no SDK and shares no
  `LAYERFS_*` environment writes.
- A native checkpoint no longer deletes binaries it skipped at
  checkout; re-provisioning a moved native branch reports `stale`
  instead of wiping the workspace; native publish refuses when the
  fork point or main's top Layer is unknown.
- The store and workspaces are `0700`, record files `0600`, and file
  modes are preserved through the sim store.
- The recorded trajectory lives in the store (`trajectory.json`),
  refreshed per affected project; the page's bundled file is a static
  sample, and running the test suite modifies no package file.
- **Breaking on-disk change**: branch head files and workspace
  directories now percent-encode `/` (`feat/x` → `feat%2Fx`), so slash
  branches and `feat__x` no longer collide and slash branches list
  correctly. Stores written by 0.6.x keep working for non-slash
  branches; a slash branch's old head file (`branches/feat/x.json`)
  and workspace (`feat__x`) are not migrated — re-fork slash branches.
- The page gained Japanese and Traditional Chinese string tables
  (matching its declared titles), a magpie-style project menu in
  place of the native `<select>`, and a branch-colour dot on the
  detail card in place of the coloured edge.

@magpie-community/tools-search1api.readme:
# Search1API for Magpie

Search1API web search, news, agentic search, page retrieval, sitemap discovery,
and trending tools in [Magpie](https://usemagpie.ai/), with browser OAuth and
API key sign-in. The source lives in this community repository and is published as
`@magpie-community/tools-search1api`. It uses native fetch with no runtime
dependencies; request bodies and defaults match the original integration.

## Install

In Magpie, open **Plugins → Add plugin** and enter:

```text
@magpie-community/tools-search1api
```

Or use the terminal:

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/tools-search1api
```

The package includes its TypeScript source and an `index.mjs` entry. Magpie's
Bun host loads it directly; installation and community packaging need no build.

## Sign in

### OAuth (recommended)

Choose **Search1API → Sign in to Search1API** in the plugin's sign-in controls,
or run:

```sh
magpie plugin login search1api oauth
```

Magpie opens your browser. Sign in with your Search1API account and approve
access, then return to Magpie. The plugin uses a dynamically registered public
OAuth client, authorization code flow with PKCE S256, and a temporary loopback
callback. No client secret or Search1API CLI is required.

The client is registered once and saved, with its callback port, in
`search1api-oauth-client.json` next to `plugin-auth.json`; later sign-ins
reuse it. If that port is busy, or a sign-in with the saved client does not
finish, the plugin registers a new client. The authorization URL carries
`utm_source=magpie` and API requests send `User-Agent: search1api-magpie/<version>`,
so Search1API can tell sign-ups and usage that come from Magpie.

The browser must run on the same computer as Magpie. For a remote or container
installation, use an API key instead. The callback expires after five minutes.

Magpie saves access and refresh tokens in `plugin-auth.json` under its config
directory (`~/.config/magpie`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/magpie`) with file mode
`0600`. The plugin reads only its own `search1api` entry and saves refreshed
tokens through Magpie's `client.auth.set`; it does not maintain a second token
store. Tool calls refresh expiring tokens and retry once after an OAuth `401`.
Refreshes are serialized across simultaneous calls and Magpie processes.

Search1API appears as a sign-in entry with **no chat models**. It authenticates
the tools, not a model provider. One Search1API account is active at a time;
signing in again replaces it.

To remove the saved sign-in:

```sh
magpie plugin logout search1api
```

This removes the local credentials. It does not revoke an authorization at the
authorization server or remove API keys configured separately below.

### API key

Choose **Search1API API key** in the same sign-in controls, or run:

```sh
magpie plugin login search1api api
```

Magpie prompts privately for the key and saves it in its credential store.
Get a key at [s1.dev](https://s1.dev/?utm_source=magpie&utm_medium=readme).

For automated deployments, the plugin also accepts an `apiKey` plugin option
in Magpie's options editor, or `SEARCH1API_API_KEY` in the environment of the
Magpie process. Precedence: plugin option → environment → Magpie sign-in.
An option or environment key overrides a saved OAuth account. `SEARCH1API_KEY`
and the CLI's `s1 login` session are not read.

`baseUrl` is an optional API base URL for a compatible deployment or local
testing. It defaults to `https://api.search1api.com`. HTTPS is required, except
for loopback test servers. OAuth discovery uses that API's protected-resource
metadata and validates the issuer and endpoints.

## Connect your agent

In **Settings → Plugins**, copy the plugin tools MCP address, then add it to
your agent's MCP configuration. The default address is:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:3425/mcp/magpie/tools
```

For Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http magpie-tools \
  http://127.0.0.1:3425/mcp/magpie/tools
```

Other agents use the same Streamable HTTP endpoint. Use the address Magpie
shows if the port or host differs. Remote calls require a Magpie gateway key;
this is separate from your Search1API credential.

Installing the plugin does not write your agent's MCP configuration or replace
its built-in search tool. Magpie exposes tools from all enabled tool plugins
on this endpoint.

## Tools

Magpie prefixes each tool with the plugin name. Use the names reported by
your Magpie tools endpoint.

- `search`: web search, engine selection, site filters, date range and native
  pagination. Page selection works on engines that support it.
- `news`: news search with optional article content.
- `ask`: describe what to find; Search1API chooses engines and a time window
  and returns ranked results. Each completed call costs **5 credits**. It
  returns search results rather than a generated answer.
- `crawl`: retrieve readable page content.
- `sitemap`: discover site links.
- `trending`: GitHub or Hacker News trends.
- `send_feedback`: report a wrong or empty result, an unresolved error,
  mismatched docs or a missing capability to the Search1API team, through
  Search1API's `POST /feedback` API. It is free and needs a Search1API sign-in or API key. The report (message,
  intent, category, request id and model) goes only to Search1API, which stores
  it in its feedback inbox on [Agentback](https://agentback.app), a
  third-party host, linked to your Search1API account.

Search tool parameters follow the existing OpenCode integration. Search and news
preserve optional `published_date` and per-result `metadata`; Ask preserves
`intent`, `source`, `relevance`, and `errors`. Attribute Grokipedia results as
“Powered by xAI”. Results are returned as JSON text.

Magpie gives tools a 55-second deadline. Cancellation is forwarded to fetch.
Automatic request retries are disabled to keep calls within that deadline; OAuth
authentication is retried once after refreshing. Other upstream errors return
to the calling agent.

## Development

From this folder, on Node 24 or later (or Bun for the tests):

```sh
npm install --workspaces=false --ignore-scripts --package-lock=false
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm run build
npm test
npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts
```

The TypeScript build is a local verification artifact in `dist/`; the published
package contains the reviewed source. `lint` checks the entry syntax and runs
the strict TypeScript checks (including unused code and switch fallthrough).

From the repository root, run the same checks as community CI with a temporary
home, as documented in `.github/workflows/pr.yml`:

```sh
bun test
bun scripts/check.mjs
```

The fetch-stub tests replace every fetch with synthetic responses, covering
all six wire bodies, defaults, validation, safe errors, OAuth discovery,
refresh/retry limits and cancellation. Local loopback fixtures additionally
exercise PKCE browser callbacks, key precedence, concurrent refreshes and
logout without real accounts or paid API calls.

An optional integration test uses Magpie's actual Bun plugin host and the same
local fixture. It is outside the default test filename pattern:

```sh
MAGPIE_HOST_PATH=/path/to/magpie/internal/plugin/host.js \
MAGPIE_BUN_PATH=/path/to/bun npm run test:magpie
```

The migrated integration was verified against Magpie host revision
`8ef9fc578ced531b7ca835a3133c37f608a70e6a`. Live-account OAuth consent still
requires manual verification on the machine running Magpie.

## Maintenance and license

Migrated from [Search1API for Magpie v0.1.0](https://github.com/superagents-lab/magpie-search1api/tree/v0.1.0),
commit `89b9cd5fd1c1c105d603768c14404873d697941f`, under MIT. The original
Search1API copyright and license are retained in `LICENSE`.

This replaces the external-package listing proposed in
[#340](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/pull/340). Source changes
are reviewed here and published by `@magpie-community` through this
repository's existing publishing workflow; see the root README. This package
does not publish from the original repository's release workflow.
